what_this_is: six tracks: four candidate routes for the paper, one contracting route, and the existing flying-fish framework
lawset: 1.6.0 (lean/registry/lawsets/current.json -> lawset-1.6.0.json, created 2026-11-01, pins 53 laws). Repo HEAD read: cb92aaf (2026-11-12). Caveat: lean/registry/laws/ holds 64 law files; 11 added after the release (turing-ddi-linear-condition, 7 cell-geometry, 3 crystal laws) are NOT pinned by lawset-1.6.0.json although README.md says 'Law set 1.6.0: 64 laws'. Counts are my own: node script over lawset-1.6.0.json (.laws.length = 53) and the laws/ directory listing (64).

scout.summary: Track 1 (shift a reporter's dose-response) has an unusually clean target: the Cello genetic-circuit design-automation libraries ship machine-readable Hill transfer functions (ymax, ymin, K, n) AND raw 250-bin flow-cytometry histograms for every characterised repressor gate, under Apache-2.0 on GitHub. I fetched five of these UCF libraries (E. coli x3, S. cerevisiae, B. thetaiotaomicron) and the mismatch-CRISPRi reporter dataset. Within the Cello E. coli library, repressor families that differ ONLY in RBS strength shift the input threshold K by 4.2x-10x while the Hill coefficient n stays within 3.8-8.9% CV - i.e. an RBS change is close to a pure translation of the transfer function along the log-input axis. That is a one-line, falsifiable, Lean-formalisable law with four independent held-out libraries to test it on, no wet lab needed. The honest counter-signal is already visible: in yeast the same families show n CV up to 28%, and the single-cell output noise is NOT invariant (log10-SD 0.244-0.435 within one SrpR family), so the law is a prokaryotic-transcription claim, not a universal one.
scout.recommended: Candidate 1: the RBS-tuned repressor gate law in the Cello E. coli libraries - FREEZE 'same repressor, RBS-only change shifts K by >2x while holding n to within 15%', then score it on the four held-out libraries I already fetched. It is the only candidate where the quantitative phenotype, the number-making model, the public data and the holdout sets are all in hand right now, as machine-readable JSON under a permissive licence, so a frozen prediction can be scored this week with zero bench time. It is also the one that actually produces a Lean-for-Biology artefact rather than a correlation: a separability statement about threshold and steepness as independent design axes, with an explicit hypothesis set and a documented yeast counterexample attached.

candidates.name: RBS-tuned repressor gates: threshold shifts, steepness invariant (Cello E. coli Eco1C1G1T1)
candidates.system: E. coli NEB 10-beta, 20 TetR-homolog repressor NOT/NOR gates (AmtR, AmeR, BetI, BM3R1, HlyIIR, IcaRA, LitR, LmrA, PhlF, PsrA, QacR, SrpR) driving YFP, measured in RPU by flow cytometry. Four families (SrpR x4, PhlF x3, BM3R1 x3, QacR x2) are the SAME repressor with different RBSs - the design change.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Steady-state YFP transfer function, input promoter activity (RPU) -> output promoter activity (RPU), fitted to a 4-parameter Hill: y = ymin + (ymax-ymin)/(1+(x/K)^n). Plus full single-cell YFP distributions (250 log-spaced bins) at 12 input levels per gate.
candidates.why_it_fits: The design change (RBS strength in front of the repressor) is discrete, cheap and already enumerated; the phenotype is a number; the model (Hill) makes a number; and the prediction 'K moves, n does not' is a clean invariance statement of exactly the kind Lean-for-Biology wants to state as a theorem with side conditions. Crucially there are four INDEPENDENT libraries (a second E. coli landing-pad set, an MG1655 phage-repressor set, a yeast set, a Bacteroides set) that can be held out, so a frozen prediction can be scored without touching a bench.

public_data.what: Cello UCF for the Nielsen 2016 Science E. coli library: 20 gates, 20 Hill models, 20 cytometry functions (12 input levels x 250 bins each), 84 parts, measurement standard and growth protocol. 4,834,067 bytes, 700 JSON records.
Input sensor models (LacI/pTac, TetR/pTet, AraC/pBAD, LuxR/pLuxStar) with ymax/ymin - gives the actual inducer-driven input range the gates were driven over.
Second independent E. coli library (different genomic landing pads / circuit topology set), 18 gates with Hill params including SrpR x4, PhlF x3, BM3R1 x3, AmeR x2 - the primary holdout.

candidates.the_test: FREEZE this statement before looking at the holdouts: 'For any two gates in the Cello-family libraries that share a repressor protein and differ only in the ribosome binding site driving that repressor, the fitted Hill coefficients satisfy |n_i - n_j| / mean(n) <= 0.15, while K_i/K_j may exceed 2.' Then score it on Eco1C2G2T2, Eco2C1G5T1 and SC1C1G1T1, which were NOT used to set the 0.15 bound (the bound comes from Eco1C1G1T1 alone, where the worst family CV is 8.9%). Procedure, 1-2 weeks, pure compute: (1) parse all five fetched UCFs, group models by repressor protein, (2) for each multi-variant family compute max K-fold and the CV of n, (3) declare pass/fail per family against the frozen 15% bound, (4) as a second, harder leg, refit the Hill function yourself from the raw cytometry histograms rather than trusting the shipped fit - compute the distribution median per input level, fit 4-parameter Hill by least squares in log space, and check the invariance survives your own fit (this guards against the possibility that n-invariance is an artefact of the original fitting procedure's priors or bounds), (5) state the taxon boundary: report whether the bound holds in E. coli and fails in S. cerevisiae. Deliverable: a table of ~15 family comparisons with pass/fail, plus a Lean statement of the invariance with its hypotheses (prokaryotic transcription-factor repressor, same protein, RBS-only change) and the yeast counterexample as a documented non-theorem.
candidates.biggest_risk: The shipped n values may be partly an artefact of how Cello's own fitting pipeline was constrained, so apparent n-invariance could be fitting-procedure invariance rather than biology. Leg (4) of the test - refitting from the raw cytometry - is what makes this risk addressable rather than fatal, and it is the single most important thing to do first. Secondary risk: RBS variants in these libraries were selected by the original authors for good digital behaviour, so there is a selection bias toward well-behaved sigmoids; the law may be 'RBS variants that pass Cello's screen have invariant n', which is a weaker and less interesting claim.

candidates.name: Mismatch-CRISPRi: guide mismatches as a continuous dial on reporter output
candidates.system: E. coli and B. subtilis dCas9 CRISPRi against a chromosomal GFP reporter. The design change is deliberate single/double mismatches introduced into the sgRNA, which weaken the guide and thereby grade repression from full knockdown to none.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Relative GFP (relgfp): reporter fluorescence of a mismatched guide normalised against the perfect-match guide and the no-guide control. 2,973 measured variants across 31 parent guides, 96 variants per parent.
candidates.why_it_fits: This is the cleanest available 'one design change, continuously shifted reporter response' dataset: 96 graded knockdown levels per parent guide, two organisms, two biological replicates, a trained predictive model checked into the same repo, and an MIT licence. The model predicts relgfp from mismatch position and identity, so a frozen cross-species prediction (train on E. coli, predict B. subtilis) is immediately scoreable.

public_data.what: Joined-replicate reporter table: sgRNA variant, parent guide, relative GFP. 3,333 rows, 2,973 with a measured value.
Per-replicate E. coli GFP data (child/parent/relative), 3,168 rows.

Repo tree listing B. subtilis replicates (bsu_biorep1.csv, bsu_biorep2.csv, ~247 KB each), the trained model (model/model.d5, xscaler/yscaler dumps) and the training script train_linear_model.py - i.e. the holdout set and the frozen predictor both exist.

candidates.the_test: FREEZE: 'The mismatch->relgfp map learned on E. coli transfers to B. subtilis with Spearman rho >= 0.7 on held-out parent guides, and the rank order of mismatch POSITION effects is conserved across the two species.' Procedure, 2-3 weeks, pure compute: fit the repo's own linear model on eco_biorep1+2 only, predict bsu_biorep1+2, report Spearman and per-position effect correlation, and separately test whether a single-parameter position-weight model (one scalar per nucleotide position along the 20-mer, shared across parent guides) is sufficient - i.e. whether the dial is separable into position x identity. A positive separability result is a compact law: 'reporter shift = product of a position weight and a mismatch-type weight, independent of target gene.'
candidates.biggest_risk: relgfp runs from -0.583 to 1.214 (measured, computed below), so a meaningful fraction of values sit outside [0,1] - measurement noise and normalisation artefacts are large at the extremes. Any clean law will have to be stated on the interior of the range, and the obvious failure mode is that the apparent cross-species transfer is driven mostly by the easy extremes (perfect-match-like and dead-guide-like variants) while the interesting middle of the dial transfers poorly.

candidates.name: Cross-kingdom transfer of the same repressor-gate law (yeast SC1C1G1T1 as a documented counterexample)
candidates.system: S. cerevisiae BY4741, 12 gates built from phage/bacterial DNA-binding proteins (CI x2, CI434 x2, LexA x2 and others) fused to eukaryotic transactivation/repression domains, driving a fluorescent reporter.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Same Hill transfer function (ymax, ymin, K, n) in RPU-equivalent units, plus cytometry, in the same UCF schema as the E. coli libraries.
candidates.why_it_fits: This is the candidate whose job is to BREAK the law cleanly rather than confirm it. Having a fetched, same-schema, different-kingdom dataset is what turns candidate 1 from a curve-fitting exercise into a statement with hypotheses. The paper needs the boundary as much as the law.

public_data.what: Cello yeast UCF: 12 gates with Hill parameters, header confirms organism S. cerevisiae BY4741.

Cello Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron VPI-5482 UCF, 7 gates with Hill parameters. Fetched, but the gates are named Gate1..Gate7 with no repressor identity in the model names, so RBS-variant families cannot be grouped from the file alone - the mapping would have to come out of the Taketani 2020 supplementary.

candidates.the_test: Apply the frozen 15% n-invariance bound from candidate 1 to the three yeast families and report failures. Measured here: CI n = [2.06, 3.08] (CV 28.1%, FAILS), LexA n = [2.94, 3.82] (CV 18.4%, FAILS), CI434 n = [3.86, 3.92] (CV 1.1%, PASSES). Then ask the mechanistic question that gives the paper its point: the two failing families have K-fold of only 2.3x while CI434 - which passes - has K-fold 1.1x, so in yeast the variants that actually move the threshold are also the ones that change the steepness. Formalise the contrast as: in prokaryotic transcriptional repression, threshold and steepness are separable design axes; in the yeast chromatin/transactivation-domain context tested here, they are not.
candidates.biggest_risk: Only three yeast families with two variants each - n=3 comparisons is far too few to claim a kingdom-level difference, and with two points per family there is no way to separate a genuine n change from fit uncertainty. This candidate is honest supporting evidence for a boundary condition, not an independent result, and it should not be written up as one.

candidates.name: Phage-repressor extended gate set (Cello 2.0 Eco2C1G5T1) - different repressor chemistry, same law
candidates.system: E. coli MG1655, 12 gates built from phage immunity repressors (lambda CI, P2, 933W) rather than TetR homologs. Families: 933W x2, Lambda x2, P2 x3.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Hill transfer function (ymax, ymin, K, n) in the same UCF schema.
candidates.why_it_fits: If the invariance law is about the physics of cooperative repressor binding at an operator rather than about the TetR fold specifically, it should hold here too. These repressors have entirely different structures, operator architectures and oligomerisation states, so this is the strongest same-kingdom generalisation test available. The file is also small (46.5 KB), so it is trivially re-runnable in CI.

public_data.what: Cello 2.0 extended E. coli gate library, 12 gates with Hill parameters, header organism 'Escherichia coli MG1655 (Extended #Gates)'.

Third E. coli library (MG1655 K-12), 6 gates with Hill parameters, one per repressor (AmeRs, AmtR, BM3R1, BetI, PhlF, QacR) - no within-repressor families, so usable only for cross-library K comparison of the same repressor, not for the invariance test.

candidates.the_test: Score the frozen 15% bound on the three phage-repressor families. Measured here: 933W n = [2.548, 2.059] (CV 15.0%, marginal FAIL at the 15% line), Lambda n = [2.255, 2.091] (CV 5.3%, PASS), P2 n = [2.659, 2.183, 2.521] (CV 10.0%, PASS). Two of three pass; the marginal 933W case at exactly the bound is the kind of edge that must be reported rather than rounded. Then test a sharper version of the law on this set: because these gates have narrower n (all between 2.06 and 2.66) than the TetR homologs (2.4-4.2), check whether n clusters by repressor FOLD - if so the law becomes 'n is a property of the repressor protein, K is a property of its expression level', which is a much more useful statement for a design framework than an empirical tolerance.
candidates.biggest_risk: The variant naming in this library may not actually correspond to RBS-only changes - I grouped by the repressor token in the model name, which is an inference from file structure, not something the file states. If the 933W/Lambda/P2 variants differ in operator sequence or promoter architecture as well as RBS, the comparison is not an RBS experiment at all and the pass/fail numbers above mean something different. This must be checked against the Cello 2.0 protocol paper's part tables before any of it is written up.

candidates.name: Marionette: 12 optimised small-molecule sensors with engineered dose-responses
candidates.system: E. coli strains carrying 12 genomically integrated, directed-evolution-optimised small-molecule sensors (inducible promoters) driving fluorescent reporters; sensors were explicitly engineered to lower leak and widen dynamic range.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Inducer dose-response per sensor: fold-induction, leak, and inducer concentration range. This is the one candidate where the design change was made FOR the purpose of shifting the dose-response, so the intent matches track 1 exactly.
candidates.why_it_fits: Directly on-topic and the sensors are widely used, so a validated model of 'what the optimisation actually changed (K? n? ymin?)' would be useful to many groups. But I could not fetch the quantitative data in this run, which is why it ranks below the Cello candidates despite the better conceptual fit.

public_data.what: Paper record confirming title, authors, journal and year. The quantitative sensor dose-response tables live in Nature Chemical Biology supplementary material, which I did NOT fetch or verify as openly downloadable. The bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/285866 exists (found via Europe PMC) and may carry open supplementary files - unchecked.
public_data.licence: unknown for the data; metadata record only

candidates.the_test: First a 1-day feasibility gate: try the bioRxiv preprint 10.1101/285866 supplementary and the Voigt lab's distribution channels for the per-sensor dose-response tables. If and only if numeric data is obtained, FREEZE: 'sensor optimisation in Marionette reduced ymin (leak) and raised ymax without systematically changing n' - i.e. the evolution campaign moved the dynamic range, not the cooperativity - and score it by refitting Hill curves to the pre- and post-optimisation sensor responses. If the data cannot be obtained openly, drop this candidate rather than citing it as evidence.
candidates.biggest_risk: The data may simply not be openly available in machine-readable form, in which case this is a dead end that costs a day. There is also a conceptual risk: directed evolution changed protein sequence, not just expression level, so there is no reason to expect n to be conserved - the prediction could fail for a reason that teaches nothing about the design law.

candidates.name: Light-inducible gene expression circuits with identified ODE models (optogenetic dose-response)
candidates.system: Light-inducible transcription in yeast (Ruess 2015, iterative experiment design on a light-inducible circuit) and in E. coli (Olson 2014, optically programmed gene expression signals with a light-plate apparatus). Design change: light intensity, duty cycle and pulse timing, which shift the reporter response without any genetic change at all.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Time-resolved fluorescent reporter output as a function of a programmed light input, fitted to identified ODE models with estimated parameters and confidence intervals.
candidates.why_it_fits: The input is continuously and precisely programmable, which makes dose-response shifting almost free experimentally, and both papers already publish identified models with parameter uncertainties - exactly the 'model that makes a number' requirement. It also connects directly to the project's optogenetic-xenobot interest (light sensors triggering behaviour) without needing animals. Ranked low only because I verified the papers and not the data.

public_data.what: Crossref record for the yeast light-inducible circuit characterisation paper with identified model. Data availability NOT verified - PNAS 2015, supplementary not fetched.
public_data.licence: unknown for the data; metadata only

public_data.what: Crossref record for the E. coli optically programmed gene expression paper. Data availability NOT verified.
public_data.licence: unknown for the data; metadata only

candidates.the_test: Feasibility first: locate the time-course reporter data (the light-plate-apparatus hardware designs are known to be open, the measurement data less so). If obtained, FREEZE: 'the circuit's steady-state dose-response to time-averaged light intensity is the same function whether that average is produced by constant dim light or by pulsed bright light at matched duty cycle, up to a pulse frequency set by the reporter maturation time.' This is a genuinely interesting invariance - it says the circuit integrates photons, not pulses - and it is testable purely by re-analysing existing pulse-train experiments if they were run at more than one duty cycle.
candidates.biggest_risk: Two compounding gaps: I verified neither dataset's availability, and the duty-cycle-matched experiments needed for the proposed test may simply never have been run, in which case the only way to test the prediction is new wet-lab work, which violates the weeks-not-months constraint. Treat as a backup track, not a primary.

could_not_find: Any openly downloadable quantitative dose-response table for the Marionette sensors. I verified the paper record via Crossref and found the bioRxiv preprint DOI 10.1101/285866 via Europe PMC, but I did not fetch or confirm machine-readable sensor dose-response numbers from either. Candidate 5's score reflects this gap, not a judgement that the data does not exist.

Any confirmed public dataset for the optogenetic candidates (Olson 2014, Ruess 2015). Both papers verified; neither dataset located. In particular I could not confirm that duty-cycle-matched pulse experiments exist in the published data, which is what the proposed test needs.

Zenodo yielded nothing usable. Structured queries ('dose-response' AND promoter AND Hill; 'transfer function' AND 'gene circuit') both returned 0 hits via https://zenodo.org/api/records, and the loose keyword query returned 157,446 hits dominated by unrelated plant and clinical records. I did not find a single curated synthetic-circuit transfer-function dataset there.

BioStudies search for 'synthetic gene circuit dose response' returned 1,198,796 hits with no useful relevance ranking - the top results were PMC-mirrored article records, not quantitative dose-response datasets. I could not make this repository yield anything for this question.

The repressor identity behind the Bacteroides UCF's Gate1..Gate7 model names. The 15.25 MB file I fetched does not state it in the model names, so I could not group RBS-variant families there and could not use that library as a holdout in this run.

Confirmation that the Cello variant suffixes (S1-S4, P1-P3, B1-B3, Q1-Q2, and the phage-repressor equivalents) denote RBS-only changes. This is an inference from the file's naming and from how the library is described, not something I read in the data. Every pass/fail number in candidates 1, 3 and 4 depends on it, and it must be checked against the papers' part tables before anything is frozen.

A canonical CIDARLAB/CELLO-UCF repository - the Cello-v2-1-Core README references it, but https://api.github.com/repos/CIDARLAB/CELLO-UCF/git/trees/master returned 404 in this run. I used the UCFs vendored inside CIDARLAB/Cello-v2-1-Core (Apache-2.0, last pushed 2024-09-16) instead, so the provenance chain runs through that repo, not an upstream UCF repo.

Any independent check that the shipped Hill parameters are the authors' published fits rather than values re-derived or re-bounded by the Cello toolchain. This is the single largest threat to candidate 1 and is why refitting from the raw cytometry is leg (4) of its test rather than an optional extra.

design.label: design-reporter
design.chosen: Candidate 1, narrowed: 'Threshold-steepness separability in translation-initiation-variant repressor gates' (Cello UCF libraries). I keep the scout's recommendation but I do NOT keep its frozen statement, which I refuted during design on its own calibration library, and I do NOT keep its yeast counterexample, which dissolves once the side condition is checked against the DNA rather than the gate name.
design.one_paragraph: A repressor NOT-gate is a sigmoid: output promoter activity y falls with input promoter activity x along y = ymin + (ymax-ymin)/(1+(x/K)^n). The claim worth freezing is that changing ONLY the ribosome binding site in front of the repressor is close to a pure translation of that sigmoid along the log-x axis: it moves the threshold K by several fold while leaving the Hill coefficient n alone. That makes threshold and steepness separable design axes, which is exactly the kind of invariance Lean-for-Biology can state as a theorem with explicit side conditions, and it closes a gap the registry already admits (lean/registry/laws/gene-regulatory-dynamics.json is a placeholder with lean_ref.module = null and lean_ref.theorem = null, status 'proposed, class gap'). I verified the raw data myself rather than trusting the scout, and found three things that change the design. (a) The scout's frozen statement, |n_i-n_j|/mean(n) <= 0.15, is already FALSE on its own calibration library: BM3R1 pairs B1/B2 and B2/B3 in Eco1C1G1T1 give 0.1587 (n = 3.4 vs 2.9). A test that fails before you start is not a freeze, it is a typo. (b) 'Same repressor, RBS-only change' must be checked against the cassette part list, not the gate name. The SrpR 'family of 4' is not one: S1_SrpR_structure uses terminator ECK120019600 while S2/S3/S4 use ECK120029600, so the headline 10x K-fold rests on a gate that differs in two parts. (c) The yeast counterexample is mostly not a counterexample. In SC1C1G1T1 the two CI gates have IDENTICAL cassettes (Kozak12, CI_a) and so do the two CI434 gates (Kozak15, CI434_a) - they differ somewhere else, so they are out of scope by the side condition. Only LexA (Kozak24 vs Kozak14) is a genuine translation-initiation-only yeast pair. So the honest boundary claim is n = 1, not a kingdom difference, and the real modifier may be repressor FOLD rather than kingdom: TetR-homologs are tightest (max relative n difference 0.1587 over 9 strict pairs), phage repressors looser (0.2124 for 933W), the single yeast pair loosest (0.2604). The test freezes two numeric bounds and a composite separability index, scores them on libraries I have not opened, and - the leg that makes it real science rather than curve-fitting - re-fits the Hill function from the shipped 250-bin single-cell cytometry histograms instead of trusting Cello's own fit.

equations: Gate transfer function (shipped verbatim in the UCF as functions/Hill_response, read from the fetched Eco1C1G1T1.UCF.json): y = ymin + (ymax - ymin) / (1 + (x/K)^n), where x is input promoter activity in RPU (relative promoter units) and y is output promoter activity in RPU.
Input composition for a 2-input NOR gate (shipped as functions/linear_input_composition): x = x1 + x2.

Refit observable (mine, leg 4): for each gate g and each of the 12 input levels x_j, the cytometry record gives a 250-bin log-spaced YFP histogram (bin[], output[]). Define the level summary as the histogram median in log10 space, m_gj. Fit the four Hill parameters by least squares on log10 m: minimise sum_j (log10 m_gj - log10 Hill(x_j; ymax,ymin,K,n))^2. Fitting in log space is part of the freeze because least squares in linear space is dominated by the ON state and would hide n.

Pairwise statistics (mine, the pre-registered test quantities). For two gates i, j in the same family: relative steepness difference dn_ij = |n_i - n_j| / ((n_i + n_j)/2); threshold fold Kfold_ij = max(K_i,K_j)/min(K_i,K_j); separability index S_ij = log2(Kfold_ij) / dn_ij, read as 'octaves of threshold shift bought per unit of relative steepness drift'. S = +inf when dn = 0.

Side condition, machine-checkable (mine). A pair is IN SCOPE iff: (i) the two gates share the same 'regulator' and 'group' field in the UCF gates collection; (ii) their cassette component lists (from the structures collection, the device whose name contains 'cassette') have the same length and differ in EXACTLY ONE position; (iii) the part at that differing position has type 'rbs' in the parts collection (type kozak or the eukaryotic equivalent for yeast); (iv) Kfold >= 2.0, i.e. the design change actually moved the threshold at least a doubling. Condition (iv) excludes near-null design changes, for which S is small by construction rather than by biology.
fitted_and_on_what: NOTHING is fitted to set the frozen bounds except the calibration library Eco1C1G1T1 (Nielsen et al. 2016, doi:10.1126/science.aac7341, verified via api.crossref.org this run), and the bounds are set with deliberate slack below its worst case so that a holdout failure is a real failure and not a margin artefact.

Calibration, computed by me from the fetched file (script D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents/scratch/design-reporter/calib.py): 9 in-scope strict pairs across 4 TetR-homolog families. dn values: BM3R1 B1/B2 0.1587, B1/B3 0.0000, B2/B3 0.1587; PhlF P1/P2 0.0253, P1/P3 0.0488, P2/P3 0.0741; QacR Q1/Q2 0.1176; SrpR S2/S3 0.0741, S2/S4 0.0741, S3/S4 0.0000. Max dn = 0.1587. Restricting further to Kfold >= 2.0 leaves 6 pairs with S = 12.01 (BM3R1 B1/B2, Kfold 3.75), inf (BM3R1 B1/B3, Kfold 6.50), 83.56 (PhlF P1/P2, Kfold 4.333), 60.24 (PhlF P1/P3, Kfold 7.667), 17.60 (QacR Q1/Q2, Kfold 4.20), 17.85 (SrpR S2/S4, Kfold 2.50). Minimum finite S on calibration = 12.01.

The shipped Eco1C1G1T1 parameters are quantised. I read them as raw strings: B1_BM3R1_model n='3.4', K='0.04', ymax='0.5'; S1_SrpR_model K='0.01'. That is two significant figures on n and one to two on K. For K = 0.01 the implied uncertainty is about +/-0.005, i.e. +/-50%, so the much-quoted SrpR 10x K-fold is not a measured 10x. The second E. coli library Eco2C1G5T1 ships full precision (R1_Lambda_model n=2.25481011, K=0.043390621), so precision is NOT uniform across libraries. This alone makes the cytometry refit mandatory rather than a nice-to-have.
held_out: UNTOUCHED (I have not downloaded or opened these; existence and byte sizes confirmed from https://api.github.com/repos/CIDARLAB/Cello-v2-1-Core/git/trees/main?recursive=1, fetched this run): library/constraints/Eco1C2G2T2.UCF.json (2,610,885 bytes) - the PRIMARY holdout, a second independent E. coli library; library/constraints/Eco2C1G3T1.UCF.json (864,264 bytes); library/constraints/Bth1C1G1T1.UCF.json (15,251,526 bytes, Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron, doi:10.1038/s41587-020-0468-5 verified).

SEEN DURING DESIGN, therefore demoted from holdout to calibration-of-the-boundary and must be reported as such in the paper: Eco2C1G5T1.UCF.json (phage repressors, 46,518 bytes) and SC1C1G1T1.UCF.json (yeast, 1,744,232 bytes, doi:10.1038/s41564-020-0757-2 verified). Pretending these are holdouts would be the easiest way to make this work dishonest, so the values I saw are listed: 933W R8/R9 dn=0.2124 Kfold=2.696 S=6.74; Lambda R1/R2 dn=0.0755 Kfold=3.755 S=25.28; P2 R13/R14 dn=0.1967 Kfold=5.194 S=12.08, R13/R15 dn=0.0533 Kfold=14.813 S=72.96, R14/R15 dn=0.1438 Kfold=2.852 S=10.51; yeast LexA P1/P2 dn=0.2604 Kfold=2.325 S=4.68 (the ONLY in-scope yeast pair).

The cytometry refit is an internal holdout: the raw 12x250-bin histograms in Eco1C1G1T1 have not been used to compute any number above; everything above came from the shipped parameters collection. Confirmed present: function F1_AmeR_cytometry has a table of length 12, each entry with keys x (float, e.g. 0.004843), bin (250 floats), output (250 floats).

frozen_predictions.statement: For every in-scope pair (same regulator, cassettes differ in exactly one position, that part is an RBS/Kozak, Kfold >= 2.0) in the untouched E. coli library Eco1C2G2T2, the relative steepness difference satisfies dn = |n_i-n_j|/mean(n) <= 0.25.
frozen_predictions.number: 0.25 (calibration max over 9 strict pairs in Eco1C1G1T1 was 0.1587; the bound is about 1.6x that, leaving room for a different library's precision while staying below the 0.2604 seen for the yeast Kozak pair)
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: Two or more in-scope pairs in Eco1C2G2T2 give dn > 0.25, OR any single in-scope pair gives dn > 0.40. One failure between 0.25 and 0.40 is recorded as a partial refutation and the law is restated with the offending repressor fold excluded, with the exclusion written into the Lean hypotheses.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Shipped Hill parameters in https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CIDARLAB/Cello-v2-1-Core/main/library/constraints/Eco1C2G2T2.UCF.json (Apache-2.0), scored by the same script that produced the calibration table, run unchanged.

frozen_predictions.statement: For every in-scope pair in Eco1C2G2T2, the separability index S = log2(Kfold)/dn is at least 6.0, i.e. an RBS swap buys at least six octaves of threshold shift per unit of relative steepness drift.
frozen_predictions.number: 6.0 (half the minimum finite calibration value, 12.01, which was BM3R1 B1/B2)
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: The median S over in-scope Eco1C2G2T2 pairs is below 6.0, OR more than one third of in-scope pairs fall below 6.0. The phage pair 933W, seen during design, sits at 6.74, just above this line; if Eco1C2G2T2 clusters near 6.74 rather than near 12-80, the law is real but far weaker than the TetR-homolog data suggests, and that must be reported as a weakening, not a pass.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Same file as P1. S comes from the same two numbers but is pre-registered separately because it is the quantity a design rule would use (how much threshold can I buy before the sigmoid changes shape), and it can fail while P1 passes - a pair with tiny dn and tiny Kfold passes P1 and fails P2.

frozen_predictions.statement: When I re-fit all four Hill parameters myself from the shipped 12x250-bin cytometry histograms of Eco1C1G1T1, by log-space least squares on the per-level histogram median, the steepness invariance survives my own fit: max dn over the 9 in-scope calibration pairs computed from MY n values is still <= 0.25, and my refit n correlates with the shipped n across all 20 gates at Pearson r >= 0.80.
frozen_predictions.number: r >= 0.80 and max refit dn <= 0.25
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: Pearson r between refit n and shipped n is below 0.80 across the 20 gates, OR max refit dn exceeds 0.25 for two or more of the 9 in-scope pairs, OR my refit n for any gate differs from the shipped n by more than a factor of 1.5. ANY of these refutes the biological reading and converts the project into a methods result: that the cooperativity reported in a widely reused circuit-design library is substantially set by the fitting procedure, not by the measurement.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: The cytometry collection inside the already-fetched Eco1C1G1T1.UCF.json. Verified structure: 12 table entries per gate, each with x (input RPU), bin[250], output[250]. No new download, no wet lab. This leg runs FIRST, because a failure here makes P1/P2 uninteresting whichever way they score.

frozen_predictions.statement: Steepness drift is ordered by repressor fold, not by kingdom: the maximum in-scope dn for TetR-homolog families is strictly less than for phage-immunity-repressor families, which in turn is less than for the eukaryotic-expression families. Direction only, no threshold on the gap.
frozen_predictions.number: Seen ordering to beat: TetR 0.1587 < phage 0.2124 < yeast 0.2604. The prediction is that adding the untouched Eco1C2G2T2 (TetR-homolog repressors per the scout) keeps the TetR maximum below 0.2124.
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: The TetR-homolog maximum dn in Eco1C2G2T2 exceeds 0.2124, which collapses the TetR-vs-phage gap and removes the fold explanation. Also refuted in the other direction if the Bacteroides library (a third prokaryote, different host physiology) shows TetR-homolog families with dn above 0.2124 while its phage-type families stay below - that would point at host, not fold.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Eco1C2G2T2.UCF.json plus, as a weak third point, Bth1C1G1T1.UCF.json. HONEST GAP stated up front: the Bacteroides UCF names its gates Gate1..Gate7 with no repressor identity in the model names (reported by the scout; I did not download the 15 MB file to confirm), so the fold assignment would have to come from the Taketani 2020 supplementary (doi:10.1038/s41587-020-0468-5). If that mapping cannot be recovered, P4 is scored on Eco1C2G2T2 alone and the ordering claim stays at n = 2 folds.

frozen_predictions.statement: After the cassette-level side condition is applied, the number of in-scope translation-initiation-only pairs in the yeast library SC1C1G1T1 is exactly one (LexA, Kozak24 vs Kozak14), so no kingdom-level claim is supportable from this dataset. This is a prediction about what a reader checking our work will find, and it is the claim most likely to be contradicted by the published supplementary.
frozen_predictions.number: 1 in-scope yeast pair out of 3 nominal families (CI and CI434 excluded: identical cassettes Kozak12/CI_a and Kozak15/CI434_a respectively, read by me from the fetched SC1C1G1T1.UCF.json)
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: The yeast Cello paper (doi:10.1038/s41564-020-0757-2) or its supplementary shows that the CI and CI434 gate pairs DO differ only in translation initiation and the UCF structures collection simply omits the difference. Then the yeast set returns to 3 pairs, the kingdom-boundary reading is back on the table, and our 'n = 1' caution was wrong - a result we must publish as such.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: The structures collection of the fetched SC1C1G1T1.UCF.json (already read: P1_CI_structure and P2_CI_structure are both ['Kozak12','CI_a']), cross-checked against the paper's supplementary part tables.

frozen_predictions.statement: RPU normalisation is library-specific, so the SAME repressor characterised in two libraries will show a K ratio larger than the within-library RBS-driven Kfold for at least one repressor. Consequence: the invariance statement is valid WITHIN a library only, and the Lean theorem must carry a 'same measurement standard' hypothesis.
frozen_predictions.number: At least one repressor with cross-library K ratio > 4.333 (the six in-scope within-library Kfold values on calibration were 2.50, 3.75, 4.20, 4.333, 6.50, 7.667, median 4.267; I take the nearest observed value above it, 4.333, as the threshold)
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: Every repressor present in two or more of Eco1C1G1T1, Eco1C2G2T2, Eco2C1G3T1 has a cross-library K ratio below 4.333. That would mean RPU is portable across libraries, the 'same measurement standard' hypothesis can be dropped from the theorem, and the law is stronger than we claimed.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: K values for BM3R1, PhlF, QacR, BetI, AmtR, AmeR across Eco1C1G1T1 (have), Eco1C2G2T2 (holdout) and Eco2C1G3T1 (holdout, scout reports 6 gates, one per repressor), plus each library's own measurement_std record (present as a collection in every UCF I opened).

design.what_is_frozen_and_when: Pre-registration as a git commit, in this order, with nothing downloaded between the commit and the scoring. STEP 0 is the freeze. Commit 1 ('freeze: track-1 reporter separability pre-registration') contains: (a) PREREG.md with P1-P6 verbatim, every threshold, the side-condition definition, and the explicit disclosure that Eco2C1G5T1 and SC1C1G1T1 were read during design and are therefore NOT holdouts, with the values I saw listed; (b) score.py, the complete scoring script, taking a UCF path and emitting the pairwise table - written and committed BEFORE any holdout file exists on disk; (c) calibration.csv, the 9-pair Eco1C1G1T1 table reproduced by that script; (d) the GitHub blob sha of each untouched holdout, taken from the tree listing already fetched, so a later claim that the file changed is checkable. Only after commit 1 is pushed does anything download Eco1C2G2T2. The scoring run is commit 2 and MUST invoke score.py unmodified; any change to score.py after commit 1 is itself a reportable deviation, logged in PREREG.md as an amendment with a reason, and the pre-amendment result reported alongside. The cytometry refit (P3) is frozen in the same commit, including the choice of log-space least squares and the histogram median as the level summary, because those two choices are where a result could be quietly tuned.
steps: 0. FREEZE. Write PREREG.md and score.py, reproduce the calibration table with score.py, commit and push. No holdout file on disk. (Half a day.)

1. P3 FIRST, the refit leg. Parse the cytometry collection of the already-fetched Eco1C1G1T1, compute per-level histogram medians, fit the 4-parameter Hill by log-space least squares with multi-start to avoid local minima, bootstrap the histograms (resample bins by their counts, 1000 replicates) for a confidence interval on each n. Report r(refit n, shipped n), the per-gate ratio, and the 9-pair dn table from refit values. If this fails, STOP and rewrite the project as a methods paper - do not proceed to the holdouts with a broken instrument. (3-4 days.)

2. Score P1, P2, P4 on Eco1C2G2T2. Download, run score.py unmodified, emit the pairwise table with the strict flag and the pass/fail per prediction. Do not inspect the file by eye before the script runs. (1 day.)
3. Score P6 cross-library on Eco2C1G3T1 plus the two E. coli libraries already in hand, and read each library's measurement_std record to document what RPU means in each. (1 day.)

4. Attempt the Bacteroides fold mapping from the Taketani 2020 supplementary (checking the Author Correction, 10.1038/s41587-020-0545-9, first). If it cannot be recovered, record the gap in PREREG.md as an amendment and score P4 on two folds. Do not guess the mapping. (1-2 days.)
5. Resolve P5 against the yeast paper's supplementary part tables. Whatever the answer, it goes in the paper; if we were wrong, the correction is the first thing a reader should see. (1 day.)

6. Write the Lean law. Propose it as the successor of registry id gene-regulatory-dynamics (currently a placeholder with lean_ref.module = null), version 2.0.0, against the current lawset. The theorem is a statement about the Hill family, not about cells: given two Hill transfer functions sharing ymax, ymin and n, the second is the first composed with a scaling of the input, y2(x) = y1(x * K1/K2) - i.e. equal n is EXACTLY equivalent to the two curves being log-translates of each other. That direction is a genuine theorem and is what makes the empirical claim worth measuring. The empirical content then lives entirely in the named hypothesis 'an RBS-only change preserves n to within 0.25 relative', which the registry records as a measured side condition with its calibration and holdout scores attached, never as a proved fact. (3-5 days, and it needs the Lean thread, not this one.)
7. Write up, treating the refuted scout statement, the SrpR terminator discrepancy, the yeast n=1 collapse, and the 2-significant-figure quantisation as findings rather than footnotes.
design.what_would_make_this_a_paper: A PAPER if either branch resolves sharply. Branch A, the law holds: P3 passes (my own refits reproduce the shipped n, r >= 0.80), P1 and P2 pass on the untouched Eco1C2G2T2, and P4's fold ordering survives. Then the result is a quantitative, pre-registered, Lean-formalised design law - threshold and steepness are separable axes for TetR-family repressor gates under a stated measurement standard, with a separability index a circuit designer can use to decide whether an RBS swap is safe, and with the exact equivalence 'equal n <=> log-translate' proved in the kernel. The hook for this project is that it closes a gap the registry itself labels 'not formalised'. Branch B, the law is a fitting artefact: P3 fails. Then the paper is 'the reported cooperativity in genetic-circuit design-automation libraries is partly set by the fitting pipeline', demonstrated by refitting from the raw single-cell histograms the libraries themselves ship - which matters to everyone who has used a UCF since 2016 (doi:10.1126/science.aac7341) and is directly actionable: ship the refit code. Branch B is the better paper if it happens. MERELY CONFIRMATORY, and we should say so and stop: P1 passes everywhere including yeast and Bacteroides, with no fold or kingdom structure and no marginal cases. Then 'n is roughly constant within a family' is a statement about how sloppy n is in a 4-parameter fit, carries no design content, and is worth a dashboard row and a registry note, not a manuscript. NOT A PAPER under any outcome: a single extra family added to the calibration set to rescue a bound, or an amended score.py whose pre-amendment result is not reported.
risks: Selection bias, the deepest risk and only partly addressable. The RBS variants in these libraries were chosen by the original authors BECAUSE they gave good digital behaviour. The honest scope of any passing result is therefore 'among RBS variants that passed Cello's own screen, n is preserved' - weaker and less interesting than a claim about RBS variants in general. Mitigation: state it in the abstract, not the limitations; and note that the frozen test is still informative because the screen was applied per gate, not per family, so n-invariance ACROSS a family was not what was selected for.

Parameter quantisation in the calibration library. Shipped n is 2 significant figures (verified: '3.4', '2.9') and some K values are 1 ('0.01'), so dn has a floor of roughly 0.015-0.03 from rounding alone and Kfold at the low-K end can be wrong by tens of percent. This does not threaten the bound (0.159 is far above the rounding floor) but it does make headline K-folds untrustworthy. The P3 refit is the mitigation and that is why it runs first.

The separability index S is my own composite and is not scale-free in a benign way: as dn -> 0 it diverges, and for small Kfold it is small by construction. The Kfold >= 2.0 precondition patches the second problem, and I chose 2.0 AFTER seeing both the calibration and the two seen libraries - a disclosed, not hidden, degree of freedom. If a reviewer objects, P1 (the dn bound alone) stands without S.
The yeast arm is n = 1 after the side condition. It cannot support a kingdom claim and must not be written as one. P5 exists to make this a prediction rather than a hedge.

Low holdout cardinality overall. The scout reports about 12 families in Eco1C2G2T2; if the strict cassette test and Kfold >= 2.0 cut that to three or four in-scope pairs, P1 and P2 are being scored on single digits and 'more than one third fail' is one or two pairs. If in-scope pairs number fewer than four, the pre-registered response is to report the result as underpowered and NOT to relax the side condition.

The refit leg runs on the calibration library because that is where the histograms are in hand. If Eco1C2G2T2 ships cytometry too (likely, given its 2.6 MB size), the refit should be extended to it - but that extension is an amendment, logged.

Confirmation pressure from the dashboard. This track is one of six and a green row is tempting. The two commits and the unmodified-script rule exist to make a red row cheap to produce and expensive to avoid.
first_week: Day 1 am: write PREREG.md with P1-P6 and the disclosure of what was already seen. Write score.py with the four-part side condition reading the gates, structures and parts collections - not gate-name regexes, since the UCF has explicit 'group'/'regulator' fields and the cassette device component list, both verified present.

Day 1 pm: reproduce the 9-pair calibration table with score.py, confirm it matches this design exactly (BM3R1 0.1587, 0.0000, 0.1587 / PhlF 0.0253, 0.0488, 0.0741 / QacR 0.1176 / SrpR 0.0741, 0.0741, 0.0000), commit and push commit 1. Record the GitHub blob shas of the three untouched holdouts. Add a track-1 dashboard row pointing at the commit, status 'frozen, unscored'.

Day 2: cytometry parser. Extract all 20 gates x 12 levels x 250 bins from the fetched Eco1C1G1T1, sanity-check that per-level medians are monotone decreasing in x for every gate, and flag any gate where they are not - a non-monotone gate cannot support a Hill fit and must be excluded by a rule written down today, not later.
Day 3: the refit itself. Multi-start log-space least squares, four free parameters, bounds only on positivity. Produce refit-vs-shipped scatter for n and for K, the Pearson r, and the per-gate ratio.

Day 4: bootstrap the refit (1000 histogram resamples per gate) and score P3. Commit the result whichever way it goes, with the figure. If P3 fails, write the one-page pivot note to the methods-paper framing and tell the orchestrator before touching the holdouts.

Day 5: if P3 passed, download Eco1C2G2T2, run score.py unmodified, score P1/P2/P4, commit as commit 2, update the dashboard row with the actual pass/fail per prediction and the pairwise table. Draft the two-paragraph result for the paper thread, and send the SrpR terminator discrepancy and the yeast cassette-identity finding to the claims thread as separate checkable notes - both are independently useful corrections to a widely used public library regardless of how our law scores.
design.compute_needed: Laptop-class Windows box only, and that is a feature of this track rather than a limitation. Total input is about 24 MB of JSON across all five libraries (verified byte sizes 4,834,067 + 2,610,885 + 864,264 + 46,518 + 1,744,232 + 15,251,526 from the GitHub tree listing). The heaviest operation is 20 gates x 1000 bootstrap replicates x a 4-parameter least-squares fit over 12 points - seconds to a couple of minutes in scipy.optimize.least_squares, single core. Extending the refit to every gate in all five libraries (roughly 70 gates) is still minutes. NO GPU is required and none should be requested: an Explorer GPU allocation sitting on a curve fit would violate this project's own fair-use rule about not holding an allocation for CPU work. Modal is worth using for exactly one optional thing: a permutation null for P2, shuffling n values across families within a library 10^5 times to get the distribution of min S under the null 'n is unrelated to family membership', which is embarrassingly parallel and would make the S bound inferential rather than descriptive. That is a strengthening, not part of the freeze.
design.physical_build: None, and proposing one here would be decoration rather than evidence. A transcription-factor dose-response result cannot be demonstrated by a printed object, and a 3D-printed 'sigmoid landscape' would be a figure pretending to be an experiment. The one defensible Formlabs use is downstream and explicitly outside the frozen test: if branch A holds and the team wants a wet-lab confirmation leg, a Form 3B+ part in BioMed Clear or standard Clear can serve as a gradient-generating microfluidic manifold or a plate-geometry insert for running an RBS-variant inducer titration at more input levels than the 12 the UCFs ship. That is a phase-3 instrument, it must be costed and scheduled separately, and nothing in P1-P6 depends on it. Flagging this honestly matters because the contracting side of this project has an incentive to attach a print to every track.

existing.statement_plain: For a two-species system linearised at a uniform steady state with Jacobian [[a,b],[c,d]] that is stable when well mixed (a+d<0, ad-bc>0), some spatial mode q>0 is unstable iff 2*sqrt(Du*Dv*(ad-bc)) < Dv*a + Du*d.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header, 'What is not proved here': nothing about organisms (that a tissue is such a system, or which chemicals u, v are); nothing nonlinear (existence, selection, stability of the finite-amplitude pattern); nothing about finite domains (the continuum condition is necessary, not sufficient, on a bounded domain). Registry scope: two species, smooth kinetics linearised about a homogeneous steady state, constant positive diffusivities, unbounded domain, no growth or mechanics.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: It is the only kernel-checked statement about the Jacobian of a two-component regulatory circuit. WellMixedStable (trace<0, det>0) is exactly the local stability test for a two-gene circuit's operating point, so a design that claims a stable reporter set-point with a committed Jacobian violating it can be eliminated by arithmetic. It also bounds the reporter track away from track 2: a two-node circuit whose two species diffuse equally cannot produce spatial reporter patterns (next row).

existing.statement_plain: With Du = Dv and the uniform state stable, the mode determinant D(q) is positive for every q >= 0: no spatial mode is unstable.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Two-species only. Header: 'with three or more species Turing instability with equal diffusivities is possible (Marcon et al. 2016, doi:10.7554/eLife.14022), so this corollary must not be applied to larger networks'. (That DOI is quoted from the file; I did not fetch it: verified=false.)
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Removes 'the reporter response shifts because the population self-patterns' from the hypothesis space for any two-node intracellular circuit in a well-mixed or equal-diffusivity culture, so a measured shift must be attributed to the input-output map itself.

existing.statement_plain: If a rate is X(T) = X0 * Q10^((T - Tref)/10) with X0 != 0 and Q10 > 0, then X(T2)/X(T1) = Q10^((T2-T1)/10) and log of that ratio is (T2-T1)/10 * log Q10.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header: 'Named hypotheses: the Q10 form itself (an empirical rule, not a theorem of physics)'. Registry: 'That a rate follows a Q10 law at all, and a value of Q10: both are inputs. The project's conditions fix 25 C and no candidate commits a Q10, so no instance is evaluated.'
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Temperature is the cheapest 'new condition' for a reporter assay. If synthesis and loss rates each carry a committed Q10, the predicted fold-change of reporter rate between two temperatures is fixed; a design committing to a temperature shift outside Q10^((T2-T1)/10) is eliminable. No reporter instance exists yet.

existing.statement_plain: Given a response curve that is zero outside [ctMin, ctMax] and at most pRef*Q10^((T-tRef)/10) inside, no positive sustained output is possible outside the window and output never exceeds the Q10 bound.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header: 'Every empirical ingredient is a NAMED HYPOTHESIS: a structure whose fields carry the observation, passed to the theorem as an argument'. Registry scope: taxa Teleostei; 'CTmin, CTmax, Q10 and P_ref are design inputs'.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Out of scope as a verdict (Teleostei, muscle power). It is the closest existing template for this track: a bounded response function carried as a structure, plus two rules_out lemmas (outside the operating window; above the ceiling). A ReporterResponse structure with floor, ceiling and window would reuse the proofs almost verbatim.

existing.statement_plain: If arterial oxygen content is any nondecreasing function ca of oxygen partial pressure and partial pressure falls with height, supply falls with height; feasibility is downward closed and infeasibility is upward closed.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header: 'Arterial content enters as a MONOTONE FUNCTION of oxygen partial pressure, which is what a Hill curve is (physiology/haemoglobin.js). Nothing here formalises the Hill equation, the Bohr shift, the Root effect, or any compensation an animal might make'. Atmosphere is 'a named hypothesis with no numbers'.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: The only place in the library where a Hill-type curve appears, and only as the hypothesis hca : forall x y, x <= y -> ca x <= ca y. It shows the house style for monotone input-output reasoning (monotone map composed with monotone input gives a one-sided feasible set). For a reporter: if the response is assumed monotone in inducer, the set of inducer doses reaching a threshold is an up-set; a claimed band-pass response is eliminable under that hypothesis. The Hill form itself is still missing.

existing.statement_plain: If the Boolean check passes, every node the map links to the gene is in the declared change set; a change set that omits a mapped node fails the check.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header, 'What is assumed, not proved': 'that the map's links are the gene's full reach (an unstudied node is not gene-free)'.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: An edit that shifts a reporter by changing a regulator must declare every other target of that regulator. A candidate 'edit TF X, only reporter Y changes' is eliminated when the map links X elsewhere (the existing certificate elim_tbx5a_fin_only_edit_G2 is this pattern). It favours designs that edit the reporter's own promoter or operator rather than a shared regulator. Needs a regulator-target map for the chosen circuit, which the library does not contain.

missing.law: Hill response function and its shape invariants
missing.statement_math: h_{n,K}(x) = x^n / (K^n + x^n), x >= 0, K > 0, n > 0. (i) 0 <= h < 1, h(0)=0, h(K)=1/2, h strictly increasing, lim_{x->inf} h = 1. (ii) log-sensitivity d ln h / d ln x = n (1 - h(x)) <= n. (iii) x_p := h^{-1}(p) = K (p/(1-p))^{1/n}, so x_{0.9}/x_{0.1} = 81^{1/n}. (iv) repressor form 1 - h is strictly decreasing. Rules-out forms: a response claimed to rise from 10% to 90% over an input ratio r < 81^{1/n} is impossible for Hill coefficient <= n; a claimed half-maximal input different from K is impossible.
missing.why_needed: Every reporter design commits to (K, n, floor, ceiling). Without the definition in Lean nothing about a dose-response can be stated, let alone eliminated. (iii) is the direct test of 'shifting': moving EC50 means changing K; changing steepness means changing n.
missing.difficulty: easy - real-power algebra and monotonicity; Mathlib has Real.rpow_le_rpow_left_iff, rpow_natCast, div_lt_one; the derivative in (ii) needs HasDerivAt.rpow but is routine.
missing.source: Weiss 1997, 'The Hill equation revisited: uses and misuses', FASEB J 11:835-841, doi:10.1096/fasebj.11.11.9285481 (Crossref resolved this run, verified=true). Ferrell and Ha 2014, 'Ultrasensitivity part I', Trends Biochem Sci 39:496-503, doi:10.1016/j.tibs.2014.08.003 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). The 81^{1/n} identity is my own calculation from (iii): (9)^{1/n}/(1/9)^{1/n} = 81^{1/n}.

missing.statement_math: dR/dt = a0 + a * h(x) - g R, with a0 >= 0, a > 0, g > 0, h in [0,1). Then R*(x) = (a0 + a h(x))/g is the unique equilibrium; R(t) = R* + (R(0) - R*) e^{-g t}; a0/g <= R* < (a0+a)/g; dynamic range R*(inf)/R*(0) <= (a0+a)/a0; half-response time t_1/2 = ln 2 / g independent of x. With growth dilution g = g_deg + lambda. Rules-out forms: a claimed fold-induction above (a0+a)/a0; a claimed steady level outside [a0/g,(a0+a)/g); a claimed response time shorter than ln2/g.
missing.why_needed: This is the smallest model that maps circuit parameters to what a plate reader measures. It gives three independent eliminators (floor, ceiling, speed) and tells the experiment which measurements can discriminate surviving designs.

missing.statement_math: fold-change(c) = 1 / (1 + p_A(c) * (R/N_NS) * exp(-b*de_RA)), with p_A(c) = (1 + c/K_A)^m / ((1 + c/K_A)^m + exp(-b*de_AI) (1 + c/K_I)^m), m = number of inducer sites. Rules-out form: a design that changes only R or only de_RA and commits to an EC50 shift with unchanged leakiness is impossible.

missing.law: Monotone (cooperative) systems: order preservation and monotone steady-state characteristic
missing.statement_math: For x' = f(x,u) on R^n_{>=0} with df_i/dx_j >= 0 for i != j (Kamke condition) and df_i/du >= 0: x(0) <= y(0) and u(t) <= v(t) componentwise imply x(t) <= y(t) for all t >= 0. Corollary: if each constant input u has a unique globally attracting equilibrium k(u), then k is nondecreasing. Signed version: with a sign-consistent interaction graph the same holds in an orthant order, so a cascade's steady-state response is monotone, increasing or decreasing by the parity of repressions on the path. Rules-out form: a sign-consistent circuit committed to a non-monotone (band-pass or biphasic) dose-response is impossible.
missing.why_needed: It turns circuit topology into a shape constraint without any parameter values: whole classes of wiring are eliminated for a target response shape before any fitting. It also licenses the bisection-style experiment (monotone means two doses bracket the EC50).
missing.difficulty: hard - Mathlib has scalar Gronwall and ODE uniqueness but no comparison theorem for systems (Kamke-Mueller); the invariance-of-the-cone argument must be built. A two- or three-node special case with explicit linear-in-state degradation is moderate.
missing.source: Hirsch 1985, 'Systems of Differential Equations that are Competitive or Cooperative II', SIAM J Math Anal 16:423-439, doi:10.1137/0516030 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Angeli and Sontag 2003, 'Monotone control systems', IEEE Trans Automat Control 48:1684-1698, doi:10.1109/TAC.2003.817920 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Smith, 'Monotone Dynamical Systems', AMS Surveys 41, doi:10.1090/surv/041 (Crossref resolved, verified=true).

missing.law: Positive feedback: bistability and hysteresis need a steep enough open-loop characteristic
missing.statement_math: Open a positive-feedback loop of a monotone system to get a nondecreasing characteristic k: R_{>=0} -> R_{>=0}. Closed-loop equilibria are the fixed points k(u) = u; one is stable if k'(u) < 1 and unstable if k'(u) > 1; almost every trajectory converges to a stable one. Scalar corollary to formalise first: for k(u) = b + a u^n/(K^n + u^n), if n <= 1 then k(u) = u has exactly one solution u >= 0 (no bistability, no hysteresis, no memory); three fixed points require n > 1 and sup k' > 1. For the mutual-repression toggle: du/dt = a1/(1+v^beta) - u, dv/dt = a2/(1+u^gamma) - v has a unique equilibrium when beta = gamma = 1.
missing.why_needed: A reporter 'shift' can be graded (EC50 moves) or switch-like (threshold with memory). This law says which circuits can show the second kind at all, so a design that promises a history-dependent reporter from non-cooperative parts is eliminated, and the experiment (up-sweep versus down-sweep) tests the survivors.
missing.difficulty: moderate for the scalar fixed-point counting (concavity of the Michaelian map, IVT, strict monotonicity of u - k(u)); hard for the general Angeli-Ferrell-Sontag convergence theorem (depends on the monotone-systems entry).
missing.source: Angeli, Ferrell and Sontag 2004, PNAS 101:1822-1827, doi:10.1073/pnas.0308265100 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Gardner, Cantor and Collins 2000, 'Construction of a genetic toggle switch in Escherichia coli', Nature 403:339-342, doi:10.1038/35002131 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Cherry and Adler 2000, 'How to make a Biological Switch', J Theor Biol 203:117-133, doi:10.1006/jtbi.2000.1068 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Toggle equations are written from background knowledge of the Gardner model; check against the paper before freezing.

missing.law: Composition of response functions (cascade matching)
missing.statement_math: If y = f(x) with f nondecreasing, range [f_min, f_max], and z = g(y) with g nondecreasing Hill with threshold K_g, then the cascade's output range is [g(f_min), g(f_max)] and its dynamic range g(f_max)/g(f_min) exceeds a target D only if f_min < K_g*c1(D,n) and f_max > K_g*c2(D,n) for explicit c1, c2 from x_p = K (p/(1-p))^{1/n}. For a repressing stage replace g by a0 + a(1 - h). Rules-out form: a sensor whose output range does not straddle the next stage's threshold cannot drive more than a stated fold-change in the reporter.
missing.why_needed: Most practical reporter failures are mismatch between a sensor's output range and the reporter promoter's input range. This is a parameter-level eliminator that needs only the Hill entry and monotonicity, and it is what a parts-library search would call thousands of times.
missing.difficulty: easy - composition of monotone functions and the Hill inverse; pure real arithmetic.
missing.source: Nielsen et al. 2016, 'Genetic circuit design automation', Science 352, doi:10.1126/science.aac7341 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). The inequality form above is my own restatement, not copied from the paper.

missing.law: Noise floor on a reporter read-out
missing.statement_math: For the birth-death model (production rate k, per-molecule loss g) the stationary copy number is Poisson(k/g): mean = variance, CV^2 = 1/mean. With a bursty two-stage model (burst size b), Fano factor = 1 + b >= 1 and CV^2 >= 1/mean. Consequence: two response levels with means m1 < m2 are separable at z standard deviations only if m2 - m1 >= z (sqrt(m1) + sqrt(m2)) in single cells (or the same over sqrt(N) for the mean of N cells). Rules-out form: a claimed single-cell-resolvable shift smaller than that bound.
missing.why_needed: 'Test what is left' needs a statement of what an assay can distinguish. Without a noise law the checker cannot tell a predicted shift that is testable from one that is below resolution, and cannot size the experiment.
missing.difficulty: moderate to hard - verifying that Poisson satisfies the stationary master equation is moderate (Mathlib has the Poisson PMF and tsum tools); deriving it as the limit of a continuous-time Markov chain is hard (thin CTMC support in Mathlib). The separability inequality given the Fano bound as a named hypothesis is easy.
missing.source: Thattai and van Oudenaarden 2001, 'Intrinsic noise in gene regulatory networks', PNAS 98:8614-8619, doi:10.1073/pnas.151588598 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Paulsson 2004, 'Summing up the noise in gene networks', Nature 427:415-418, doi:10.1038/nature02257 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Formulas from unverified background knowledge; the separability inequality is my own calculation (gap between means >= z times the sum of the two Poisson standard deviations).

missing.law: Growth-rate coupling of reporter concentration
missing.statement_math: For a stable reporter in balanced exponential growth at rate lambda: concentration R* = s / (lambda + g_deg), so at fixed synthesis s and g_deg << lambda, R* scales as 1/lambda. As a named hypothesis (bacterial growth law): ribosomal fraction phi_R = phi_0 + lambda/kappa_t and constitutive-protein fraction phi_P = phi_max - lambda/kappa_n style linear relations. Rules-out form: a claimed inducer-specific shift that equals, within committed intervals, the dilution factor lambda_1/lambda_2 between the two conditions cannot be attributed to the circuit.
missing.why_needed: Any new test condition (medium, temperature, inducer toxicity) changes growth rate, which shifts every reporter regardless of the circuit. This is the confound law; without it the loop will accept shifts that are dilution artefacts.
missing.difficulty: easy - algebra once the linear growth laws are carried as a structure of named hypotheses, in the style of Delphi.Empirical.
missing.source: Scott et al. 2010, 'Interdependence of Cell Growth and Gene Expression: Origins and Consequences', Science 330:1099-1102, doi:10.1126/science.1192588 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). The linear relations are written from unverified background knowledge; constants must be taken from the paper.

missing.law: Retroactivity (load) from the reporter on its upstream node
missing.statement_math: A transcription factor x binding p_T downstream sites with dissociation constant K_d follows, on the slow manifold, dx/dt = (1 - Rr(x)) * (k(t) - g x) with Rr(x) = 1 / (1 + (1 + x/K_d)^2 K_d / p_T). So adding reporter binding sites leaves the steady state of total-free balance unchanged but slows the response by the factor 1 - Rr in (0,1]. Rules-out form: a design that adds a high-copy reporter and commits to an unchanged upstream response time.
missing.why_needed: The reporter is not a passive probe. Reporter copy number is a design variable on this track, and this law says what changing it must do to the circuit being measured.
missing.difficulty: moderate - the algebraic bound 0 < 1 - Rr <= 1 and its monotonicity in p_T are easy; justifying the slow-manifold reduction (singular perturbation) is hard and should stay a named hypothesis.
missing.source: Del Vecchio, Ninfa and Sontag 2008, 'Modular cell biology: retroactivity and insulation', Mol Syst Biol 4, doi:10.1038/msb4100204 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). The expression for Rr is from unverified background knowledge and must be checked against the paper.

missing.law: Negative feedback: no sustained oscillation in a two-node loop; adaptation needs specific topologies
missing.statement_math: (a) For a planar system x' = f(x,y), y' = g(x,y) with df/dx + dg/dy < 0 everywhere on a simply connected region (true for two genes with linear degradation and no autoregulation), there is no periodic orbit (Bendixson). More generally, bounded orbits of monotone cyclic feedback systems converge to equilibria or periodic orbits. (b) Perfect adaptation of a three-node enzyme network requires a negative feedback loop with a buffering node or an incoherent feed-forward loop. Rules-out forms: a two-gene negative loop committed to a sustained oscillating reporter; a pure cascade committed to an adapting (pulse-then-return) reporter.
missing.why_needed: Covers the dynamic response shapes (pulse, oscillation, adaptation) a reporter might be asked to show, and removes topologies that cannot show them. Lower priority than the steady-state laws for a first freeze.
missing.difficulty: hard - Bendixson's criterion needs Green's theorem on a region bounded by an orbit, which Mathlib does not provide in usable form; the adaptation result is a computational enumeration in the source, not a theorem, and would enter only as a named hypothesis.
missing.source: Mallet-Paret and Smith 1990, 'The Poincare-Bendixson theorem for monotone cyclic feedback systems', J Dyn Diff Eq 2:367-421, doi:10.1007/BF01054041 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Ma et al. 2009, 'Defining Network Topologies that Can Achieve Biochemical Adaptation', Cell 138:760-773, doi:10.1016/j.cell.2009.06.013 (Crossref resolved, verified=true). Elowitz and Leibler 2000, Nature 403:335-338, doi:10.1038/35002125 (Crossref resolved, verified=true) for the three-node case that does oscillate.

laws.elimination_pattern: A certificate is two layers. Layer 1 is a hand-written lemma named *_rules_out in a law module or in lean/Delphi/Constraints.lean: its hypotheses are (a) the law's own premises or named-hypothesis structure, (b) the candidate's commitment, usually an interval such as a <= quantity and quantity <= b, and (c) one last decidable fact about the committed numbers; its conclusion is False (or a negation). Layer 2 is a generated file in lean/Delphi/Certificates/ (header: 'GENERATED by lean/eliminate/eliminate.mjs from <candidates>.json ... Do not edit; regenerate'), holding one theorem per elimination named elim_<candidate>_<constraint id>, which applies the layer-1 lemma to the candidate's numbers written as exact rationals and discharges fact (c) with by norm_num (or by decide +kernel for finite checks such as the genetic code). A real example, quoted from lean/Delphi/Certificates/Eliminations.lean lines 28-32: "/-- Candidate `neutral-mutant-fixes-one-percent`, constraint C2. -/ theorem elim_neutral_mutant_fixes_one_percent_C2 : ∀ (hM : 0 < 2000), ((1 / 200 : ℝ) ≤ (Delphi.wrightFisher 2000 hM).fixationProbability (Delphi.oneCopy 2000 hM) ∧ (Delphi.wrightFisher 2000 hM).fixationProbability (Delphi.oneCopy 2000 hM) ≤ (1 / 50 : ℝ)) → False := fun hM hu => Delphi.Constraints.neutral_fixation_rules_out 2000 hM hu (by norm_num)": the candidate committed the fixation probability to [1/200, 1/50] at M = 2000, the law says it is 1/2000, and norm_num checks 1/2000 < 1/200. Per the Constraints.lean header, the elimination is only as strong as the law's assumptions, a candidate that does not commit to them gets 'cannot rule' rather than a pass, and a surviving candidate is only 'not ruled out'. This track would first add a module (say lean/Delphi/Reporter.lean) with the Hill definition and a structure ReporterCircuit carrying a0, a, g, K, n as named hypotheses, then lemmas such as dynamic_range_rules_out (commitment lo <= R*(x2)/R*(x1), side condition (a0+a)/a0 < lo, conclusion False) and ec50_rules_out (commitment EC50 in [c,d] disjoint from the interval the law gives for K), reusing Delphi.Constraints.ne_of_lt_intervals. A reporter candidates JSON would then generate lean/Delphi/Certificates/EliminationsReporter.lean with one elim_<design>_R<k> theorem per killed design, each closed by norm_num; since rpow with non-integer n does not reduce under norm_num, commitments should use natural-number Hill coefficients or carry the evaluated power as an interval hypothesis, as elim_real_fish_sustained_flight_any_teleost_E3 does with hval. Each new law also needs a Nonempty witness and must pass propose.mjs before it can turn a verdict red.
