reader_unknown_words: Lean / Lean proofs (half: a proof checker, but not why it matters here)
reader_could_not_follow: Each cell brings a fixed length of inner wall. So the number of cells shapes the dents.

The 2021 authors ran their model many times with different settings, 243 in our check. We call this the published sweep. Even the best run fit normal cells worse than the plain average does. So our first check, which asks us to reproduce their model, may fail.
One formula in our plan was written upside down. We found the correct version and it matches to 14 decimal places. We must fix the plan before we start.
We keep a list of rules that a computer has checked, using a tool called Lean. That list has no rule about lumen shape. So no proof tool backs the biology here.
We left out one photo day at a time and tested on it.
reader_unanswerable: What does the model's formula for wall length per cell look like?
reading.reader_help: Say the core idea in one concrete sentence first, for example why more cells would make the hollow rounder or more dented. Define "dentedness" and the 0 to 1 scale at first use. Say which formula was upside down and why it matters. Cut the Lean, law-library, ANOVA and ICC material or explain why a reader should care. Give one number a reader can picture for what "winning" means. The p-value and the error figures need a plain gloss.

tracks.title: A fin or body constraint in a passive glide surrogate

scout.summary: Five printable passive-descent/glide experiments were found where a published mechanical model outputs a number before the build. The strongest is the double-winged whirling fruit of Rabault, Fauli and Carlson: it was printed on a Formlabs Form 2, dropped in a 1.2 m water tank, and its MIT-licensed repository (fetched, 3.1 MB) holds the parametric FreeCAD file, the blade-element model code, the raw per-trial descent speeds, and a stored model prediction for a wing base angle of 15 degrees that the two papers did not test experimentally (experiments are at 0 and 35 degrees only). Second is a ballasted thin-plate glider (the Li et al. 2022 quasi-steady model, extended by Pomerenk and Ristroph 2025), where the position of the centre of mass along the chord sets flutter, glide or dive; I reproduced the published maximum glide ratio (3.77 at 0.218 chord vs the paper's 3.8 near 0.22) from the fetched coefficients, but found no public raw trajectory data. Third to fifth are a 3D-printed maple samara (CC BY design files), a flying-fish body-and-fin model (digitised lift and drag polars in an MIT repository, but needs a tow tank or tunnel), and the flying-snake cross-section (needs a force balance). Gaps: no physical-model study of gliding fish larvae was found; the flying-fish wind-tunnel paper and the original Alsomitra flight paper could not be read in full (403 / not open), so their numbers here come only from abstracts, a secondary source, or a third-party digitisation.
scout.recommended: Run candidate 1, the whirling-fruit fold-angle test at a 15 degree base angle: it is the only option where the printer family (Formlabs), the CAD, the model code, the raw comparison data and an already-stored prediction for an untested condition were all fetched under an MIT licence, and it needs only a water column and a camera. Candidate 2 (ballasted plate, fin position versus glide) should follow in the same tank because it is the true forward-glide and fin-placement test, but it has no public raw data to calibrate against.

candidates.name: Whirling-fruit fold angle at an untested wing base angle (15 degrees)
candidates.system: 3D-printed double-winged autorotating fruit (dipterocarp-like): hollow spherical pod plus two curved wings of fixed mass; wing fold angle KL (wing length / radius of curvature) and base angle psi are CAD parameters. Dropped fully immersed in a water tank to match Reynolds 2400-14000 and Strouhal 0.35-0.82 of wild fruits.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Terminal descent speed U (m/s) and rotation frequency f (Hz) from 30 Hz side-view video; the fold angle KL that minimises U.
candidates.why_it_fits: Seed-like body with two fins whose curvature, base angle and loading are controllable in CAD; a blade-element model gives U and f as numbers; the original work used a Formlabs Form 2; the constraint is explicit (fixed wing mass, only curvature changes); model output for psi=15 degrees already sits in the public repository (committed 2019) while published experiments cover psi=0 and 35 only, so the prediction is frozen before any build.

public_data.what: GitHub jerabaul29/EffectFoldAngleAutorotatingSeeds: parametric FreeCAD model, blade-element model code, image-processing code, all_results_experiments.pkl (per-trial U and f for psi=0 at 4 fold angles x 7 masses x 10 repeats and psi=35 at 7 fold angles x 8 masses x 3 repeats), stored model curves for psi=0, 15, 35
arXiv full text of the methods paper (Fauli, Rabault, Carlson) and the letter (Rabault, Fauli, Carlson)
public_data.licence: arXiv non-exclusive licence (not checked per paper)

candidates.the_test: 1. Freeze: record sha256 of model/model_data_camber_psi_15.0.pkl (f24a01ae2052a2504ce1cf27c9aa3eaac2bc4571557f201618a9865749398062 in my download) and the prediction read from it: at 1.2 g differential loading, wing length scale 0.06 m, water, the minimum descent Reynolds number is 4352 at KL=1.81, i.e. U=0.0725 m/s and f=0.735 Hz (St 0.608); predicted U at KL 0.95/1.34/1.73/2.11/2.50/2.89 is 0.094/0.077/0.073/0.075/0.082/0.091 m/s. 2. Build: export six fruits at psi=15 degrees with those KL values from the FreeCAD file (plus one psi=35, KL=1.2 fruit as a positive control whose published U at the 2.16 g setting is 0.068 m/s), print on a Formlabs SLA printer, wash, cure, ballast the hollow pod with lead to the same loading. 3. Drop each 10 times in a water column at least 1.2 m tall and 25 cm wide, film at 30 Hz or faster, extract U and f. 4. Pass if the measured optimum KL lies in 1.5-2.1 (between the psi=35 optimum near 1.2-1.3 and the psi=0 optimum near 2.0-2.3) and every U is within 15% of prediction; the control must reproduce the published value within 10% first. Model-vs-experiment error at psi=35 in the fetched data is 3-11% (model low), which sets that tolerance.
candidates.biggest_risk: The stored prediction assumes the paper's exact chord (15 mm), pitch (15 degrees), camber term (2.5 degrees) and loading; a different resin density or wall thickness shifts the differential mass, so the control fruit must match first. Also unresolved: which lead-mass key in the data corresponds to the model's 1.2 g loading at psi=0 (at the 2.16 g key the psi=0 experiment gives Re about 6070 against a model value near 4730, a 28% gap, while psi=35 agrees to 3-11%). The model code is Python 2.7 and needs porting if predictions must be regenerated. Autorotation is a sink-rate test, not a forward glide.
candidates.cost_and_time: About 2-3 weeks: 1 print batch of 3 fruits took about 5 hours in the paper, so 7 fruits is 3 batches; a clear tube or tank, lead shot, a phone camera. Material cost is small (unverified background: under 100 USD of standard resin).

candidates.name: Ballasted plate glider: fin (lifting-surface) position versus flight mode and glide ratio
candidates.system: Thin rigid plate (or a printed fusiform body carrying one flat fin pair that can be clipped at different stations) with the centre of mass set by a nose ballast; released in water (resin plate) or air (paper/Mylar). Intermediate Reynolds number 10^2-10^5.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Flight mode (flutter/tumble, steady glide, dive), glide angle or glide ratio, glide speed and sink rate from side-view video.
candidates.why_it_fits: This is the closest match to a fin/body constraint: where the weight sits relative to the lifting surface decides whether the body glides at all, and the quasi-steady model returns glide ratio and speed for each position. Stable gliding at low mass is reported only for the centre of equilibrium between about 0.1 and 0.3 chord from the middle, with a dive beyond 0.3; maximum glide ratio 3.8 near 0.22. The same model with coefficients fitted to the Javan cucumber seed is public, giving the biological bridge to a real gliding seed.

GitHub ckessler2/Plate_Model_Site: Python implementation of the Li et al. plate ODE with Javan-cucumber-seed-fitted coefficients (also deployed as a web app)

candidates.the_test: 1. Freeze the table I computed from the published coefficients (script: D:/Users/ashenoy00000/delphi-work/agents/scratch/scout-glide/glide_eq.py): for centre-of-equilibrium offset e = 0.10, 0.15, 0.22, 0.28, 0.32 chord the model gives glide ratio 1.00, 3.54, 3.77, 2.94 and no glide (dive); glide angles 45.0, 15.8, 14.9, 18.8 degrees. For a 40 x 160 x 1.0 mm resin plate in water at an assumed density of 1150 kg/m3 the predicted speeds are 0.047, 0.058, 0.064, 0.089 m/s. 2. Print five plates with a leading-edge slot for a steel or tungsten rod sized to hit each e (weigh, then balance on a knife edge under water to measure e). 3. Release each 10 times from rest at about 15 degrees nose-down in a tank at least 0.6 m deep and 1.5 m long; film from the side. 4. Pass if the mode sequence is correct (unsteady or steep at 0.10, glide at 0.15-0.28, dive at 0.32) and the measured glide ratio at 0.22 is within 20% of 3.8. 5. Fish version: mount the same fin plate at three stations on a printed fusiform body so that only fin position changes e, and repeat.
candidates.biggest_risk: The model is two-dimensional; a finite-span fin loses lift, so absolute glide ratio will fall below the prediction unless span/chord is large (Li et al. used span/chord of 8 in water per the fetched table: 20.3 cm by 2.54 cm). No raw public data to check our rig against. The public Python port writes one drag term as sin(alpha^2) where the papers have sin^2(alpha) and its inertia normalisation should be audited before any dynamic (stability) claim is frozen. With the seed-fitted coefficients my calculation finds three equilibrium attack angles for one ballast position; which one is reached depends on launch, and I did not compute stability.
candidates.cost_and_time: 2-4 weeks; five small plates, ballast rod, aquarium or pool lane, phone camera.

candidates.name: 3D-printed maple samara: descent speed versus wing loading
candidates.system: Single-winged autorotating samara replicas (Norway maple and silver maple planforms) dropped in still air.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Steady descent speed (m/s) and rotation rate (rad/s).
candidates.why_it_fits: Published replica already exists with print files; the descent-factor relation v_d = sqrt((W/S)/(0.5 rho DF)) with DF about 3 makes a number from mass and area alone; artificial and natural seeds had matching centre of mass (27.7% vs 28.5% of length).

public_data.what: Figshare design files: NorwayMaple.ipt, SilverMaple.ipt, NorwayMaple.stl (163 MB, not downloaded), two gcode files
public_data.size: NorwayMaple.ipt 4.5 MB downloaded; whole record about 220 MB

public_data.what: arXiv 2010.12553 full text with Table 1 (mass, length, centre of mass, wing loading, rotation, lab and field descent speed)
public_data.licence: arXiv licence; journal version is open access

candidates.the_test: Freeze DF=3.0 from the paper. Print the Norway maple replica at three seed-pod thicknesses to give three wing loadings (for example 3.2, 4.8, 6.4 N/m2); predicted descent speeds are 1.32, 1.62, 1.87 m/s (my calculation: sqrt((W/S)/(0.6125*3.0))). Drop each 30 times from 3 m or more, measure by video. Pass if the slope of v_d against sqrt(W/S) is within 15% of prediction.
candidates.biggest_risk: The paper printed 0.05 mm wings by filament deposition in PLA; resin printers may not hold a wing that thin, so the replica will be heavier and may not autorotate. Drop-to-drop scatter is large even for identical prints (artificial Norway: 1.28 +/- 0.17 m/s). The descent factor is an empirical coefficient, not a first-principles model.
candidates.cost_and_time: 1-2 weeks; cheapest of all, but weakest model.

candidates.name: Flying-fish body with spread pectoral and pelvic fins: equilibrium glide angle from a measured polar
candidates.system: Printed flying-fish body (darkedged-wing flying fish geometry) with pectoral fins, with and without pelvic fins; ballasted free glide in water at matched Reynolds number, or tow-tank / wind-tunnel force measurement.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Lift and drag coefficients against attack angle; lift-to-drag ratio; equilibrium glide angle; pitch stability with pelvic fins spread or folded.
candidates.why_it_fits: Directly reuses the flying-fish evaluation (track 6) and has explicit fin-configuration contrasts: pelvic fins raise lift-to-drag and static pitch stability; pelvic fin station and pitch trade efficiency against stability at Reynolds 30,000 in a modular robotic model.

public_data.what: Digitised lift and drag coefficients (13 attack angles, -15 to 45 degrees) from the flying-fish wind-tunnel study, in TheSochaLab/Global-dynamics-of-non-equilibrium-gliding-in-animals (Data/Park2010)
public_data.licence: MIT (repository); the numbers are a third-party digitisation of a published figure
public_data.size: two CSV files of about 0.5 KB each fetched; whole repository about 41 MB (not downloaded)

candidates.the_test: Freeze from the digitised polar: maximum lift-to-drag 3.85 at -5 degrees body attack angle, i.e. a best equilibrium glide angle of 14.6 degrees; lift-to-drag 3.24 at 0 degrees and 2.27 at 10 degrees. Print a 1:1 or scaled body with rigid fins, ballast to near-neutral trim in water so Reynolds number matches the tunnel value, launch at fixed speed from a rail, and measure the glide angle in the steady segment; then fold the pelvic fins and predict only the sign (shallower with pelvic fins spread). Pass if the best measured glide angle is 14.6 +/- 3 degrees.
candidates.biggest_risk: I could not read the original paper, so the tunnel Reynolds number, which fish model the digitised file ('L2') refers to, and the fins-folded polar are all unverified. Trimming a free model to a chosen attack angle is hard; a force balance in a tunnel or tow tank turns this into months. Fin geometry must be reconstructed from figures.
candidates.cost_and_time: 6-10 weeks without a tunnel; longer with one.

candidates.name: Flying-snake body cross-section as a bluff lifting profile
candidates.system: Straight extruded rod with the flattened, roughly triangular cross-section of the paradise tree snake, towed or held in a water channel.
candidates.phenotype_measured: Lift and drag coefficients against attack angle and Reynolds number; presence of the lift peak at 35 degrees.

Trivial to print as an extrusion.

Full text of the flying-fish wind-tunnel paper (publisher returned HTTP 403): its Reynolds number, model dimensions, fin aspect ratios and the fins-folded polars are not verified here. The digitised polar I used is a third-party file whose label 'L2' I could not map to a specific model configuration.

The original Javan cucumber seed flight paper (1987) and the 2023 Edinburgh thesis that the seed-fitted coefficients come from: DOI resolves for the former, neither was read; no glide ratio for the real seed is given here from a primary source.

Raw trajectory or force data for the Li et al. 2022 plates, and any arXiv version of that paper: none found. The Alsomitra motion-capture repository contains plotting scripts and figures but not the CSV recordings.
CAD or data for the modular robotic flying-fish model (2022) and a public flying-fish body mesh with fins: none found on GitHub, Zenodo, Figshare or Dryad.
Numbers from the two gliding-frog physical-model papers and from the comparative flying-lizard paper: abstracts carry no values and full texts were not fetched.
Wind-tunnel studies of gliding squid: one Crossref query, no relevant hit.

Formlabs resin densities, minimum wall thickness and prices: not fetched; the 1150 kg/m3 used in the plate example and all cost figures are unverified background and must be replaced from the datasheet before freezing.

Stability (as opposed to equilibrium) predictions for the plate glider: I computed equilibria only. The public Python port differs from the published drag formula in one term and should be audited before use.
Whether a base angle of 15 degrees has been tested experimentally elsewhere: I checked only the two papers and the repository, not the later citing literature.
BioStudies/IDR and bioRxiv were not searched (imaging archives are unlikely to hold glide data; bioRxiv tool has no keyword search). One GitHub query was rate-limited (HTTP 403).

design.label: design-glide
design.chosen: Scout candidate 1, kept but redesigned: the 3D-printed double-winged whirling fruit (Fauli, Rabault and Carlson, doi:10.1103/physreve.100.013108 and doi:10.1103/physrevlett.122.024501, both resolved on Crossref in this run). The test is no longer 'does the stored psi=15 curve match within 15%'. It is a two-axis discrimination between two constraint laws: the published blade-element model (BEM) and a parameter-free disk-loading rule (U proportional to 1/swept radius, the autorotation analogue of the registry law vmin_le). Base angle psi changes swept radius; wing pitch does not. The two laws disagree in opposite directions on the two axes, so at least one must fail. I did not override to candidate 2 (ballasted plate glider) because it has no public raw data, a two-dimensional model, an unaudited port and no computed stability; it stays the follow-on in the same tank. Stated limit: this is a sink-rate surrogate, not a forward glide, so glide_range_le does not apply.
design.one_paragraph: I ported the published blade-element model to Python 3 (scratch/design-glide/bem.py) and it reproduces all five stored model files in the MIT repository to within 0.17% in Reynolds number (check_port.py; psi=15 file sha256 f24a01ae...8062, minimum Re 4352 at KL 1.805). Reading the public per-trial data against the model gave three things the scout did not have. (1) The model's ratio of descent speeds between base angles is insensitive to every fitted parameter (psi=15 optimum over psi=35 optimum = 1.114 to 1.118 across camber 0-5 deg, drag divisor 1.5-3, pitch 12-18 deg, chord +/-10%; predict.py), so it is a clean structural prediction. (2) On the public data that ratio already fails between the two published base angles: psi=0, KL 2.31 over psi=35, KL 1.2 is 1.50 measured (0.1011/0.0676 m/s, 2.16 g lead key, file all_results_experiments.pkl) or 1.40 (other psi=0 series, dict_all_results.pkl), against 1.22 from the BEM and 1.39 from the disk rule; BEM RMS log error is 0.048 inside the psi=35 series but 0.227 for psi=0 (freeze.py). (3) Inside one base angle the BEM beats the disk rule (0.048 vs 0.149 at psi=35), and the BEM predicts a large pitch effect (pitch 5 deg descends at 0.64 of the pitch 15 deg speed) where the disk rule predicts none. So the build is 21 fruits on a Formlabs SLA printer: psi=35 controls, psi=0 replication, six fold angles at the untested psi=15, three at psi=55 (extrapolation beyond the published range), and pitch 5 and 25 deg variants. Every prediction is a ratio to our own control fruit at measured immersed weight, which removes the unresolved meaning of the paper's '1.2 g' loading. Not verified: whether psi=15 or pitch variants were tested elsewhere (I listed 26 and 53 citing papers via Semantic Scholar and read four abstracts; none varies base angle or pitch on printed fruits, but the 2024 origami-fruit paper doi:10.1007/s11071-024-09618-4 has no public abstract and was not read); the Formlabs cured-resin density (not in the data sheets the materials agent read); the letter's supplement with per-species fold angles (not fetched).
design.model: MODEL A, blade-element model (BEM), doi:10.1103/physreve.100.013108 / arXiv:1811.12221, code github.com/jerabaul29/EffectFoldAngleAutorotatingSeeds (MIT), ported in scratch/design-glide/bem.py (sha256 f4d3088c...c8dd). Geometry per wing: straight root 15 mm at base angle psi from vertical with 2.5 mm radial offset, then a circular arc of length L = 60 mm and radius L/KL (KL = fold angle, rad); chord c = 15 mm; wing pitch theta_p = 15 deg; 100 + 100 elements. For an element dl at radius R with inclination phi to horizontal: U_N = U cos(phi); U_T = 2 pi f R; beta = atan2(U_N, U_T); alpha = beta - theta_p + delta (delta = 2.5 deg camber offset); q = 0.5 rho (U_N^2 + U_T^2) c dl; dL = q C_L(alpha); dD = q C_D(alpha); dF_fwd = dL sin(beta) - dD cos(beta); dF_vert = (dL cos(beta) + dD sin(beta)) cos(phi). Steady descent: M = 2 sum(dF_fwd R) = 0 and 2 sum(dF_vert) = m_net g. C_L = 0.225 + 1.58 sin(2.13 alpha - 7.2 deg); C_D = (1.92 - 1.55 cos(2.04 alpha - 9.82 deg))/2. Consequence (exact in the model, because the coefficients do not depend on Re): M = 0 fixes St = f L/U for a geometry independent of weight, and U = U_ref sqrt(m_net/m_ref). Public data agree: U^2 is linear in lead mass with R^2 0.992-0.997 in 10 of 11 series and St is flat (train_data.py). Solver: the original intersects contour lines on a 25 x 25 grid; the port brackets M(St) = 0 and uses brentq, then U in closed form. MODEL B, disk-loading rule (rival, mine): U = k sqrt(m_net g / (rho pi Rmax^2)), Rmax = largest element radius from the same geometry code; k cancels in ratios. It is the registry law vmin_le (Scaling.lean, v >= sqrt(2W/(rho S C_max))) with S replaced by swept disk area. MODEL C, linear interpolation in psi of the public minima (empirical rival, no physics). PARAMETERS. Not fitted to this system: the C_L and C_D forms (robotic insect-wing hovering experiments, doi:10.1242/jeb.00739, resolved on Crossref; the repository comment cites its formulas 12-13). Fitted by the original authors on their own psi=0 and psi=35 tank data: the drag divisor 2 (paper text: 'we reduce the value of the drag coefficient to obtain good agreement with our experiments'), the effective loading 1.2 g, and delta = 2.5 deg (set, not measured). Fitted by us: ONE scalar, the normalised speed u* = U/sqrt(m_net g) of our own psi=35, KL=1.2 control fruits; every prediction is a ratio to it. SEEN (training, not blind): all psi=0 and psi=35 public data. HELD OUT: every psi=15 fruit, every psi=55 fruit, both pitch variants, and the absolute coefficient C_eff = 2 m_net g/(rho U^2 pi Rmax^2) of the control at directly weighed immersed mass. Frozen table: scratch/design-glide/frozen_predictions.json (sha256 a7c7bcaf...3f91).

frozen_predictions.statement: With the true immersed weight, the BEM as published predicts the control fruit (psi=35, KL=1.2, pitch 15) has effective disk coefficient C_eff = 2 m_net g/(rho U^2 pi Rmax^2) = 0.43. My rival reading of the public data says about 0.87, i.e. the paper's 1.2 g is an effective number and the BEM's vertical force is low by about 2x.
frozen_predictions.number: BEM 0.433 = 2*0.0012*9.81/(1000*0.0654^2*0.01271); rival 0.875 from net mass 2.59 g = (2.16+0.68)*(1-1/11.34) and public U = 0.0676 m/s (freeze.py; 0.68 g is the mean U^2-vs-lead intercept of the psi=35 series; lead density 11.34 is unverified background)
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: BEM-absolute is refuted if measured C_eff > 0.60 or < 0.30. My rival reading is refuted if C_eff < 0.60. Void if two control fruits differ by more than 8% in u*.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Three control fruits; immersed weight by hanging each from a 0.01 g balance in water; 10 drops each; U from side video.

frozen_predictions.statement: At equal immersed weight, the best psi=15 fruit descends faster than the control by the factor R15 = u*(psi=15, KL=1.73)/u*(psi=35, KL=1.2). BEM: 1.111 (1.114-1.118 at the optima under all nuisance settings). Disk rule: 1.183. Linear interpolation of public minima: 1.23-1.29. Replication arm: R0 = u*(psi=0, KL=2.31)/control; BEM 1.220, disk 1.391, public data 1.40-1.50.
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: BEM is refuted on base angle if the 95% interval of R15 excludes 1.111, or if R0 >= 1.31. The disk rule is refuted if the interval of R15 excludes 1.183 or R0 < 1.31. Inconclusive (not a pass) if the R15 interval half-width exceeds 0.06.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Three psi=15, KL=1.73 fruits, two psi=0, KL=2.31 fruits, three controls; 10 drops each; interval from fruit-level means.

frozen_predictions.statement: At psi=15 the descent speed is minimised near KL = 1.77 and rises on both sides: u* ratios to control at KL 0.95/1.34/1.73/2.11/2.50/2.89 are 1.440/1.185/1.111/1.146/1.259/1.396 (BEM). Strouhal number at KL 1.73 is 0.62.
frozen_predictions.number: KL_opt 1.77; curve above; St 0.616 (0.54-0.70 under nuisance settings)
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: Refuted if the minimum of a quadratic fit in KL lies outside 1.45-2.10; or if u*(KL 0.95)/u*(KL 1.73) < 1.10 or u*(KL 2.89)/u*(KL 1.73) < 1.10 (BEM says 1.30 and 1.26); or if the RMS log error of the six ratios, each taken relative to the psi=15, KL=1.73 fruit so that the G2 offset is removed, exceeds 0.10; or if St at KL 1.73 is outside 0.50-0.74. The 0.10 threshold sits between the BEM's public-data error inside a base angle (0.048) and across base angles (0.227).
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Six psi=15 fruits, 10 drops each; U and rotation frequency f (FFT of wing-tip position) from 30 Hz or faster video.

frozen_predictions.statement: At psi=15, KL=1.73, lowering wing pitch from 15 to 5 deg cuts descent speed to 0.64 of its value; raising it to 25 deg increases it 1.50-fold. The disk rule predicts 1.00 for both. If true, the published and wild-inspired pitch of 15 deg is not the slow-descent optimum and the pitch-5 fruit beats the published best geometry.
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: BEM is refuted on pitch if U(5)/U(15) > 0.80, or the pitch-5 fruit fails to reach steady autorotation in more than 2 of 10 drops, or U(25)/U(15) < 1.25. The disk rule is refuted if either ratio differs from 1 by more than 0.12.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Two pitch-5 fruits and one pitch-25 fruit (CAD spreadsheet cell wing_angle), against the three psi=15, KL=1.73 fruits.

frozen_predictions.statement: Outside the published range (0-35 deg), at psi=55, both laws agree: the best fruit (KL 0.95) descends at 0.90 (BEM) or 0.89 (disk) of the control speed, and the optimum fold angle has moved down to about 0.86-0.92.
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: Both laws are refuted if R55 >= 0.97 (no gain beyond psi=35) or < 0.80, or if the psi=55 fruits do not hold a steady vertical axis (coning or tumbling) in more than 2 of 10 drops. Requires a container at least 0.40 m wide; otherwise void.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Three psi=55 fruits (swept diameter 0.143 m), 10 drops each, wide tank or pool.

frozen_predictions.statement: If slow descent shapes these fruits, fold angle should fall with base angle across wild species: BEM optimum KL_opt = 2.08 - 0.0213*psi(deg); maximum-swept-radius rule gives 2.34, 1.96, 1.44, 0.92 at psi = 0, 15, 35, 55 (slope -0.026 per deg). The letter reports wild KL = 1.8 +/- 0.18 for 27 fruits without relating it to base angle.
frozen_predictions.number: Regression slope of KL on psi between -0.015 and -0.030 rad per deg
frozen_predictions.refuted_if: Refuted if the slope's 95% interval excludes all negative values, given at least 10 species spanning at least 15 deg of base angle. If the species do not span 15 deg the bridge is untestable from this sample and is reported as such.
frozen_predictions.data_or_measurement: Per-fruit KL from the letter's Supplemental Material (not fetched in this run), with psi measured from the same or herbarium images by someone who has not seen the KL values. No printing needed.

steps: 0. PREREGISTER (commit 0, before any CAD export or data module): commit prereg/glide/PREREG.md with the model equations, bem.py and its sha256, frozen_predictions.json and its sha256, the five upstream .pkl hashes, the thresholds above, the drop count (10), exclusion rules (drop excluded only if the fruit touches a wall or has not reached constant speed in the measurement window, decided by a rule in code), and the void conditions.

1. VALIDATE THE MECHANICAL MODEL on public data only (already done here, to be re-run in the repo): port reproduces stored outputs to 0.17%; U^2 linear in load; St constant; BEM RMS log error 0.048 (psi=35) and 0.227 (psi=0); disk rule 0.149 and 0.133.

2. Commit 1: the video-analysis module (pod tracking for U, wing-tip FFT for f), tested on synthetic video and on the position traces stored in all_results_experiments.pkl (keys 'y pos seed', 'y pos wings'), before any of our own footage exists.

3. Optional commit 2, before the first drop: a blade-element-momentum variant (BEM plus induced inflow) with its own frozen table, so that if both A and B fail there is a third pre-stated candidate rather than a post-hoc fix.

4. BUILD: export 15 geometries from the FreeCAD file by changing three spreadsheet cells (wing_long_angle_low = psi, wing_long_circular_radius_curvature = 60 mm/KL, wing_angle = pitch); print 21 fruits in 7 batches; wash, cure, light sanding; label with random codes held by a second person.
5. BALLAST AND WEIGH: add shot to each hollow pod until immersed weight is 2.60 +/- 0.05 g (matches my inferred public loading, keeps Re about 4000-10000); record immersed weight to 0.01 g.

6. GATES (control fruits only, before unblinding anything else): (a) three controls agree within 8% in u*; (b) one control at three loads gives d log U / d log m_net in 0.42-0.58; (c) control in the narrow and the wide container differs by less than 5%; (d) u*(psi=35, KL=0.6)/u*(control) within 1.31 +/- 0.10, the public value. If a gate fails, fix the rig; the predictions stay as committed.
7. DROPS: 21 fruits x 10 drops, randomised order, fully immersed release, 30 Hz or faster side video, water temperature logged (viscosity).
8. ANALYSE with the committed code, unblind, score G1-G5 exactly as written; publish all per-drop numbers including excluded drops.
9. BIOLOGICAL BRIDGE REVIEW (G6) in parallel by a separate person: wild-fruit fold angle against base angle; and check whether wild pitch is nearer 5 or 15 deg, which G4 makes a pointed question.

10. LEAN: state the homogeneity lemma (forces of degree 2 in (U, fR) imply St independent of weight and U proportional to sqrt(W)) and a disk_rules_out lemma in the pattern of vmin_rules_out; emit an elimination certificate for each geometry whose committed u* ratio the winning law excludes. Written in a scratch copy; nothing in upstream is touched by this design.
design.what_is_frozen_and_when: Commit 0 (before CAD export, before the analysis module, before any print): model equations; bem.py (sha256 f4d3088cc7d0516d69968bb085b44b18d4155624bec4a0f7a6a3485d5eb9c8dd); frozen_predictions.json (sha256 a7c7bcaf3269111d0e5662258a4d77eef93f284431756353c001cc5a09ff3f91) with BEM and disk-rule ratios for all 15 geometries; upstream file hashes (model_data_camber_psi_15.0.pkl f24a01ae2052a2504ce1cf27c9aa3eaac2bc4571557f201618a9865749398062; psi_0.0 ca104417...c16a; psi_35.0 ca4ac77b...6c7d); thresholds, void conditions, drop count, exclusion rule, the list of 21 fruits. Commit 1 (before any footage): analysis code. Commit 2 (before first drop, optional): third-model table. After commit 0 the only number allowed to be set from our own data is the control normalisation u*(psi=35, KL=1.2). The paper's psi=15 curve is itself older than this project (repository files dated 2019-07-22 in the downloaded archive; script effect_psi.py lists psi = 0, 15, 35), which I cite as provenance, not as our freeze.
design.what_would_make_this_a_paper: PAPER: (a) a split verdict, which the public data make likely: the BEM fails on base angle (R15 interval excludes 1.111, R0 >= 1.31) while the disk rule fails on pitch (G4 ratios far from 1). That shows neither a section-level nor a disk-level law is a sufficient design constraint for autorotating bodies and says exactly which term each lacks; with G1 it also shows the published agreement depended on an effective loading. (b) The pitch-5 fruit descending at least 20% slower than the best published geometry: a new shape, predicted before printing, that beats the literature optimum, plus the pointed biological question of why wild fruits would not use it. (c) G5 failing by instability at psi=55: a stability boundary neither law contains, i.e. a new constraint to formalise. (d) G6 refuted: wild fold angle does not track base angle, which weakens the published claim that wild fruits sit at the aerodynamic optimum. MERELY CONFIRMATORY: R15 inside the BEM interval, optimum at 1.45-2.10, St in window, pitch trend right. That is a clean replication with one new base angle and would be a methods note or a figure in the larger paper, not a finding.
risks: Sink rate, not glide. Autorotation has no forward travel, so the track's glide laws (glide_range_le, static trim) are untested here. The plate-glider follow-on (doi:10.1017/jfm.2022.89, doi:10.1017/jfm.2025.10275, both resolved on Crossref) is needed for a true fin-position glide claim.

Resolution at psi=15. BEM and disk rule differ by only 6.5% in R15 (1.111 vs 1.183). Per-drop scatter in the public data is 0.3-7.5% (CV, train_data.py) and the two public psi=0 series differ by 6-13% at the same nominal geometry (for example 0.1137 vs 0.1027 m/s at KL 1.71; their loads may differ slightly, 2.16 g key vs a stated 20 mN), so fruit-to-fruit variation may swamp it; hence three replicate fruits and the explicit inconclusive rule. The pitch axis (36% effect) and the psi=0 arm (14% apart) carry the discrimination if R15 is inconclusive.

Wall effects bias the key ratio in the direction of the known discrepancy: wide-psi fruits fill more of the tank (control swept diameter 0.127 m; the original tank was 0.25 m) and blockage slows them. Gate 6c and a container at least 0.40 m wide, or a pool with an underwater camera, address this.

The meaning of the paper's 1.2 g loading and of the data's mass keys is inferred, not documented. My reading (keys are lead mass in air; intercept 0.53-0.85 g is the resin's own net weight; resin volume 3.4 cm3 from the CAD cells implies density about 1.18) is self-consistent but unconfirmed; G1 is built to settle it. Asking the authors is a cheap alternative.

Print fidelity: wings are 1 mm thick, 15 mm chord, 75 mm long. Warping on cure changes KL, pitch and camber. Measure each printed fruit's KL and pitch from a photo against a protractor grid and exclude by a pre-stated tolerance (KL within 0.08, pitch within 2 deg). Cured-resin density and water uptake over a session should be measured, not assumed (the materials agent found 0.0-0.9% 24 h mass gain for most SLA resins, no density for the standard resins).

CAD: the file is FreeCAD 0.16/0.17 and the README warns newer versions may break it. I read the spreadsheet cells from the archive XML but did not open or regenerate the model. Fallback: rebuild the wing from the three numbers in a current CAD tool; geometry is fully specified by the model code.

Pitch-5 fruit may not self-start. The BEM shows a second, unstable root appearing at pitch 0 and below, not at 5 deg, but spin-up distance is not modelled and the tank is finite. A stall at 17-21 deg mid-span angle of attack (my BEM calculation) is physically plausible and would falsify G4; that is the intended risk.

Novelty not fully checked: one possibly relevant citing paper (origami winged fruits, 2024) could not be read. Prior work on samara blade-element-momentum models exists (doi:10.3390/aerospace10050414, abstract read) and should be the starting point for the optional third model.
Lead handling: use steel or tungsten shot instead; immersed weight is measured directly so the ballast material does not matter.
first_week: Day 1: copy scratch/design-glide/{bem.py, frozen_predictions.json, check_port.py, train_data.py, predict.py, disk.py, freeze.py} into a prereg folder of the project repo (by whoever owns that folder), write PREREG.md from this file, commit 0. Email the original authors one question: what do the mass keys and the 1.2 g loading denote.

Day 1-2: open the FreeCAD file in 0.17 (or rebuild), export the control (psi=35, KL=1.2) and the psi=15, KL=1.73 fruit as STL; check wing thickness and hole size against the chosen resin's minimum features; start batch 1 (three controls).
Day 2-3: write and commit the tracking module; run it on the public position traces and reproduce the stored 'u mean' and 'f mean' for five trials to within 2%.
Day 3: source the water column (clear tube or tank at least 0.40 m wide and 1.2 m tall, or book a pool lane), a 0.01 g balance with a hook, shot, a phone on a tripod, a backlight and a scale bar.
Day 4: ballast and weigh the three controls; run gates 6a-6d and G1. This alone answers whether the published absolute calibration holds.
Day 4-5: print batches 2-4 (psi=15 series, psi=0 pair) while the gates run; decide and commit the optional third model before any non-control fruit is dropped.
Day 5: start G6 data collection (supplement of the letter, herbarium images) with a person blind to the predictions.
design.compute_needed: Laptop only. The BEM solves one geometry in well under a second and the full prediction table in a few seconds (run in this session on the Windows box with numpy 2.5.4 and scipy 1.18.1 from an existing venv). Video tracking of about 210 clips with OpenCV is minutes on CPU. No Modal credits and no GPU cluster are needed. Optional, only if the split verdict appears and a mechanism is wanted: rotating-frame CFD of three geometries at Re about 5000, which would be a cluster CPU job of order tens of core-hours each (my estimate, not costed).
design.physical_build: 21 fruits on a Formlabs SLA printer in one rigid standard resin (Clear or Grey; the original used a Form 2, about 5 h per batch of 3, so about 7 batches and 35 h of printing). Geometry: hollow spherical pod (10 mm outer radius, 1 mm wall, two 1.5 mm filling holes), two wings 1 mm thick, 15 mm chord, 15 mm straight root plus 60 mm arc (values read from the CAD spreadsheet). Set: psi=35 at KL 1.20 (x3, control) and 0.60; psi=0 at KL 2.31 (x2) and 1.71; psi=15 at KL 0.95, 1.34, 1.73 (x3), 2.11, 2.50, 2.89; psi=55 at KL 0.60, 0.95, 1.34; psi=15, KL 1.73 at pitch 5 deg (x2) and 25 deg. Rig: water column at least 1.2 m tall and 0.40 m wide (or a pool), 0.01 g balance with under-hook, steel or tungsten shot, thermometer, phone camera at 30 Hz or faster, backlight, scale bar. Time: about 2-3 weeks including the gates.

laws.lawset_version: 1.6.0 (lean/registry/lawsets/current.json -> lawset-1.6.0.json, created 2026-11-01T04:37:40Z) in upstream leanbio at commit cb92aaf (2026-11-12, equal to origin HEAD by git ls-remote in this run). The lawset file pins 53 laws (36 accepted, 5 candidate, 7 proposed, 3 contested, 2 retired; my count from the file); README.md says 'Law set 1.6.0: 64 laws ... 16 candidate' and lean/registry/laws/ holds 64 files, so 11 law files are not pinned by the lawset. NOTE: the local Delphi application copy (delphisci/lean/registry/lawsets/current.json) is at 1.8.1 and is AHEAD of upstream for flight constraints.

existing.status: accepted (v1.0.0, physical, class theorem; constraints C15, C16)
existing.statement_plain: A steady glide with no thrust, lift equal to weight and L/D <= (L/D)max, started at height h, covers at most h*(L/D)max horizontally. Proof is an energy balance W*h = D*x + loss with loss >= 0.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header, 'What is assumed, not proved': 'steady gliding with lift equal to weight and no thrust (ground effect, updraft and taxiing thrust are outside, which is why the field glide distances exceed the bound)'. (L/D)max is an input number, not derived. Registry adds: single steady glide; wind and updrafts outside.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: The core law for a passive glide surrogate. For a printed glider released from bench height h with a measured or committed (L/D)max, any predicted or claimed range above h*(L/D)max is eliminated before the drop test. It turns the fin/body design space into one number, (L/D)max, that the experiment then has to measure.

existing.statement_plain: If flying near a surface cuts drag by a fraction delta (0 <= delta < 1) and leaves lift unchanged, the range bound becomes h*(L/D)max/(1 - delta).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: delta is an input ('Park and Choi (2010) measured delta of 0.09 to 0.14 for a flying-fish model; the number enters only as a candidate input', docstring in the file). No model of how delta depends on height over span.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Gives the surrogate two test conditions with different bounds: free-air drop (delta = 0) and low pass over a flat plate or water tray (delta > 0). A design that claims a ground-effect gain larger than 1/(1 - delta) is eliminated.

existing.statement_plain: With power balance P_avail = P_req + W*c + loss and loss >= 0, climb rate c <= (P_avail - P_req)/W. Companion: climb_nonneg_iff (0 <= climbRate iff P_req <= P_avail).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: The power balance itself is a hypothesis; losses non-negative.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: For a passive surrogate P_avail = 0, so the lemma forces c <= -P_req/W < 0: any design or simulation output that shows a sustained climb in still air is eliminated. Useful as a sanity gate on simulator outputs.

existing.statement_plain: Definition: f L = a * L^b for L > 0 with real exponent b and a > 0. Theorems: powerLaw_ratio, powerLaw_log, powerLaw_div (a quotient of power laws has exponent b1 - b2), cubeLaw_powerLaw.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'the power-law forms with their exponents' are named hypotheses; 'No number from physics/ appears in a statement.' Registry: fitted exponents are separate regressions with their own errors.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Lets the track scale a fish to a printed surrogate with measured (non-isometric) exponents instead of assuming isometry: wing loading exponent is forced to be bW - bS, so a design sheet with three inconsistent exponents is eliminated.

existing.statement_plain: If weight and lifting area follow power laws in length with exponents bW and bS, and air density and C_L,max are constant, the minimum-speed exponent is (bW - bS)/2.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Single power laws over the size range; constant rho and C_L,max across sizes (Reynolds effects ignored).
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Predicts how the minimum launch speed of the surrogate changes with scale. With the registry's E1 exponents (mass 2.981, area 1.834; lean/registry/laws/E1.json) the exponent is (2.981 - 1.834)/2 = 0.5735 (my arithmetic), against 0.5 for an isometric print. That difference is a testable prediction across two print sizes.

existing.statement_plain: If demand and supply are power laws in size and the supply exponent is smaller, there is a size above which supply is below demand.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Power-law forms; the supply exponent is 'whatever the physiology gives, not derived here'.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Not about the passive glide itself; it is the biological-bridge law. It says powered flight has a size ceiling, which is the reason the organism glides and the reason a passive surrogate is the right physical model.

existing.statement_plain: If sustained flight needs P_req = W*v/(L/D) and sustained power is aerobic, then P_req <= eta*E*Q*Ca. Related: aerobicPower, aerobic_le_Ca, aerobic_le_metabolic, sustained_le, climb_le_aerobic.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: Fick delivery Q(Ca - Cv), mechanical power at most eta times metabolic power, 0 <= Cv <= Ca, 0 <= eta <= 1, 'sustained power is aerobic (anaerobic bursts are outside)'. The registry says the glide phase, which needs no muscle power, is outside.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Out of scope for an unpowered glide (the local 1.7.0 changelog makes the checker return out-of-scope for a declared unpowered glide). Its role on this track is the 'review the biological bridge' step: it rules out the alternative reading that the fish flaps.

existing.statement_plain: Exact, no isometry: if lift (1/2)*rho*v^2*S*C_L equals weight W with 0 < C_L <= C_L,max, then v >= sqrt(2W/(rho*S*C_L,max)). Definitions used: lift, vmin.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'the same C_L,max across sizes (Reynolds effects)', steady lift-supported flight. C_L,max is an input.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: The strongest ready-made cut on the fin design space. For a surrogate of weight W and fin planform area S, any (W, S, launch speed) triple with v below vmin is eliminated. It is the lemma behind the two existing C9 certificates.

existing.statement_plain: Under the cube law, the area law and constant rho and C_L,max, vmin scales as sqrt(L). Log form: vmin_log (exponent 1/2).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: isometry of mass and areas, constant density, same C_L,max across sizes. 'Nothing here is a measured fact.'
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Fixes how launch speed must change when the surrogate is printed at a different scale; a scale model flown at the same speed as the animal is not dynamically matched.

existing.statement_plain: In an isometric family an area scales as L^2 (AreaLaw; areaLaw_ratio, areaLaw_log). With the cube law, weight per unit area scales as L (wingLoading_ratio, wingLoading_log).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: isometry is a named hypothesis and 'real animals break it: Davenport 1992 measured fin area ∝ L^1.83 and wing loading ∝ L^1.24 within one flying-fish species'.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: A geometrically scaled solid print has wing loading proportional to L. So the print scale, the wall thickness or the infill must be chosen to hit the target wing loading; a design that scales the animal up as a solid and keeps the animal's wing loading is eliminated.

existing.statement_plain: At vmin with constant L/D, power required scales as L^3*sqrt(L), exponent 7/2 (powerRequired_log). Definition: powerRequired W v LD = W*v/LD.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Constant L/D, flight at vmin, isometry.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: For a passive glide the same expression is the rate of potential-energy loss, so sink rate = v/(L/D). Indirect use only: no theorem in the library states the sink-rate form.

existing.status: accepted (v1.0.0); depends on MusclePowerLaw, registry id muscle-power-premise, status retired
existing.statement_plain: Under the cube law, area law and Thompson's muscle premise there is a size above which power required exceeds power available. Supporting: powerAvailable_ratio, powerRatio_eq.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'Thompson's muscle premise (p constant), which modern expectation puts below L^3'. The size exists; its value is not supplied.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Bridge only (why gliding, not flapping). Caution: the docstring of this theorem in the file contains holdout-category wording; do not quote it verbatim.

existing.status: accepted (v1.0.0; constraints C8, C8b, C8c, C8d, C8e)
existing.statement_plain: Axial breaking load sigma*A scales as L^2; the safety factor F_break/W = sigma*k3/(k1*L) falls as 1/L (safetyFactor_eq, safetyFactor_scaled, stress_ratio); above L_max = sigma*k3/(k1*n) the member cannot carry n body weights (cannot_carry).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'the same material (sigma)', 'axial loading', isometric sections.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Gives a maximum print scale for a given resin strength and load factor n (launch or landing loads). Axial only, so it bounds the body, not the fin spar.

existing.statement_plain: For a slender beam, sigma_b = F*l/Z. With similar sections and a load that scales as the body, bending stress scales as L and there is a size limit (bendingSafety_eq, bending_cannot_carry). With a sheet-like load (F ∝ L^2), bending stress is independent of size (bendingStress_ratio_sheet, bendingStress_log_sheet). Definitions: SectionModulusLaw, LeverLaw, bendingStress.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Registry: 'Slender linear-elastic (Euler-Bernoulli) beam; sigma_b = M_b/Z with a point load at the free end'; similar sections; 'Constant sigma_max; static loads only'; which load family applies is empirical.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: The only existing law on the fin as a structure. In a steady glide the fin carries the body weight (body-like load), so root bending stress grows with L: it bounds fin span times scale for a given printed material. It gives scaling only; it has no deflection or stiffness statement, so it cannot yet say whether a printed fin stays flat enough to keep its lift.

existing.statement_plain: At equal Froude number, speed scales as sqrt(L). Definition: froudeSpeed.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Equal Froude number is assumed, not derived.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Relevant if the surrogate test includes the water-exit or taxiing launch at model scale; fixes the model launch speed for a scaled tank test.

existing.statement_plain: If W = k*L^3 then the log-log slope between any two sizes is exactly 3. Also CubeLaw, cubeLaw_ratio, not_cubeLaw_of_exponent_ne_three.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'density constant and shape fixed are what W = k L^3 encodes'; the tolerance band [2.5, 3.5] is 'a decision rule outside this module'.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: A solid print of fixed shape and material must obey it exactly, so mass at a second scale is predicted from the first. A hollow or lattice print breaks it on purpose, and then the PowerLaw route must be used.

existing.status: accepted (v1.0.0, physical, theorem-from-hypothesis; constraint P4b; promoted in 1.5.0 by role human:project-lead)
existing.statement_plain: With horizontal airspeed u, sink rate s (u/s = L/D <= (L/D)max), height h and along-track wind w (positive = tailwind, w >= -u), ground range x = (u + w)*(h/s) cannot exceed (L/D)max*h*(1 + w/u). Supporting: glide_ground_range, glide_ground_range_le.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'Wind (pure kinematics, no source needed)'; steady glide; sign convention fixed in the file.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: A ready-made *_rules_out lemma that is present in upstream leanbio and takes exactly what a drop test measures (h, u, s, x, w). Indoor tests set w = 0; a fan or outdoor test uses w. This is the lemma the track's first certificate should instantiate.

existing.statement_plain: In the ISA troposphere density falls with height (isa_rho_anti) and vmin rises with height; vmin is proportional to 1/sqrt(rho) (vmin_inv_sqrt, vmin_density_ratio). Structure: ISATroposphere.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Barometric form rho0*(1 - beta*h/T0)^n as a named hypothesis; witness numbers rho0 1.225 kg/m^3, T0 288.15 K, beta 0.0065 K/m, n 4.2559 in Delphi.Perturb.measured (file lean/Delphi/Perturb.lean).
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Corrects vmin for the lab's air density. vmin_density_ratio is also the template for a model tested in a different fluid density.

existing.statement_plain: At fixed height a larger lifting area lowers vmin and so the power required. The module also proves vmin_mono, demand_mono, supply_anti, feasible_downward_closed, ceiling, infeasible_at_ground_infeasible_everywhere.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Header: 'Air density and oxygen partial pressure enter as a MONOTONE ATMOSPHERE, a named hypothesis with no numbers'; no animal compensation; no temperature, humidity or wind.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: demand_anti_area gives the monotone direction of the fin-area design variable (more area never raises vmin at fixed weight). The rest is about powered flight and is bridge material only.

existing.status: accepted (v1.0.0, empirical-observation; deliberately NOT a constraint)
existing.statement_plain: measuredFinRatio r means 0.406 <= r <= 0.823 (pectoral fin length over standard length, 49 flying-fish specimens, median 0.687; numbers from lean/registry/laws/E5.json). A design outside the range is below 0.406 or above 0.823.

existing.statement_plain: WithinSpeciesAllometry: fin-area exponent below 2 and wing-loading exponent above 1 within one flying-fish species (area 1.834, loading 1.236, mass 2.981; lean/registry/laws/E1.json).

existing.statement_plain: MassExponentBand: the fitted mass exponent lies in [2.90, 3.02]; for a single power law, a scaled design's weight ratio must lie between r^2.90 and r^3.02 (weight_ratio_band).

existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Bounds the target mass of a surrogate at a given length if it is meant to stand for an adult flying fish.

existing.statement_plain: Every measured flying-fish specimen with mass and lifting area in the project has wing loading between 37.025 and 46.375 N/m^2 (n = 4; numbers from the registry file).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: n = 4 specimens from one source table (Park and Choi 2010 Table 1, per the registry). A structure, not a theorem.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: The target wing-loading window for the surrogate. Candidate status means a violation is advisory only.

existing.statement_plain: Every measured flying fish has pectoral/SL of at least 0.406 and every measured non-flying beloniform at most 0.389; the groups do not overlap (n = 49 and 60; registry file).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: A record of museum measurements; says nothing about why.

existing.status: generated certificate; references Delphi.Constraints.vmin_rules_out, which is NOT defined in upstream leanbio (see flags)

existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: The direct precedent for this track: a fin/body design committed to numbers and eliminated by a flight law. My check: 2*0.5886/(1.225*0.04905*0.78) = 25.12, so vmin = 5.01 m/s > 4 m/s.

existing.statement_plain: The same design is too slow at 4 m/s in air of density 1.1133 kg/m^3 (the 1000 m value used by the generator).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Generated from lean/eliminate/tff-candidates.json; density profile is the physics thread's fit.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Shows how to re-run one elimination under a changed environment parameter.

existing.status: accepted (v1.0.0; constraint C6); certificate proved by decide +kernel
existing.statement_plain: The generated flying-fish anatomy graph (536 ontology terms, 674 part_of edges) is well-formed: edges go strictly down in level, closed, acyclic, every node reaches the body root, and no kept term is excluded from the taxon. Also aFlyingFish_check, aFlyingFish_nodup, aFlyingFish_counts, aFlyingFish_size.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Blueprint.lean header: 'That Uberon and the Cell Ontology are right, and that Ubergraph served their ... statements correctly and completely on the retrieval date'; 'Nothing about any organism: the certificate says the emitted structure is internally coherent under its own stated rules.'
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: It constrains the anatomical description, not the mechanics. Its use here is the bridge step: the fin and body parts named in the surrogate must be terms of this certified graph.

existing.status: accepted law; certificate proved by decide +kernel
existing.statement_plain: In the 12-term pectoral-fin developmental subtree, every derivative is staged strictly after its precursor and develops_from is acyclic.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header: 8 edges certified; '4 further edges have an unknown stage and are not certified'. Zebrafish anatomy terms and stages.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Bridge only: limits which developmental routes to a longer fin are admissible when the mechanical result is carried back to biology.

existing.registry_id: none (ThompsonLaws modules are not in the registry)
existing.status: proved; moved into leanbio 2026-11-12; not pinned by any lawset
existing.statement_plain: At fixed bending stiffness a hollower tube needs less wall material (gasCoreAreaFactor_strictAntiOn, gasCore_no_interior_min). With a core of relative density q in (0,1), mass is minimised at inner/outer radius ratio k* = sqrt(1 - q) (massFactor_deriv_eq_zero_iff, massFactor_lt_of_ne_optimum); with a wall-thickness floor lambda the optimum is min(k*, 1 - lambda) (constrained_optimum, gasCore_constrained_optimum).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: File header: 'These are statements about the model; whether [biological tubes] sit at these optima is left to measurement.' Local buckling enters only as a symbolic bound t/R >= lambda.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Directly usable for printed fin rays or spars: for a hollow printed ray filled with air or uncured resin it fixes the lightest wall ratio at a required stiffness, with the printer's minimum wall as lambda.

existing.statement_plain: For a thin-walled tube under a uniform distributed load on a simply supported span, the wall thickness that keeps bending stress at a fixed working value is proportional to the bending moment and is greatest at mid-span (uniformStressThickness_stress, uniformStressThickness_prop).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: No header section; the docstrings assume a thin-walled tube with section modulus pi*r^2*t and a simply supported beam. A fin is a cantilever, so the moment profile differs.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Template for a tapered fin spar (thickness follows the moment). Needs a cantilever version before it applies to a fin.

existing.registry_id: none (the registry gap elastic-similarity is still 'proposed' with no module)
existing.status: proved; not linked to the registry gap
existing.statement_plain: If diameter ∝ mass^(3/8) then cross-section area ∝ mass^(3/4) and circumference ∝ mass^(3/8). Companion: geometric_similarity_exponents (1/3 gives 2/3 and 1/3).
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Circular sections; the diameter power law is a hypothesis. The length exponent 1/4 is not used.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Partly fills the 'elastic-similarity' gap. It lets a size series of surrogates be designed with spar diameters that keep elastic rather than geometric similarity.

existing.statement_plain: A two-layer strip curves in proportion to the swelling-strain mismatch between its layers, with Timoshenko's geometric coefficient (timoshenkoCoefficient, bilayerCurvature_linear, bilayerCurvature_ofEquilibrium). Also snapParameter_mono_size, poroelasticTime_scale.
existing.assumptions_outside_kernel: Module docstring: formalises 'the mathematical core of the claims' of a plant-hygromorph claim set; linear bilayer beam theory.
existing.how_it_constrains_this_track: Not a glide law. It is the link to the biomaterials track: a two-material printed fin that changes camber with humidity or temperature would be bounded by it.

missing.law: Induced drag and the drag polar (fills registry gap aspect-ratio-induced-drag)
missing.statement_math: C_D = C_D0 + C_L^2/(pi*e*AR), with AR = b^2/S, 0 < e <= 1, C_D0 > 0. Rule-out form: a committed (C_L, C_D, AR, e_max) with C_D < C_L^2/(pi*e_max*AR) is False.
missing.why_needed: Today L/D enters every glide theorem 'only as a committed number' (registry note on aspect-ratio-induced-drag). Without the polar, fin shape cannot narrow anything: the track's design variables (fin span, fin area) never reach the range bound.
missing.difficulty: easy as a named hypothesis with algebraic consequences (field_simp, nlinarith); hard if derived from lifting-line theory, because Mathlib has no potential-flow or Biot-Savart library.
missing.source: Spedding GR, McArthur J (2010) Span efficiencies of wings at low Reynolds numbers, J Aircraft 47:120-128, doi:10.2514/1.44247 (verified=true, Crossref fetched this run). Measured polar for a flying-fish model: Park H, Choi H (2010) J Exp Biol 213:3269-3279, doi:10.1242/jeb.046052 (verified=true).

missing.law: Maximum lift-to-drag ratio from aspect ratio
missing.statement_math: For the polar above, for all C_L > 0: C_L/C_D <= (1/2)*sqrt(pi*e*AR/C_D0), with equality iff C_L = sqrt(pi*e*AR*C_D0).
missing.why_needed: This is the bridge that composes with glide_range_le: x <= (h/2)*sqrt(pi*e*AR/C_D0). It turns the range bound into a statement about fin geometry, which is the whole point of a fin constraint model.
missing.difficulty: easy: AM-GM on C_D0/C_L + C_L/(pi*e*AR); Real.sqrt lemmas and nlinarith.
missing.source: Follows from the polar; no separate paper needed. Polar source as above (doi:10.2514/1.44247, verified=true).

missing.law: Fin geometry link (fills registry gap fin-length-ratio as a geometric law, not as a cause)
missing.statement_math: With body length L, body width w, fin length l_f = r*L and mean chord c: span b = 2*r*L + w, area S = 2*r*L*c + S_body, AR = b^2/S. Then AR is strictly increasing in r at fixed c, and wing loading W/S is strictly decreasing in r at fixed W.
missing.why_needed: E5 gives the observed band for r (0.406 to 0.823, lean/registry/laws/E5.json) but nothing connects r to S, AR, vmin or L/D. Without this link the fin ratio is 'an input the model carries' (registry note) and cannot be eliminated or optimised.
missing.difficulty: easy: monotonicity of rational functions on positive reals. The modelling choice (rectangular versus tapered fin, what counts as body area) is the real work.
missing.source: Fin measurements: Daane JM et al. (2021) Curr Biol 31:5052-5061, doi:10.1016/j.cub.2021.08.054 (verified=true). Planform areas of a flying-fish model: doi:10.1242/jeb.046052 (verified=true).

missing.law: Glide-speed polar: sink rate and best-glide speed
missing.statement_math: In a steady glide at speed v: D(v) = (1/2)*rho*v^2*S*C_D0 + 2*W^2/(rho*v^2*pi*b^2*e); sink rate s(v) = v*D(v)/W; D is minimised at v* = (2W/(rho*S))^(1/2) * (pi*e*AR*C_D0)^(-1/4). Rule-out: a committed (v, s) with s < v*D_min/W is False.
missing.why_needed: A bench drop test measures speed and sink rate, not L/D directly. The existing lemmas take u/s <= (L/D)max as a hypothesis; this law would derive it from the design, so the measured (v, s) pair can eliminate designs.
missing.difficulty: moderate: minimisation of a*v^2 + b/v^2 needs fourth roots (Real.rpow) and care with positivity; no new theory.
missing.source: Socha JJ, Jafari F, Munk Y, Byrnes G (2015) How animals glide: from trajectory to morphology, Can J Zool 93:901-924, doi:10.1139/cjz-2014-0013 (verified=true).

missing.law: Launch energy: range from height plus initial speed
missing.statement_math: With launch speed v0 and landing speed v1 >= 0 at height drop h: W*h + (W/(2g))*(v0^2 - v1^2) = D_mean*x + loss, loss >= 0, so x <= (h + v0^2/(2g))*(L/D)max.
missing.why_needed: glide_range_le assumes all energy comes from height. A catapult-launched surrogate, like a fish leaving the water at speed, carries kinetic energy; the header itself says field glide distances exceed the bound. Without this term a correct surrogate flight looks like a violation.
missing.difficulty: easy: same proof shape as glide_range_le with one more non-negative term.
missing.source: Davenport J (1994) How and why do flying fish fly? Rev Fish Biol Fish 4:184-214, doi:10.1007/BF00044128 (verified=true). Non-steady glide framing: Yeaton IJ, Socha JJ, Ross SD (2017) Bioinspir Biomim 12:026013, doi:10.1088/1748-3190/aa60e2 (verified=true).

missing.law: Longitudinal static stability and trim
missing.statement_math: With pitching-moment coefficient C_m(alpha) = C_m0 + C_m_alpha*alpha about the centre of mass: a trimmed, statically stable glide needs C_m0 > 0 and C_m_alpha < 0, where C_m_alpha = -C_L_alpha*(x_np - x_cg)/c. So x_cg must lie ahead of the neutral point x_np = (S_1*a_1*x_1 + S_2*a_2*x_2)/(S_1*a_1 + S_2*a_2) for a two-surface (pectoral plus pelvic) layout. Rule-out: x_cg >= x_np is False for a design that claims a stable passive glide.
missing.why_needed: A passive surrogate has no control, so an unstable design tumbles and never reaches the steady glide every existing theorem assumes. This is the law most likely to eliminate printed designs, and it constrains body mass distribution and the pectoral/pelvic fin placement together. Nothing in the library mentions moments or centre of mass.
missing.difficulty: moderate: the algebra is linear, but a new structure (surfaces with positions and lift slopes) and a clear definition of 'stable' are needed; proving dynamic stability from it would be hard.
missing.source: Davenport J (1992) Wing-loading, stability and morphometric relationships in flying fish (Exocoetidae) from the north-eastern Atlantic, J Mar Biol Assoc UK 72:25-39, doi:10.1017/S0025315400048761 (verified=true). Glider-shaped seed: Azuma A, Okuno Y (1987) J Theor Biol 129:263-274, doi:10.1016/S0022-5193(87)80001-2 (verified=true). Gliding frog: McCay MG (2001) J Exp Biol 204:2817-2826, doi:10.1242/jeb.204.16.2817 (verified=true).

missing.law: Non-equilibrium glide dynamics (existence and approach to the steady glide)
missing.statement_math: v' = -g*sin(gamma) - (rho*S/(2m))*C_D(alpha)*v^2 ; v*gamma' = -g*cos(gamma) + (rho*S/(2m))*C_L(alpha)*v^2. Claim to prove: for fixed alpha with C_L, C_D > 0 there is a unique equilibrium with tan(gamma*) = -C_D/C_L and v*^2 = 2*m*g/(rho*S*sqrt(C_L^2 + C_D^2)), and a bound on the height lost before the trajectory is within epsilon of it.
missing.why_needed: A bench drop of 1 to 2 m may be shorter than the transient. If the surrogate never reaches equilibrium, comparing its range with h*(L/D)max tests the wrong thing. This law tells the experiment how much height it needs.
missing.difficulty: hard: the equilibrium algebra is easy, but a kernel-checked convergence or transient bound needs ODE stability arguments (Lyapunov function, Gronwall) that Mathlib supports only at a basic level.
missing.source: Yeaton IJ, Socha JJ, Ross SD (2017) Global dynamics of non-equilibrium gliding in animals, Bioinspir Biomim 12:026013, doi:10.1088/1748-3190/aa60e2 (verified=true).

missing.law: Reynolds-number dependence of C_L,max and C_D0
missing.statement_math: Re = rho*v*c/mu. Named hypothesis: C_L,max = f(Re) nondecreasing and C_D0 = g(Re) nonincreasing on the test range, with a critical band Re_c below which C_L,max drops sharply. Consequence: vmin(L) is no longer ∝ sqrt(L); for two scales with Re_1 < Re_2, vmin_1/vmin_2 >= sqrt((W_1/S_1)/(W_2/S_2)).
missing.why_needed: Every scaling theorem assumes 'the same C_L,max across sizes (Reynolds effects)' (Scaling.lean header). A small printed surrogate flies at lower Re than the animal, exactly where that assumption fails. Without it, a model-to-animal transfer is unbounded.
missing.difficulty: moderate: easy as a monotone named hypothesis (same pattern as Altitude.Atmosphere); the numbers for f and g are empirical and must be measured or sourced per fin section.
missing.source: Lissaman PBS (1983) Low-Reynolds-number airfoils, Annu Rev Fluid Mech 15:223-239, doi:10.1146/annurev.fl.15.010183.001255 (verified=true).

missing.law: Dynamic similarity of surrogate and organism
missing.statement_math: A steady glide is fixed by the dimensionless groups (AR, shape, C_L, Re, relative density m/(rho*S*c), static margin). Theorem to state: if two gliders share shape, AR, static margin and the polar, then glide angle is equal and v_1/v_2 = sqrt((W_1/S_1)/(W_2/S_2)*(rho_2/rho_1)).
missing.why_needed: This is the formal licence for 'surrogate': it says which measured quantities transfer to the animal and which do not. Without it the physical comparison is an analogy, and a reviewer of the biological bridge has nothing to check.
missing.difficulty: moderate: the specific glide statement is algebra over existing vmin and lift definitions; a general Buckingham-pi theorem would be hard and is not needed.
missing.source: Buckingham E (1914) On physically similar systems, Phys Rev 4:345-376, doi:10.1103/PhysRev.4.345 (verified=true).

missing.law: Fin stiffness: cantilever deflection under lift
missing.statement_math: For a fin of semi-span l carrying half the weight as a uniform load q = W/(2*l) on a cantilever of flexural rigidity E*I: tip deflection delta = q*l^4/(8*E*I) = W*l^3/(16*E*I); root stress sigma = W*l/(4*Z). Constraints: delta/l <= d_max and sigma <= sigma_y/n. Rule-out: a committed (W, l, E, I) with W*l^2/(16*E*I) > d_max is False.
missing.why_needed: The existing bending law gives only how stress scales with size. It has no modulus and no deflection, so it cannot say whether a fin printed in a given resin stays flat. This is where the material enters the design space, and it is what would connect this track to the biomaterials track.
missing.difficulty: easy if the beam formula is taken as a named hypothesis (algebra only); moderate to hard if the deflection is derived from the Euler-Bernoulli equation, since Mathlib has no beam theory and the fourth-order boundary-value problem must be solved explicitly.
missing.source: Fin-ray bending mechanics: Alben S, Madden PG, Lauder GV (2007) The mechanics of active fin-shape control in ray-finned fishes, J R Soc Interface 4:243-256, doi:10.1098/rsif.2006.0181 (verified=true). The cantilever formula itself is unverified background (standard beam theory; no DOI fetched).

missing.law: Elastic similarity in the registry (gap elastic-similarity)
missing.statement_math: d ∝ l^(3/2), equivalently d ∝ M^(3/8) and l ∝ M^(1/4); then bending stress and relative deflection under self-weight are size-independent.
missing.why_needed: The exponent consequences are already proved in lean/ThompsonLaws/LimbBoneSimilarity.lean (elastic_similarity_exponents) but the registry gap has no module, and the link to bendingStress in Scaling.lean (replace SectionModulusLaw k*L^3 by the elastic family) is missing. Needed to design a size series of surrogates whose fins deflect alike.
missing.difficulty: easy: reuse PowerLaw and bendingStress; rpow algebra.
missing.source: McMahon T (1973) Size and shape in biology, Science 179:1201-1204, doi:10.1126/science.179.4079.1201 (verified=true).

missing.law: Ground-effect drag reduction as a function of height over span
missing.statement_math: delta = phi(h/b) with phi nonincreasing in h/b, phi -> 0 as h/b -> infinity, 0 <= phi < 1; composed with glide_range_le_groundEffect.
missing.why_needed: Today delta is a free input. A function of h/b makes the low-pass test predictive, and it ties the benefit to fin span, which is a design variable.
missing.difficulty: moderate: easy as a monotone hypothesis; an explicit phi from image-vortex theory would be hard for the same reason as lifting-line theory.
missing.source: Park H, Choi H (2010) J Exp Biol 213:3269-3279, doi:10.1242/jeb.046052 (verified=true); the 0.09 to 0.14 range is quoted from the docstring in lean/Delphi/Flight.lean, not re-read from the paper in this run.

missing.law: Taxiing thrust (registry gap taxiing-thrust)
missing.statement_math: Not written here: needs a tail-beat thrust model T(f, A, U). Out of scope for a passive surrogate.
missing.why_needed: Listed for completeness. The registry says field glide distances require it beyond one unpowered glide, so the biological-bridge review must state that the surrogate tests the unpowered segment only.

laws.elimination_pattern: A certificate is two layers. Layer one is a hand-written lemma in lean/Delphi/Constraints.lean (or beside its law, as with Delphi.Perturb.wind_glide_rules_out) that takes the law's hypotheses plus the candidate's commitment and concludes False, with the last hypothesis a decidable fact about numbers; the Constraints.lean header says 'Every lemma concludes `False` from the law **plus** the candidate's commitment' and that a candidate which does not commit to the assumptions gets 'cannot rule', never 'passes'. Layer two is a GENERATED file in lean/Delphi/Certificates/ (header: 'GENERATED by lean/eliminate/eliminate.mjs from <candidates>.json ... Do not edit; regenerate'), with one theorem per elimination named elim_<candidate id>_<constraint id>, which instantiates the lemma with the candidate's numbers written as exact rationals and discharges the arithmetic by norm_num (or decide +kernel for finite data). Real example, lean/Delphi/Certificates/EliminationsFlier.lean lines 18-20: `/-- Candidate `flier-F1-too-slow`, constraint C9. -/ theorem elim_flier_F1_too_slow_C9 : ∀ C : ℝ, 0 < C → C ≤ (39 / 50 : ℝ) → Delphi.lift (49 / 40 : ℝ) (4 : ℝ) (981 / 20000 : ℝ) C = (2943 / 5000 : ℝ) → False := fun C hC hCm hlift => Delphi.Constraints.vmin_rules_out (by norm_num) (by norm_num) hC hCm (by norm_num) hlift (by norm_num)`. It reads: at air density 1.225, speed 4 m/s, area 0.04905 m^2 and any lift coefficient up to 0.78, lift cannot equal a weight of 0.5886 N (my check: vmin = sqrt(2*0.5886/(1.225*0.04905*0.78)) = 5.01 m/s).
