specialists.topic: Hygromorphic and 4D-printed self-shaping materials: state of the art and its numbers (spec-hygromorph-4d)
specialists.summary:
Passive humidity-driven bilayers are well characterised in wood and in filament-printed (FFF) cellulose composites, and no vat-photopolymer (SLA/DLP) or SLS hygromorph turned up in this search. Nor did any hygromorph whose design space was narrowed by a machine-checked law. Both gaps rest on a limited search (Europe PMC plus a handful of web queries), so treat them as probable, not proven.

Measured numbers, all from fetched full texts: wood bilayers 4.2-8 mm thick reach 1.5-8.7 m^-1 in 24 h (Rueggeberg & Burgert 2015); 15-45 mm mass-timber bilayers need ~400 h or more (Groenquist 2019); sub-millimetre FFF cellulose bilayers reach 15.5 m^-1 within 30 min and survive 170 cycles plus 13 months outdoors (Cheng 2024); pine cone scales keep 97% of blocking force after 102 wet/dry cycles (Ulrich 2024).

Timoshenko's 1925 formula works for stiff, linear wood bilayers (errors under 5% to 13%; under 10% near the optimum thickness ratio) and fails for soft or printed ones: it over-predicts PEDOT:PSS/PDMS films by 3.8-4.4x (Dingler 2021), and FFF Laywood/PLA curvatures could only be fitted with a modulus ratio of 150-690 against ~40 measured (Krueger 2021). Reported causes are humidity-dependent modulus, non-linearity, print-path width effects and large rotations.

One result is my own derivation rather than a literature finding: Timoshenko's factor is bounded, kappa*h/d_eps <= 3/2 with equality at n = 1/m^2. It is a simple inequality that could be machine-checked and used as a hard design-space bound.

Not retrieved: numbers from Gladman 2016, Erb 2013, Correa 2015, Le Duigou 2016, Holstov 2015, Reichert 2015, Wood 2018, Vailati 2018, and the original Dawson 1997 and Timoshenko 1925 texts. Their DOIs resolve but the texts were paywalled or blocked.

findings.claim: Pine cone scale as a bilayer (Reyssat & Mahadevan 2009): thickness ratio passive/active m ~ 1, modulus ratio n ~ 5, cell hygroscopic expansion alpha = 0.001 +/- 0.0001 per %RH, active tissue strain up to 20%; predicted curvature change ~1.3 cm^-1 for h ~ 1 mm over a 100 %RH swing, giving ~75 deg; a Pinus coulteri scale rotates up to ~100 deg.
findings.value: m~1; n~5; alpha=1e-3 /%RH; d_kappa~1.3 cm^-1 at h~1 mm; predicted 75 deg vs observed up to 100 deg

findings.claim: Reyssat & Mahadevan measured pine cone tissue response times that do NOT follow the diffusive h^2 law: drying tau = 96*h^1.5 min and wetting tau = 29*h^1.3 min (h in mm); the simple diffusive estimate h^2/D with D ~ 1e-9 m^2/s gives ~1000 s at 1 mm.
findings.value: tau_dry=96 h^1.5 min; tau_wet=29 h^1.3 min; h^2/D~1000 s at 1 mm

findings.claim: Reyssat & Mahadevan paper/polymer bilayer: paper (active) 100 um, polymer (passive) 200 um, total 0.3 mm, strips ~5 cm x 5 mm, alpha ~ 4e-4 per %RH, stiffness ratio n ~ 0.4; expected curvature change ~0.19 mm^-1, called 'comparable' to observation. No error metric is given.
findings.value: h_a=100 um; h_p=200 um; alpha=4e-4 /%RH; kappa~0.19 mm^-1; no quantified error

findings.claim: Own check of the Reyssat paper bilayer with Timoshenko's factor: m=2, n=0.4 gives f = 6(1+m)^2/[3(1+m)^2+(1+mn)(m^2+1/(mn))] = 54/36.45 = 1.48; kappa = alpha*dRH*f/h = 4e-4*dRH*1.48/0.3 mm, so 0.19 mm^-1 needs dRH ~ 96 %RH, consistent with a near-full humidity swing.

Pine cone tissue moduli (Pinus wallichiana, Eger et al. 2022): sclereid layer 35 MPa at 50% RH falling to 25 MPa at 60% RH; brown tissue 52 MPa (43 MPa above 70% RH); sclerenchyma fibre strands 800 MPa at 30% RH falling to 200 MPa at 75% RH.
findings.value: E_sclereid=35->25 MPa; E_fibre=800->200 MPa; E_brown=52 MPa

findings.claim: Pine cone scale geometry and strain (Eger et al. 2022): sclereid layer ~1000 um at its thickest, sclerenchyma fibre strands ~500 um; wet sclereid layer is 27% thicker and 22% longer in the bending zone than dry; fibre strands 3% thinner and ~1% longer; P. sylvestris scale angular change dry-to-wet 24 deg; 12 deg between 30% and 80% RH.
findings.value: t_sclereid~1.0 mm; t_fibre~0.5 mm; +22% length wet; 24 deg (water); 12 deg (30-80% RH)

findings.claim: Pine cone scales (Pinus jeffreyi) cycled 102 times by submerging and drying kept 97% of blocking force and torque and over 94% of opening angle, despite cracking and delamination (Ulrich et al. 2024, abstract).

Dawson et al. 1997 pine cone hygroscopic expansion coefficients, as quoted by Cecchini et al. 2023: sclereids (active) 0.20 +/- 0.04 and fibres (passive) 0.06 +/- 0.02. Units as quoted are ambiguous; the original Nature text was not retrieved in this run.

Pelargonium appendiculatum awn (Cecchini et al. 2023): cap layer 39.8 +/- 6.9 um thick, E_cap = 0.78 +/- 0.29 GPa, E_ridge = 1.48 +/- 0.25 GPa (nanoindentation, 50% RH, 25 C); natural seed torque 20.7 +/- 2.5 uN m and extensional force 5.1 +/- 1.1 mN.
findings.value: E=0.78/1.48 GPa; torque 20.7 uN m; force 5.1 mN

findings.claim: Beech/spruce wood bilayers (Rueggeberg & Burgert 2015): 120 x 20 mm strips, 4 mm beech active layer, spruce passive layer 0.2-4 mm (m = 0.05-1). Step from 85% to 35% RH (wood moisture ~18% to ~10%) gave curvature up to 8.7e-3 mm^-1 for spruce <= 1 mm and 1.5e-3 mm^-1 for 4 mm spruce after 24 h; 8.7e-3 mm^-1 over 120 mm = 59 deg computed vs 55 deg measured.
findings.value: kappa up to 8.7e-3 mm^-1 (8.7 m^-1); 1.5e-3 mm^-1 at m=1; 24 h to equilibrium

findings.claim: Rueggeberg & Burgert material parameters: differential swelling (shrinking) coefficient beech 3.2 +/- 0.1 e-3 per % moisture content, spruce 0.7 +/- 1.0 e-4 per %; literature moduli used: spruce longitudinal 10-15 GPa, beech tangential 0.5-0.8 GPa (stiffness ratio n = 10-30); curvature optimum at thickness ratio m = 0.2-0.3.

Rueggeberg & Burgert report Timoshenko agreement: step-change specific curvature 'matches' theory; under cyclic humidity the 0.2 mm and 0.8 mm spruce bilayers ran 11% and 13% above the calculated value, the other two within 5%.

Own Timoshenko check of Rueggeberg & Burgert: m = 0.8/4 = 0.2, n = 20, f = 8.64/5.77 = 1.50; d_eps = (3.2e-3 - 0.07e-3)*8 %MC = 0.0250; kappa = 0.0250*1.50/4.8 mm = 7.8e-3 mm^-1, about 10% under the reported 'up to 8.7e-3 mm^-1' (inputs 'around 18% to around 10%' are approximate).
findings.value: 7.8e-3 mm^-1 predicted vs up to 8.7e-3 measured

findings.claim: Rueggeberg & Burgert cyclic and durability data: 85%<->35% RH cycles of 24, 12, 6 h gave curvature amplitudes 4.1 +/- 0.4, 2.9 +/- 0.2, 2.0 +/- 0.05 e-3 mm^-1 (0.2 mm spruce); curvature phase lag 1.6 h falling to 0.6 h; outdoor weathering Aug 2013-Apr 2014 kept specific curvature at 3-4e-4 mm^-1 per %RH, dropping to 2-3e-4; 100 g and 150 g tip loads (1-1.5 N) reduce curvature by less than 3% (calculated) but cause creep offset.
findings.value: amplitudes 4.1/2.9/2.0e-3 mm^-1; ~9 months outdoors; <3% loss under 1-1.5 N

findings.claim: Thin beech bilayers (Groenquist et al. 2018): 120 x 20 mm; curvature after 48 h at 35% RH (moisture 17.5% to 9.5%) was ~4.5 m^-1 at thickness fraction r = h1/(h1+h2) = 0.17 and ~1.5 m^-1 at r = 0.49. A 2D anisotropic extension of Timoshenko predicts within 10% at r = 0.34 (R^2 0.986/0.992), slightly under-predicts at r = 0.12-0.17 and over-predicts at r = 0.43-0.49; mean R^2 0.972 (plane strain) and 0.950 (plane stress). Model optimum r = 0.253; 2 mm bilayers computed at 10-25 m^-1.

Large-scale self-shaping wood (Groenquist et al. 2019): beech and spruce bilayers 15, 30 and 45 mm thick at passive:active = 1:2; moisture change 7.5% (beech, to 14.5%) and ~9% (spruce, to 12.5%); equilibrium after ~400 h for 15-30 mm, not reached after 900 h at 45 mm; peak stresses ~30 MPa (beech) and 25 MPa (spruce) compressive at the passive-layer interface; no plastic strain. FE and the analytical Timoshenko-type model both predict beech fairly and overestimate spruce.

Groenquist et al. 2019 sensitivity result: for beech all shape variability traces to the active layer's swelling coefficient; adhesive thickness, stiffness and shear modulus do not influence shape; thicker bilayers curve less only through the higher second moment of area, with stress magnitudes independent of thickness at fixed thickness ratio.

Urbach Tower (ICD/ITKE Stuttgart with Empa/ETH): 14 m tower of 12 spruce components built from 5 m x 1.2 m bilayer panels made flat at 22% wood moisture and kiln-dried to 12%. Press-level sources; the curvature radius was not retrieved.
findings.value: 5 m x 1.2 m panels; 22% -> 12% MC; 14 m tall

findings.claim: livMatS shading (Cheng et al. 2024, FFF): cellulose-filled polyketone (35/65 mass) active layer + ASA restrictive layer; 75 x 20 mm specimens; mean curvature 0.0155 mm^-1 at 80% RH at all temperatures (radius 1/0.0155 = 64.5 mm, own arithmetic); at low RH ~0 at 30 C but 0.011 mm^-1 at 10 C.
findings.value: kappa=0.0155 mm^-1 at 80% RH; R=64.5 mm

findings.claim: Cheng et al. 2024 durability and speed: 170 actuation cycles between 30% and 90% RH with slight curvature loss only in the first ten; UV exposure (60 C, 96 h) changed curvature by <0.001 mm^-1 at 90% RH and reduced it by 0.002-0.006 mm^-1 at 30% RH; full transformation between 30% and 90% RH within 30 min; 424 modules outdoors June 2022-July 2023 over 10-91% RH with no noticeable loss.

Tahouni et al. 2023 FFF filaments: active layer two 0.26 mm layers; matrix polyketone 1500 MPa and TPU; printed moduli TPU 34.7 MPa rising to 68.07 MPa with 30% cellulose, PK+30% cellulose 1345 MPa with 2.15% elongation at break; full transformation over 35-90% RH; maximum curvature with one restrictive and two or three active layers.

Krueger et al. 2021 (FFF Laywood/PLA, Stuttgart): Laywood modulus 6.3-9.7 MPa wet, 38-62 MPa humid (80% RH), 99-110 MPa dry (30% RH); PLA 1785-2467 MPa; measured modulus ratio ~40. Fitting Timoshenko to measured curvature required n = 150-690 and swelling strain 0.034-0.051. The authors state the experimental values 'could not be reproduced computationally' and that the unmodified formula predicts the wrong trend when the passive layer's effective width varies.

Krapez Tomec et al. 2021 (FFF wood-PLA/PLA): 200 x 12 x 1.8 mm bilayers of six 0.3 mm layers; PLA longitudinal swelling 0.09% between 20% and 80% RH; theory placed maximum deflection at PLA thickness 0.82-0.84 mm, measured maximum fell at 0.6 and 0.9 mm (0.5 < m < 1.0).
findings.value: t_total=1.8 mm; optimum t_PLA 0.82-0.84 mm predicted, 0.6-0.9 mm observed

findings.claim: Humidity-driven printed seed robot (Cecchini et al. 2023, extrusion plus coaxial electrospun PEO/CNC fibres): torque 30.4 +/- 5.1 uN m, extensional force 2.4 +/- 0.6 mN, lifts ~100 times its own weight.
Li et al. 2019 bio-hygromorph: FFF wood-flour PLA scaffold passive layer 0.8 mm with fish swim bladder hydrogel active layer 3.0 mm.

MIT Self-Assembly Lab (Raviv et al. 2014) used material-jetting (Stratasys Connex inkjet, UV-cured), not vat photopolymerisation: rigid polymer 2 GPa (Poisson 0.4) plus a hydrophilic UV-curable acrylate that swells to up to 200% of original volume in water, modulus 40 MPa dry and 5 MPa swollen; disk primitive grows from 0.813 mm to 1.245 mm; resolution ~85 um XY, ~30 um Z. Stimulus is water immersion, not air humidity.
findings.value: E_rigid=2 GPa; E_active=40->5 MPa; swelling up to 200% volume

findings.claim: Polymer thin-film bilayer (Dingler et al. 2021): 6 um PEDOT:PSS on 11 um or 48 um PDMS reached 1.2 mm^-1 and 0.42 mm^-1 at 90% RH. Timoshenko fed with independently measured strain (6.1%) and humidity-dependent moduli (PEDOT:PSS 605 MPa at 1% RH, 68 MPa at 90% RH) predicts 5.3 mm^-1 and 1.6 mm^-1.
findings.value: measured 1.2 and 0.42 mm^-1; predicted 5.3 and 1.6 mm^-1

findings.claim: Own arithmetic on Dingler et al.: Timoshenko over-predicts by 5.3/1.2 = 4.4x (17 um) and 1.6/0.42 = 3.8x (54 um). I reproduced the 5.3 mm^-1: m=0.48, n=6.8, f = 13.14/8.86 = 1.483; kappa = 0.061/0.017 mm * 1.483 = 5.32 mm^-1. The authors attribute the gap to the linear small-rotation assumption; using a dry-state modulus instead shifts the prediction from 5.3 to 3.2 mm^-1.

Paper/CMC bilayer (Seelinger et al. 2024): finite-element prediction deviates ~15% from experiment at 10 wt% CMC and worsens above 20 wt% because the hygroscopic expansion coefficient becomes moisture-dependent; after cycling between 10% and 90% RH the strip misses its start position by 5-6 mm.

Sinn et al. 2022 flag that swapping thermal for moisture expansion in Timoshenko's formula is exact only for the strain difference; their estimated error from this is about 1% of total strain difference, and the formula cannot distinguish bilayers joined with different adhesives.

Synthesis: Timoshenko's 1925 formula predicts equilibrium curvature of stiff, thin, linear-elastic wood bilayers to roughly 5-13% when swelling coefficients and moduli are measured on the same material (Rueggeberg 2015; Groenquist 2018), but fails by factors of ~4 in curvature (Dingler 2021) or ~4-17 in the fitted modulus ratio (Krueger 2021, 150-690 fitted vs ~40 measured; own ratio) for soft, printed or large-rotation systems. Stated causes: humidity-dependent modulus, non-linear material behaviour, unequal effective layer widths from print-path spacing, large rotations, moisture gradients before equilibrium.

Own derivation, a candidate formal law: Timoshenko's factor f(m,n) = 6(1+m)^2/[3(1+m)^2 + (1+mn)(m^2 + 1/(mn))]. Expanding (1+mn)(m^2+1/(mn)) = m^2 + 1 + m^3 n + 1/(mn) >= m^2 + 1 + 2m = (1+m)^2 by AM-GM, with equality at n = 1/m^2. Hence kappa*h/d_eps <= 3/2 for every thickness and modulus ratio. Dingler et al.'s stated global maximum 5.4 mm^-1 equals 1.5*0.061/0.017 mm = 5.38 mm^-1, consistent.

Response time versus thickness across fetched sources: ~30 min for sub-millimetre FFF bilayers (Cheng 2024), ~24 h for 4.2-8 mm wood bilayers (Rueggeberg 2015), ~400 h for 15-30 mm and over 900 h for 45 mm (Groenquist 2019). Materials and end-point criteria differ, so no single exponent is claimed; Poppinga et al. 2018 name the poroelastic time scale as the common limit and metre-scale actuation in minutes as unsolved.

Gap: no humidity-driven (air RH) bilayer hygromorph made by vat photopolymerisation (SLA/DLP) was found. Nearest precedents are DLP parts actuated by liquid immersion: desolvation-induced self-folding of grayscale-cured sheets (Zhao et al. 2017) and hydrophilic/hydrophobic photopolymer bilayers that bend in water (Zhao et al. 2018). Searches: Europe PMC title and abstract queries combining DLP/stereolithography/vat photopolymerisation with humidity/hygroscopic/moisture (zero relevant hits) and three web searches. Absence of evidence from a limited search.

Gap: no SLS / powder-bed hygromorph was found. SLS '4D' work located is magnetically driven (Wu et al. 2021 grippers). SLS nylon-12 is reported to swell measurably with ambient humidity, treated as a dimensional-tolerance defect rather than used for actuation (conference study, no DOI retrieved).

Gap: no hygromorph or bilayer actuator whose design space was narrowed by a machine-checked (proof-assistant) law was found. A Europe PMC query pairing hygromorph/bilayer terms with formal verification, proof assistant, Lean, Coq, Isabelle returned no relevant paper, and one web search returned only conventional analytical mechanics papers.

findings.claim: A web-search summary attributed an SLA-printed humidity bilayer to Cremonini et al. 2023; the fetched abstract says direct ink writing, and the response is to liquid water, light and heat. It is not a vat-photopolymer hygromorph.

Hygroscopic liquid-crystal-elastomer actuators responsive to ambient humidity have been printed, but by UV-assisted direct ink writing with an acid surface activation step (Kim et al. 2021), not in a vat.

recommendations: Treat a vat-photopolymer humidity-driven bilayer as plausibly novel but run a patent and Scopus/Web of Science check before claiming it; the nearest prior art is DLP bilayers that bend on water immersion (Zhao 2017, 2018) and PolyJet swelling parts (Raviv 2014).

Before printing, measure for each candidate resin the linear hygroscopic strain and the modulus as functions of RH. Every Timoshenko failure found here traces to using dry-state or single-point material data.

Use kappa <= 1.5*d_eps/h as the first machine-checkable law: it needs only real-number algebra (AM-GM) and immediately rules out target curvatures a resin pair cannot reach. Report Timoshenko as an upper estimate, not a prediction, for soft or large-rotation designs.
Design near the optimum n = 1/m^2 where the bound is attained, and keep the active layer thin: fetched data run from 30 min below 1 mm to 24 h near 5 mm and ~400 h at 15-30 mm.

Benchmark the proof of concept against Cheng 2024 (15.5 m^-1 at 80% RH, 30 min, 170 cycles) and Rueggeberg & Burgert 2015 (8.7 m^-1, 24 h), and report cycles survived and a blocking force or moment, which most printed-hygromorph papers omit.
Have a second agent or a library login pull the paywalled numbers (Gladman 2016, Correa 2015, Le Duigou 2016, Holstov 2015) before the paper cites them quantitatively.
could_not_find: Any SLA/DLP (vat photopolymer) bilayer actuated by ambient relative humidity; only liquid-immersion DLP precedents were found.
Any SLS / powder-bed hygromorphic actuator; only a magnetic SLS gripper and reports of unwanted humidity swelling in SLS nylon-12.
Any hygromorph or bilayer design constrained by a proof-assistant-verified law.
Measured numbers from Gladman et al. 2016 (swelling strains, moduli, curvature): paywalled; only the abstract was read.

Measured numbers from Correa et al. 2015 (MIT DSpace returned HTTP 429), Le Duigou et al. 2016 (HAL blocked the fetch), Holstov et al. 2015 (repository 403), Reichert et al. 2015, Wood et al. 2018, Vailati et al. 2018, Erb et al. 2013.
Original Dawson et al. 1997 values for pine cone layer moduli; expansion coefficients are quoted second-hand and their units are ambiguous.
Timoshenko's 1925 text itself; the formula was taken as reproduced in three fetched open-access papers, which agree with each other.
A directly measured blocking force or blocking moment for an engineered wood or FFF bilayer; forces found are for pine cone scales (retention percentages only) and seed awns (mN, uN m).
Cycle counts beyond 170 for any printed hygromorph, and any failure-cycle (fatigue limit) figure.
Wheat awn and chiral seed pod numbers: only abstracts were read, which carry none.
The Urbach Tower panel curvature radius and lamella thickness.
A single agreed exponent for response time versus thickness; Reyssat & Mahadevan measured 1.3-1.5 for pine cone tissue, below the diffusive value of 2.

specialists.topic: Patents and prior art around law-constrained, printed stimulus-responsive architectural materials (preliminary scan, not legal advice)
specialists.summary: PRELIMINARY SCAN, NOT LEGAL ADVICE, NOT A FREEDOM-TO-OPERATE OR PATENTABILITY OPINION. Run 2026-11-12 with keyword searches on Google Patents (one batch of 18 queries before the service returned HTTP 503 for the rest of the run) and USPTO Patent Public Search (36 queries, US grants and published applications only, claims read for 22 documents). No Espacenet, WIPO, CNIPA or classification-code (CPC) search was possible, so non-US families are listed from Google Patents result rows only and their claims were not read. No patent in the user's repo or name was looked for or found: 'license your patent' presumes a filing that this scan cannot confirm exists. What looks crowded: (1) stimulus-responsive printed objects in general - MIT/Stratasys hold a granted method patent (US 11155025 B2, 2013 priority) on multi-material printing with differential swelling arranged into joints giving a predicted shape transformation, and the 2015 parent application claimed any additively manufactured object that transforms predictably under a non-biasing stimulus; (2) hydrogel-composite 4D printing with anisotropic fillers (Harvard applications 2015-2019); (3) hygromorphic material compositions and coated/printed bilayers (MIT 9931829, NTU 12655582, CMU 12575478, US Air Force 10457780, CityU application); (4) wood-bilayer self-shaping building parts and shading (ETH Zurich WO2018033422, Empa DE112019001411, University of Stuttgart EP4019251) - backed by a deep academic record from 2009-2024 that is itself prior art against any broad claim to a humidity-driven printed bilayer or a hygromorphic facade flap. The bilayer curvature mechanics have been public since 1925. What looks open in this scan: zero US documents had 'theorem prover' or 'proof assistant' in the claims together with material/geometry/mechanical and design terms; zero had formal-verification terms in claims about a design/model/build file with a certificate; zero combined biological/morphological/scaling-law constraints with a design space and additive manufacturing in the claims. The nearest formal-methods patents are in software and systems architecture (Microsoft US 8473895, theorem-prover-driven design-space exploration of architectures), chips, and cyber-physical monitors (CMU application). Kinds of thing that could plausibly be novel here, in descending order of how open the scan found them: (a) a design-and-verification METHOD - generating candidate geometries/material layouts, checking each against machine-checked biological and physical laws in a proof assistant, and releasing only candidates with a proof certificate to a printer; (b) a certified design FILE FORMAT / data structure binding geometry, material assignment and a machine-checkable proof (the '.life' idea) - open in the scan but software/data-structure claims face subject-matter eligibility hurdles, especially in the US, and need a concrete technical effect; (c) a specific GEOMETRY that the law-constrained search finds and that shows a measured, unexpected response - patentable only as the specific structure, not the bilayer principle; (d) a MATERIAL COMPOSITION - least promising if the proof of concept uses stock commercial resins, since the vendor's formulations are not ours and hygromorphic compositions are already heavily claimed. Any public dashboard, repo, preprint or paper already disclosing the method counts as prior art against a later filing in most jurisdictions (the US has a one-year grace period for the inventor's own disclosure; most others do not) - unverified background, to be confirmed with counsel before the paper is posted.

Harvard and MIT filed a US application on a printed lattice whose ribs are bilayers of filaments with different thermal expansion and/or modulus so that the lattice adopts a predetermined 3D geometry under a stimulus. Found as an application only; grant status not determined.

Full-text co-occurrence of theorem prover / proof assistant with additive manufacturing or 3D printing is nearly absent in US documents: 3 hits, none about material design (a robotics executive network, a vaccine method, a conversational AI system). findings.claim: The closest formal-methods patent found is Microsoft's: a computer-implemented method that symbolically executes a design specification into a quantifier-free logical formula and interacts with a theorem prover module to find distinct solutions (architectures) within a design space. It concerns system/software architectures, not physical materials, but it shows 'theorem prover + design space exploration' as a generic concept was claimed with a 2010 filing.

Other formal-methods neighbours are in cyber-physical systems and engineering architecture generation, not materials: a CMU application on synthesizing a runtime monitor from a proven hybrid model of a cyber-physical system, and a Siemens patent on a modeling language for generating engineering design architectures.

At least one 2026 individual-inventor US application family in the metamaterial area mentions proof assistants in its specification (stating the invention is not limited to any proof assistant or verification environment) while claiming a fabrication process, not a verification method. This shows proof-assistant language is starting to appear in materials filings.

Computational design-method claims for shape-morphing structures exist but are specific: Toyota holds a granted patent on designing and additively manufacturing an inflatable shape-morphing structure via finite-element topology optimization converted to a Turing-pattern texture. A claims-field query for stimulus-driven shape change + simulation/optimization/inverse design + 3D printing + target shape returned zero US documents.

No US document was found claiming vat-photopolymerization / stereolithography / DLP printing combined with shape change or shape memory, a water/humidity/swelling trigger and a bilayer/gradient/grayscale architecture. The resin-printer route to a hygromorphic part therefore looked uncrowded by keyword, but a separate query showed Toyota/Georgia Tech hold a 2023-priority patent on grayscale DLP printed shape-morphing (US 12768208 B2), whose claims were not read.

findings.claim: The physics of the bilayer is long-public: the curvature of a two-layer strip under differential expansion was derived in 1925, applied to pine-cone-like hygromorphs in 2009, demonstrated in 3D-printed wood composites in 2015, in hydrogel 4D printing in 2016, at building scale in wood in 2018-2019, and as 4D-printed cellulose weather-responsive shading on a real facade in 2024. Any claim reading on a humidity-driven printed bilayer flap as such would meet this literature.
findings.source_url_or_path: https://api.crossref.org/works (each DOI resolved in this run; saved scratch/spec-ip-landscape/crossref.json)

findings.claim: Inverse design of shape-shifting bilayers (computing the growth pattern for a target shape) is published academic prior art (2017) and was reduced to practice in printed lattices (2019), so 'compute the print pattern that yields a target shape' is not new as a concept.

Using the Lean theorem prover to formalize physical-science derivations is published (chemical physics, 2024; high-energy physics, 2024 preprint), and a 2026 preprint applies Lean 4 with machine-checkable certificates to patent analysis itself. None of the three describes constraining a printable material or geometry design space. So 'formalize science in Lean' is not new; applying machine-checked laws as a gate on fabricable designs was not found.

Formlabs' own US filings returned by a keyword query for shape memory / swelling / shape change / hygroscopic / 4D were about mixing, casting molds, support structures and dentures, not stimulus-responsive printed parts. Only the first 14 of 37 family-expanded results were inspected.

Coverage limits of this scan: Google Patents answered 18 queries then returned HTTP 503 for 22 further queries and all single-patent pages; Espacenet, WIPO Patentscope, Justia and uspto.report returned 403. The remaining 36 queries ran on USPTO Patent Public Search, which covers US grants and published applications only. No CPC-class search, no citation chaining, no legal-status or assignment check, no non-English full text.
findings.value: 18 Google Patents queries answered, 22 refused; 13+15+8=36 USPTO queries; 22 US documents with claims read

recommendations: Treat this as a first-pass keyword scan only. Before anyone tells an investor there is something to license, establish whether any patent application has actually been filed by the team; this scan found none and did not look inside the team's own records.

Before the paper, dashboard or repo discloses the law-constrained design pipeline publicly, ask a patent attorney whether to file a provisional. Public disclosure is prior art against later filings in most jurisdictions (unverified background on grace periods: confirm with counsel). Check what is already public on the live dashboard and in the repo history.

Frame the candidate invention as a design-and-verification method (machine-checked biological/physical law set as a gate on generated geometries, with a proof certificate released to the printer) rather than as a humidity bilayer. The bilayer principle, hygromorphic compositions and 4D printing as such are crowded; the method and a certified design file were the only areas with zero keyword hits.

If a certified file format ('.life') is pursued, tie claims to a concrete technical effect (for example, a printer or slicer that refuses to build without a valid proof, or a measured property guaranteed by the certified constraint), since bare data structures and abstract verification steps face eligibility objections. This is a question for counsel.

Commission a professional search before relying on the open-space finding: CPC classes B33Y, B29C64, E04F10 / E06B9 (shading), G06F30 (computer-aided design) and G06N5 (knowledge-based reasoning), plus Espacenet and CNIPA full text. Chinese 4D-printing filings were visible in results but not analysed.

Read the claims of the three building-scale wood-bilayer families (ETH WO2018033422, Empa DE112019001411, Stuttgart EP4019251) and of MIT/Stratasys US 11155025 before the proof-of-concept is described commercially; these are the families a printed hygromorphic architectural element is most likely to sit next to.

Do not plan on a material-composition claim if the demonstration uses unmodified commercial resins. A specific geometry found by the constrained search, with a measured unexpected response, is the more defensible physical claim.
Keep a dated record of which Lean laws constrained which design and what the measured print did; whichever route is taken, that record is the evidence of conception and of the technical effect.

specialists.topic: Levin lab: xenobots, bioelectricity, and an optogenetic, hands-off variant (label spec-levin-bioelectric)
specialists.summary: Three generations of Xenopus biobot are measurable from fetched sources: gen-1 cardiomyocyte-driven designs evolved in a voxel soft-body simulator (Kriegman 2020, PNAS), gen-2 cilia-driven spheroids of 3026 +/- 180 cells at 487-602 um diameter moving at >100 um/s and living 9-10 d unfed or >90 d in media (Blackiston 2021, Sci Robot), and kinematically self-replicating semitoroids reaching 3 +/- 0.8 replication rounds vs 1.2 +/- 0.4 for spheroids (Kriegman 2021, PNAS). Anthrobots from a single adult human lung cell are 30-500 um and move at 5-50 um/s (Gumuskaya 2024, Adv Sci). The decisive finding for the brief is Fotowat et al. 2026 (Adv Sci, Levin lab): 'neurobots' built from Xenopus ectoderm plus implanted neural precursors show enrichment of visual-perception pathways exclusively in neurobots, including rhodopsin (rho), cone opsins (opn1lw, opn1sw), melanopsin (opn4, opn5) and rgr, and the authors state the neurobots 'could potentially sense and process light stimuli' -- inferred from transcriptome only, with NO light-response behaviour tested and optogenetic activation named explicitly as future work. So the brief's 'optogenetic xenobot where light sensors trigger movements' is, as of today, an open and publicly flagged gap, not a published result. The one reported instance of light-driven xenobot locomotion (ChR2 by mRNA microinjection, significant velocity increase, paired t-test p=0.0124, n=8) exists only in a Levin/Blackiston patent that I could not fetch directly, and in no peer-reviewed paper: a Europe PMC query for (xenobot OR 'biological robot' OR anthrobot) AND (optogenetic OR channelrhodopsin) returns 8 hits, none of them such a study. Peer-reviewed precedent for light-driven biohybrid locomotion is in other systems: ChR2 cardiomyocytes steering a 1/10-scale soft-robotic ray by light frequency and independent left/right fin stimulation (Park 2016, Science), optogenetic skeletal muscle giving up to 300 uN (0.56 kPa) and 310 um/s locomotion (Raman 2016, PNAS), and bPAC raising cAMP to accelerate flagellar beat within seconds (Jansen 2015, eLife) -- which makes bPAC, not a cation channel, the mechanistically better-supported effector for a cilia-driven bot, since ciliary beat frequency is cAMP-dependent. On the local .life format: it is a genuinely strong provenance and consistency layer (five per-cell channels, per-channel provenance stamps, five refusals, a measured/assumed/depicted/not-established value vocabulary, usableFor gating, stamped STL and FASTA export) and it cannot currently express this experiment at all. A grep of the whole organism-format tree for opsin|light|optogen|locomot|behaviour|actuat|cilia|contract|velocity|motil returns zero vocabulary hits -- the only matches are prose in comments and one scope string. There is no locomotion channel, no stimulus/actuation axis, no membrane-potential channel, no sub-ontogenetic time unit (all eight TIME_UNITS are developmental, none are seconds), and no causal link from a genome edit to a behaviour, so 'genome to locomotion' would be two unlinked records in one file. Computationally, the morphology-and-motion half is validatable today with open tools (Voxelyze/VoxCAD, CompuCell3D, Morpheus, PhysiCell, BETSE for bioelectrics); the chain opsin photocurrent -> ciliary beat frequency -> hydrodynamic thrust has no open published implementation I could find, and that is the real computational gap. On nonprofits: the only clearly confirmed one is The Guy Foundation Family Trust, a registered charity in England and Wales (no. 1178782), which granted US$199,589 and US$290,778 to Levin's Tufts lab for bioelectric-field work; ICDO's legal status is stated nowhere I could fetch, and Morphoceuticals, Fauna Systems and Astonishing Labs are companies.

findings.claim: Gen-2 cilia-driven xenobots are spheres of 3026 +/- 180 cells that differentiate into ciliated epithelium over 4 days
findings.value: 3026 +/- 180 cells; ciliated epithelium by day 4; motile from day 3

findings.claim: Fully differentiated xenobot spheres range from 487 +/- 39 um (smallest cut explants, n=15) to 602 +/- 30 um (largest, n=13) in diameter
Xenobots move at rates exceeding 100 um/s in aqueous solution
findings.value: >100 um/s (the published PDF text reads '100 m/s'; the micro sign is lost in pdftotext extraction, and 100 m/s is physically impossible for a 0.5 mm swimmer)

findings.claim: Normalised xenobot speed is about 0.18 body lengths per second
findings.value: 100 um/s / ((487+602)/2 = 544.5 um) = 0.18 BL/s -- my own calculation from the two Blackiston figures

findings.claim: Xenobots are self-powered on maternal yolk platelets for 9-10 days, extendable beyond 90 days in Xenopus-specific culture media
findings.value: 9-10 d unfed; >90 d in culture media

findings.claim: Xenobot average velocity does not change significantly across the lifespan, but doubling body size significantly reduces it
findings.value: lifespan effect Kruskal-Wallis P = 0.29; size doubling Student t test P = 0.04, attributed to reduced surface-to-volume ratio

findings.claim: Xenobots locomoted through confined spaces down to a 580 um inner-diameter capillary

Blackiston 2021 already demonstrates a hands-off, imaging-free light experiment: xenobots expressing photoconvertible EosFP were released into a 5 cm arena with a 7 mm illuminated spot 20 mm from the loading zone, left 1 hour unsupervised, then scored after the fact; 3 of 10 showed strong red emission
findings.value: 5 cm arena; 7 mm spot; 20 mm away; 1 h; 390-400 nm light; 10 individuals released, 3 strongly photoconverted

findings.claim: Cilia-driven locomotion is abolished by overexpressing the Notch receptor intracellular domain (NotchICD), which diverts differentiating tissue to other epidermal fates -- a clean genetic negative control for any light-driven-motility claim
findings.value: NotchICD overexpression; multiciliated cells quantified per 500 um diameter region

findings.claim: Gen-1 (cardiomyocyte) xenobot papers report no absolute body length; a 100 um concavity is described as 12% of total body length, implying roughly 833 um
findings.value: 100 um / 0.12 = 833 um (my calculation). Contraction cycled at 2 Hz; selection on net displacement over a 10 s period; 6 organisms built; ground contact 52.7% then 93.3% of the gait cycle

findings.claim: Gen-1 xenobots were built from pluripotent blastula cells, epidermal cells and cardiac progenitors, reared at 14 C, with 370 pg mRNA microinjected per transcript into all four cells
findings.value: 14 C rearing; 22 C healing; 20 C imaging; 370 pg mRNA per transcript; 5 animal caps pooled per construct; designs >50% muscle were filtered out

findings.claim: Kinematic self-replication: semitoroid progenitors achieved 3 +/- 0.8 replication rounds (max 4) versus 1.2 +/- 0.4 (max 2) for spheroids, a 250% increase
findings.value: 3 +/- 0.8 SD vs 1.2 +/- 0.4 SD rounds; +250%, P < 0.05; offspring diameter 149% larger, Mann-Whitney P = 0.037; generations P = 0.019; size-generation correlation rho = 0.93

findings.claim: Self-replication required ~60,000 dissociated stem cells in a 60 mm dish at 25-150 cells/mm2, with a minimum pile of at least 50 cells to mature into an offspring; one replication round takes about a week and wild-type organisms live 10-14 days
findings.value: ~60,000 cells per 60 mm dish; 25-150 cells/mm2; >=50 cells minimum pile; ~3,000 cells per progenitor; 1 week per round; 20 h per trial generation; lifespan 10-14 d; 14 C culture, 20 C trials

findings.claim: The self-replication design search used a GPU-parallelised voxel-based soft-body simulator (unnamed in text, cited to ref. 40) with a pile threshold of 108 voxels, 9 progenitors and 1,262 simulated loose cells per dish, 49 independent trials, 48 h wall clock on eight NVIDIA Tesla V100s, integration step 2.14e-4 s over 16,366 steps
findings.value: 108 voxels threshold; 9 progenitors + 1,262 cells; 49 trials; 48 h on 8x V100; 2.14e-4 s step; 16,366 steps; 3.5 s evaluation

findings.claim: Anthrobots are 30-500 um in diameter, form from a single adult human lung cell after about two weeks in extracellular matrix, move by cilia at 5-50 um/s, and can traverse and rapidly repair scratches in cultured human neural sheets
findings.value: 30-500 um diameter; 5-50 um/s; single seed cell; ~2 weeks in ECM. Normalised: 50 um/s / 300 um = 0.17 BL/s (my calculation)

findings.claim: DECISIVE GAP: Levin-lab 'neurobots' (2026) show enrichment of visual-perception pathways exclusively in neurobots, including rhodopsin (rho), cone opsins opn1lw and opn1sw, melanopsin opn4 and opn5, and rgr; the authors state the neurobots 'could potentially sense and process light stimuli' but tested NO light-response behaviour and name optogenetic activation of neurons only as future work
findings.value: opsin genes rho, opn1lw, opn1sw, opn4, opn5, rgr; retinal development genes neurod1, neurod2, pou4f1, onecut1, lhx1, unc5d, prdm13; 6,774 genes up / 3,578 down vs biobots; inference from transcriptome only

findings.claim: Neurobots are significantly larger than non-neural biobots, show more complex movement, differ in response to neuroactive drugs, and have the same 9-10 day unfed lifespan; neural precursors came from animal caps of about 50 embryos
findings.value: size Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.0007; n = 46 neurobots vs 48 biobots in movement recordings; 16 vs 16 in the PTZ experiment at 15 mM PTZ; calcium imaging 10 min at 5 frames/s; neurite extremes 327 terminals / 7635.9 mm vs 40 terminals / 753.8 mm; lifespan ~9-10 d unfed; ~50 embryos' animal caps per precursor pool

findings.claim: No peer-reviewed study of optogenetic or channelrhodopsin control of xenobots, biobots or anthrobots exists in Europe PMC
findings.value: Europe PMC query (xenobot OR 'biological robot' OR anthrobot) AND (optogenetic OR channelrhodopsin) returns 8 total hits, all reviews or unrelated platform papers (e.g. Drosophila microrobotics 10.1073/pnas.2426180122, biohybrid review 10.1038/s44182-025-00056-x); none reports light-driven biobot locomotion

findings.claim: The only reported light-driven xenobot locomotion is in a Levin/Blackiston patent, not in the literature: ChR2 delivered by mRNA microinjection gave a significant velocity increase under blue light versus untreated controls, and the filing claims to be first to show control of cilia beating with light
findings.value: paired t-test p = 0.0124, n = 8 individuals per treatment; ChR2 by mRNA microinjection; proposed mechanism is cation efflux raising cilia beat frequency. Patent US20220220437A1 / granted US12215344, 'Engineered multicellular ciliated organisms and kinematic self-replication thereof'
findings.source_url_or_path: WebSearch extract of https://patents.google.com/patent/US20220220437A1/en -- I could NOT fetch the patent document itself: patents.google.com returned HTTP 503 on three attempts, the USPTO PDF exceeded the 10 MB fetch limit and a curl of it truncated at 3.8 MB with an unreadable xref table, patentguru returned 468, espacenet 403, freepatentsonline ECONNRESET

findings.claim: Peer-reviewed precedent for light-steered biohybrid locomotion: a 1/10-scale soft-robotic ray with optogenetically engineered rat cardiomyocytes on a microfabricated gold skeleton, where light frequency sets speed and independent left/right fin stimulation sets direction through an obstacle course
findings.value: 1/10 scale; serpentine muscle circuits; sequential light-triggered activation. Absolute length, mass, cardiomyocyte count, wavelength and irradiance were NOT in the records I fetched (PMC5526330 fullTextXML returned HTTP 500)

findings.claim: Optogenetic skeletal-muscle bioactuators on 3D-printed flexible skeletons reach up to 300 uN (0.56 kPa) active tension under non-invasive optical stimulation, driving 310 um/s directional locomotion (1.3 body lengths/min) and 2 deg/s steering, and adapt after exercise training
findings.value: 300 uN (0.56 kPa); 310 um/s = 1.3 BL/min; 2 deg/s rotation

findings.claim: bPAC (photoactivated adenylyl cyclase) is the mechanistically better-supported effector for a cilia-driven bot than a cation channel, because light-triggered cAMP elevation accelerates the flagellar beat within seconds and restored motility and in vitro fertilisation in sperm lacking bicarbonate-stimulated sACY
findings.value: beat frequency rises within seconds of light; restored IVF in sACY-null sperm

findings.claim: Direct ciliary targeting of optogenetic tools can impair protein function, so fusing bPAC or LAPD to cilia-localising sequences reduces activity -- a design constraint for any cilia-targeted opsin
findings.source_url_or_path: https://www.zfin.org/ZDB-FIG-200715-7 (reported in a WebSearch result; I did not fetch the underlying paper, so treat as a flag to check rather than a settled constraint)

findings.claim: Light-gated ion translocators have already been used in Xenopus by the Levin lab to control bioelectric state and tumorigenesis, and optogenetics has been used in Xenopus to prevent ethanol-induced brain and eye defects -- so the opsin-in-Xenopus half of the design is established, independent of biobots
findings.value: Chernet, Adams, Lobikin, Levin 2016 Oncotarget (PMID 26988909); Pai & Adams 2019 Bioelectricity (PMID 32685918)

findings.claim: I could not find any published light dose for driving xenobot motility: no irradiance in mW/mm2 appears in any xenobot source I fetched. The only xenobot light numbers are 390-400 nm for photoconverting the EosFP recorder, which is a readout, not an actuator
findings.value: 390 nm / 400 nm (EosFP photoconversion only); no actuation irradiance found

findings.claim: The .life / .organism format has zero vocabulary for locomotion, light, actuation or behaviour. A case-insensitive grep of the whole organism-format tree for opsin|light|optogen|locomot|behaviou?r|actuat|cilia|contract|stimul|velocit|speed|motil returns only prose in code comments and one scope string about a flight surface -- no field, no channel, no unit
findings.value: 4 matches total across .mjs, .organism and .life files, none of them a format field

findings.claim: The .life format's five per-cell channels are transcriptome, mechanics, geometry, lineage and signalling -- there is no membrane-potential or ion-flux channel, so the central observable of the bioelectric programme (Vmem, gap-junction coupling) is not expressible
findings.value: CHANNELS = transcriptome, mechanics, geometry, lineage, signalling; signalling carries only pathway, readout, readout_value

findings.claim: All eight .life time units are developmental, none is sub-second, so a behavioural trace cannot be given a time axis; and the no_cross_unit_distance refusal would block mixing a behavioural timescale with a developmental one
findings.value: TIME_UNITS = hpf, dpf, days, weeks, hours_post_hCG, E, carnegie_stage, cell_cycles; ORDINAL_UNITS = carnegie_stage; refusal no_cross_unit_distance forbids arithmetic across time units and any arithmetic on an ordinal one

findings.claim: What the format CAN already express for this project: an opsin transgene as inline sequence (the .organism genome is an edit list against a named assembly, with inline sequence allowed for a transgene that has no reference to diff against, flagged separately, reader warning above 100 kb)
findings.value: edit list + inline transgene sequence; 100 kb warning threshold; zebrafish primary assembly cited as 1.37 Gbp / 410 MB compressed as the reason not to embed a genome

findings.claim: The format's strongest asset for a light-driven claim is usableFor: a simulation that consumes an assumed value produces a result about the assumption, and publish_a_number admits measured values only -- which is exactly the gate a light-dose number taken from a patent would fail
findings.value: render: anything if captioned; simulate: measured, derived, calibrated; publish_a_number: measured only; compare_to_a_real_organism: measured, measured-secondhand

findings.claim: The format carries no ecology and its environment block names only predation, competition, food, flow and conspecifics as absent -- illumination is not even on the list of acknowledged absences, so a light-driven organism has nowhere to declare its light environment
findings.value: environment names absent: predation, competition, food, flow, conspecifics

findings.claim: No measured geometry exists anywhere in the organism-format directory: every committed stage is depicted, so the non-DEPICTION branch of exportStage has never produced a file from real data and is exercised only by tests
findings.value: worked example: geometry present on 31 of 31 cells, measured on 0; status DEGRADED with 7 things a reader must be told; 11 of 12 constraints applied; transcriptome, mechanics and signalling present on 0 of 31 cells

findings.claim: A sphere-packed mesh export has no contact faces, so every cell's exposed surface area comes out too large -- which matters specifically for a ciliated surface-driven swimmer, because thrust scales with exposed ciliated area, so any STL exported from a .life would systematically overestimate available thrust
findings.value: qualitative; the format itself states the bias direction (inner cells resemble outer ones) and that any mesh export contradicts a measured exposed_surface_area

findings.claim: A binary STL exported from a .life has no unit field and most slicers assume millimetres, so a micrometre-scale organism is wrong by a factor of 1000 with no complaint -- a hard blocker for handing a 500 um bot geometry to a printer or a solver
findings.value: factor of 1000; the exporter states the unit it dropped in its 80-byte header, e.g. 'life-stl/0.1.0 stage=morula provenance=depicted units=um DEPICTION'

findings.claim: Open simulators that could validate the morphology-and-motion half today: Voxelyze/VoxCAD (open-source C++, soft multimaterial voxel dynamics with volumetric actuation and collision handling -- the lineage both xenobot design papers used), plus CompuCell3D, Morpheus and PhysiCell for cell-level morphogenesis and BETSE for bioelectrics
findings.value: Voxelyze: thousands of degrees of freedom at interactive frame rates on a single desktop thread, open-source C++, platform agnostic; xenobot design code at github.com/skriegman/reconfigurable_organisms

findings.claim: No open simulator couples an opsin photocurrent to ciliary beat frequency to hydrodynamic thrust. BETSE models bioelectric signalling, Voxelyze models soft-body actuation as an abstract volumetric force, and nothing I could fetch bridges them -- so the opsin-to-motion link cannot be validated purely computationally today without writing that coupling
findings.value: In the Blackiston 2021 simulations cilia are modelled as a manually tuned tangential force per surface voxel with no photophysics: 'the maximal magnitude of the force was manually adjusted'; 22,940 time steps per simulation

findings.claim: The clearest bioelectricity nonprofit is The Guy Foundation Family Trust, a registered charity in England and Wales (no. 1178782), established 2018, founder and chairman Prof. Geoffrey Guy, which funded Levin's Tufts lab for bioelectric-field work
findings.value: US$199,589 for bioelectric fields and information storage in physiological rather than genetic media; US$290,778 for V-ATPase proton pumps and whole-body form; charity no. 1178782

findings.claim: ICDO (Institute for Computationally Designed Organisms), founded by Joshua Bongard (U. Vermont) and Michael Levin (Allen Discovery Center at Tufts), spans the Allen Discovery Center at Tufts and the Morphology, Evolution & Cognition Laboratory at UVM -- but its own site states nothing about legal status, nonprofit registration or funding
findings.value: two sites; no legal status stated

findings.claim: Michael Levin's own resources page lists no organisation as a nonprofit; entities adjacent to the bioelectric programme include the Allen Discovery Center at Tufts, Tufts Center for Regenerative and Developmental Biology, ICDO, the Wyss Institute, the Proteus Institute, and the companies Morphoceuticals and Unravel Biosciences
findings.value: legal/tax status not stated for any of them on that page

findings.claim: Other bodies that appear in this space but should not be mistaken for dedicated bioelectricity nonprofits: Morphoceuticals is a for-profit company (US$8m Seed-2 led by Prime Movers Lab and Juvenescence), the Frank Reidy Research Center for Bioelectrics is a university centre at Old Dominion, and BioSingularity Institute is a tiny Every.org-listed nonprofit with $0 raised against a $1,000,000 goal whose focus is a qigong-based healing practice and whose scientific standing is unclear

recommendations: Build the optogenetic design on the one hands-off experiment that is already published rather than on the patent. Blackiston 2021 released 10 EosFP-expressing xenobots into a 5 cm arena with a 7 mm illuminated spot 20 mm away, left them 1 hour with no imaging and no handling, and scored photoconversion afterwards; 3 of 10 had been exposed. Pair that integrator with a light-driven actuator and you get open-loop drive plus a post-hoc record with zero live microscopy -- exactly the 'no imaging or direct interaction' constraint in the brief, and it is defensible from a fetched source.

Choose bPAC over ChR2 as the effector, and say why in the paper. Ciliary and flagellar beat frequency is cAMP-dependent, and bPAC's light-to-cAMP-to-faster-beat chain is peer-reviewed with a seconds-scale latency (Jansen 2015, eLife 10.7554/eLife.05161). The ChR2 route for ciliated biobots rests on a cation-efflux mechanism the patent itself only calls 'hypothesised', and it is unpublished. A reviewer will ask which link in the chain is measured; with bPAC the answer is the effector link.

Use the published negative control. NotchICD overexpression diverts the differentiating tissue to non-ciliated epidermal fates and abolishes motion (Blackiston 2021). A light-driven-motility claim with a NotchICD arm distinguishes 'light raised the beat frequency' from 'light did something else that happened to move the bot'. Without it the velocity change is uninterpretable, which is the main weakness of the n=8, p=0.0124 patent result.

Deliver the opsin by mRNA microinjection at the 4-cell stage, not as a transgene. Kriegman 2020 injected 370 pg of mRNA per transcript into all four cells; Blackiston used the same route for NotchICD, EosFP, centrin-RFP and CLAMP-GFP. This keeps the genome reference-only, which means the .life genome block stays an honest edit-free record and the FASTA export correctly refuses rather than emitting a reference assembly dressed up as a design.

Treat the light dose as an open hole and pre-register it as not-established. No irradiance in mW/mm2 for driving xenobot motility appears in any source I could fetch; the only xenobot light numbers are 390-400 nm for photoconverting a recorder. Put it in the .organism as a not-established entry with a what_would_resolve_it field naming the measurement (irradiance at the arena floor, exposure duration, and the resulting velocity, with a NotchICD arm) -- the format is built for exactly this and it is more credible than importing a number from a patent.

Lead the paper with the 2026 neurobot gap, because it is the strongest framing available and it is Levin's own. Fotowat et al. (10.1002/advs.202508967) found rho, opn1lw, opn1sw, opn4, opn5 and rgr enriched exclusively in neurobots and wrote that these bots 'could potentially sense and process light stimuli', tested no light behaviour, and named optogenetic activation as future work. A 'light sensors trigger movements' design is therefore the published next step of the field's own paper, not a speculative pivot. Note the albino caveat: the calcium-imaging bots were albino and the authors flag that albino tadpoles differ in visually evoked behaviour.

Extend .life with four things before claiming it can hold a genome-to-locomotion design, and keep the format's own discipline while doing it: (1) a behaviour channel carrying the four quantities Blackiston actually computed -- position, linear speed, heading, angular speed -- with a provenance stamp per track, not per point; (2) a stimulus block with wavelength_nm, irradiance_mW_per_mm2, duty_cycle, exposure_s and a geometry for where the light was; (3) a seconds-scale time unit, which forces a decision about no_cross_unit_distance rather than silently violating it; (4) a membrane_potential channel with readout_kind and is_relative, mirroring the mechanics channel's hard-won lesson that a field name must not impose a unit the measurement does not have.

Add one refusal rather than one field for the causal claim: no_unlinked_mechanism -- a file that carries both a genome edit and a behaviour measurement, and no stated mechanism connecting them, degrades rather than passes. This is the same move the format already makes with no_identity_drift, and it is the difference between a genome-to-locomotion file and two records in one envelope. 'Nothing checked is not a pass' is already a standing rule in the spec; this applies it to the claim the whole project rests on.

Scope the computational validation honestly in the paper: the morphology-and-motion half is validatable today in open tools (Voxelyze for soft-body actuation and thrust, CompuCell3D or Morpheus or PhysiCell for the morphogenesis, BETSE for the bioelectric state), but no open simulator couples a photocurrent to a ciliary beat frequency to a thrust. In Blackiston 2021 the cilia force is a manually tuned tangential force per surface voxel. Writing that coupling -- even a one-parameter map from irradiance to per-voxel tangential force, calibrated against one measured velocity -- is a small, publishable, and genuinely missing piece.

Do not let an STL exported from a .life reach a printer or a solver unexamined. Binary STL has no unit field, most slicers assume millimetres, and a 500 um bot is then wrong by 1000x; separately, the sphere-packing shape model has no contact faces, so exposed surface area is overestimated in exactly the direction that inflates the ciliated area a thrust estimate depends on. Both are stated in the format's own README; the thrust bias should be written into any simulation result as a derived value with its rule named.

For funding and framing, The Guy Foundation Family Trust (charity no. 1178782) is the one confirmed nonprofit funder with a track record here -- two grants to Levin's Tufts lab totalling about US$490k for bioelectric-field and V-ATPase work. ICDO is the natural institutional partner for a computationally designed organism, but its legal status is stated nowhere public, so ask directly rather than describing it as a nonprofit in any document.

Avoid one trap in the measured numbers: the Blackiston PDF's '100 m/s' is a lost micro sign and the self-replication paper gives NO absolute parent or offspring diameters in um, only scale bars and percentage changes (+149%). Any table that prints a self-replication diameter in microns is inventing it. Likewise the 30-500 um anthrobot range is confirmed in the published abstract but no cell count per anthrobot was in anything I fetched.
