fleet.label: q2-physics
fleet.topic: Q2 binding-affinity prediction: the physics that models skip
fleet.summary: Binding affinity is hard in principle because the quantity is a small difference of large, compensating terms (dG = dH - TdS; a 10 cal/mol/K entropy change is 2.98 kcal/mol at 298 K), the useful resolution is 0.5-1.4 kcal/mol (5-10x in K; RT ln10 = 1.364 kcal/mol), and the labels are noisy: independent experiments agree to only 0.77-0.95 kcal/mol RMS (Ross 2023), with R2max about 0.81 on public Ki sets (Kramer 2012). Relative FEP reaches median pairwise RMSE 1.08 kcal/mol against an experimental 0.85 on a carefully prepared benchmark, near the floor, but only after protonation, tautomers, poses, waters and flexible loops were fixed by hand. Learned scoring functions reach RMSE 1.3-1.5 pK (1.8-2.1 kcal/mol) and a pure lookup of similar training complexes gets 1.517 pK on the leaky CASF split, so much benchmark skill is memorisation (Graber 2025). A Lean statement can capture the arithmetic and statistical ceilings (log conversion, noise floor, Kd = koff/kon, Cheng-Prusoff, cycle additivity); the sizes of sigma, prevalence of compensation, water and protonation effects, and model generalisation are empirical. No Lean was compiled in this run.
fleet.lay_summary: Drug makers want to predict how tightly a small molecule sticks to a protein. The difference between a good and a mediocre drug can be tiny, about the energy of one weak bond, and 1.4 kcal/mol of energy already means a tenfold change in stickiness. It is like weighing a ship's captain by weighing the ship with and without him: two huge numbers, and a small error in either swamps the answer. Even the lab measurements disagree with each other by about that much, so no model can honestly be judged better than the lab noise. Heavy physics simulations get close to that limit but need expert care, while many machine-learning models score well mostly because their test questions resemble their training answers.

The maximum possible squared Pearson correlation coefficient (R(2)) on large data sets is estimated to be 0.81.

findings.claim: Kramer: models with errors below experimental uncertainty are overtrained, so experimental uncertainty is a natural upper limit on predictive performance (the statement a Lean noise-ceiling theorem would formalise).
findings.evidence_quote: experimental uncertainty defines a natural upper limit to the predictive performance possible. Models that yield errors smaller than the experimental uncertainty are necessarily overtrained.

findings.claim: Ross et al. survey: median RMSE between experimental assays is 0.85 kcal/mol; median pairwise RMSE of FEP+ on their benchmark is 1.08 kcal/mol.
findings.evidence_quote: The median RMSE in the experimental survey is 0.85 kcal mol−1 and the median in the FEP+ benchmark is 1.08 kcal mol−1.

findings.claim: Of 13,732 FEP+ relative binding free energy predictions, 57.5% were within 1 kcal/mol of experiment and 12.9% off by more than 2; among 314,535 experimental pairs 83.0% agreed within 1 kcal/mol and 2.1% differed by more than 2.

findings.claim: Ross et al.: experimental RMSE is about 1 kcal/mol on average, so FEP matching it on a large diverse set would be an extraordinary challenge; with careful structure preparation FEP can reach accuracy comparable to experimental reproducibility.

findings.claim: FEP accuracy depends on preparation: protonation and tautomeric states of ligand and protein residues are historically difficult to assign; missing loops and flexible regions need care.
findings.evidence_quote: A historically difficult aspect of preparing structures has been the determination of the protonation and tautomeric states of the ligands and the protein binding residues

findings.claim: A trivial memorisation baseline (average labels of the 5 most similar training complexes) reaches Pearson R=0.716, RMSE=1.517 (pK units, about 2.07 kcal/mol) on CASF-2016, competitive with published deep-learning scoring functions: train-test leakage between PDBbind and CASF.
findings.evidence_quote: This algorithm showed competitive CASF2016 prediction root-mean-square error (r.m.s.e.) compared with some published deep-learning-based scoring functions (Pearson R = 0.716, r.m.s.e. = 1.517).

findings.claim: After removing leakage (PDBbind CleanSplit) the search baseline drops to RMSE 1.648, R=0.653; GEMS trained on CleanSplit gets RMSE 1.308, R=0.803 (Pafnucy 1.484/0.746, GenScore 1.362/0.780).
findings.evidence_quote: With a prediction r.m.s.e. of 1.308 and a Pearson correlation of 0.803, GEMS considerably outperforms Pafnucy (r.m.s.e. = 1.484, Pearson R = 0.746) and GenScore (r.m.s.e. = 1.362, Pearson R = 0.780)

findings.claim: The best leakage-free learned scoring function (1.308 pK, 1.78 kcal/mol) is about 1.9-2.3x the experimental pairwise RMS (0.77-0.95 kcal/mol); caveat: different quantities (absolute pK vs relative dG) and different sets.

findings.claim: On CASF-2016, current scoring functions do better at docking power than at scoring, ranking and screening power.
findings.evidence_quote: the performance of current scoring functions is more promising in terms of docking power than scoring, ranking, and screening power.

findings.claim: Entropy-enthalpy compensation: evidence for severe compensation is weak because errors in measured entropy and enthalpy are large and correlated; a limited form may be common.
findings.evidence_quote: We find the evidence for severe compensation to be weak in light of the large magnitude of and correlation between errors in experimental measurements of entropic and enthalpic contributions to binding, though a limited form of compensation may be common.

findings.claim: Chodera and Mobley recommend assessing changes in binding free energy directly, since entropic and enthalpic changes are hard to predict or measure to useful precision.
findings.evidence_quote: Given the difficulty of predicting or measuring entropic and enthalpic changes to useful precision, or using this information in design, we recommend ligand engineering efforts instead focus on computational and experimental methodologies to directly assess changes in binding free energy.

findings.claim: Illustration: at 298.15 K an entropy change of 10 cal/mol/K is worth T*dS = 2.98 kcal/mol (about 153-fold in K), so dH and TdS terms of several kcal/mol each can cancel to leave dG within the 1.4 kcal/mol scale.
findings.source: own calculation: arithmetic.py (the 153 is exp(2.98/0.5925), computed here)

findings.claim: Water displacement: a ligand change that displaces an ordered water can raise or lower affinity depending on the cost of removing the water versus new interactions; naive ligand-only perturbation can trap the water and mislead.
findings.evidence_quote: the binding affinity may diminish if the free-energy increase due to the removal of the bound water molecule is not more than compensated by the additional interactions of the water-displacing moiety.

findings.claim: Protonation: binding can shift pK and protonation states, making binding pH dependent, though shifts do not occur in every complex and prevalence estimates vary by complex and method.
findings.evidence_quote: While there is no doubt that these changes occur, they do not occur all the time; the estimated prevalence varies, both between individual complexes and by method.

findings.claim: Flexibility: conformational selection may be far more common than believed, and a rise in k_obs with ligand concentration is not unequivocal evidence of induced fit.
findings.evidence_quote: We conclude that conformational selection as a mechanism for a ligand binding to its target may be far more common than currently believed.

findings.claim: Residence time (dissociative half-life of the drug-target complex) is an alternative to Kd/IC50 for optimisation, with potential advantages for duration of effect and selectivity.
findings.evidence_quote: This article presents an alternative perspective on drug optimization in terms of drug-target binary complex residence time, as quantified by the dissociative half-life of the drug-target binary complex.

findings.claim: Kinetics arithmetic: Kd=koff/kon, so Kd=1 nM is reached by (kon 1e6 /M/s, koff 1e-3 /s; residence 1000 s) or (kon 1e8, koff 0.1; residence 10 s): same dG, 100-fold different residence time.
findings.source: own calculation: arithmetic.py (Kd=koff/kon is the definition for 1:1 binding)

findings.claim: Assay conditions: mixing ChEMBL IC50 values from different assays adds moderate noise (SD only 25% larger than for Ki); a Ki-IC50 conversion factor of 2 was most reasonable.
findings.evidence_quote: The standard deviation of IC50 data is only 25% larger than the standard deviation of Ki data, suggesting that mixing IC50 data from different assays, even not knowing assay conditions details, only adds a moderate amount of noise

findings.claim: Cheng-Prusoff (competitive inhibitor): IC50 = Ki(1+[S]/Km). At [S]=Km a 2-fold (0.41 kcal/mol) offset; at [S]=10 Km an 11-fold (1.42 kcal/mol) offset, so assay design alone can exceed the 1.4 kcal/mol scale.
findings.source: own calculation: arithmetic.py; formula is unverified background (standard; the 1973 paper's DOI resolved but no text was read)

findings.claim: Brown et al.: expected model performance is often not supported by the underlying data because of neglected assay and prediction errors.
findings.evidence_quote: the expected performance of many models is simply not supported by the underlying data, because of often neglected effects of assay and prediction errors on the reliability of the predicted outcome.

findings.claim: Merck KGaA prospective FEP+ study: physics-based free energy calculation is regarded as the most rigorous way to estimate binding affinity; large-scale prospective use exposed limitations.
findings.evidence_quote: Physics-based free energy calculations are regarded as the most rigorous way to estimate binding affinity.

findings.claim: Relative FEP is the mature form: it predicts affinity differences for congeneric ligands with enough accuracy to add value in hit-to-lead and lead optimisation.
findings.evidence_quote: RBFE simulations can now predict the affinity differences for congeneric ligands with sufficient accuracy and throughput to deliver considerable value in hit-to-lead and lead optimization efforts.

findings.claim: Noise-ceiling arithmetic: R2max = 1 - sigma^2/Var(obs). Kramer's R2max=0.81 with sigma=0.54 pK corresponds to an observed-label SD of about 1.24 pK (assuming the same sigma).
Cooperativity (binding at one site changing affinity at another) is a distinct non-additive effect; no numeric benchmark was extracted.

recommendations: Lean-capturable (theorems from explicit hypotheses): (1) dG = -RT ln K, so a factor 10 in K is RT ln10; (2) noise ceiling: for label = truth + independent noise of variance s^2 with observed variance V, any predictor's squared correlation with the observed label is at most 1 - s^2/V and its expected squared error against one measurement is at least s^2; (3) pairwise replicate RMS = sqrt2 * sigma; (4) additivity of dG around thermodynamic cycles, so an RBFE graph is identifiable only up to a constant; (5) Kd = koff/kon, so equal dG allows different residence times and no function of dG alone predicts residence; (6) Cheng-Prusoff offset; (7) compensation: with dG = dH - T dS, dH and T dS can both move while dG stays fixed, so enthalpy alone does not identify dG; (8) a nearest-neighbour memoriser has error bounded by label variation among similar inputs, so benchmark skill under leakage is not evidence of physics. None of these were compiled in this run; they are proposals.

Empirical (needs data, not Lean): size of sigma per assay type; prevalence and magnitude of compensation; water-network energetics; protonation shifts; induced fit versus selection; cooperativity; whether a given deep model generalises. Test the Lean noise-ceiling statement against public replicate data (ChEMBL pairs, Ross survey) and the CleanSplit versus original PDBbind results.
Convert pK to kcal/mol explicitly (x1.364). Ross reports relative dG pairwise errors, Graber reports absolute pK errors, so do not compare 1.08 kcal/mol and 1.308 pK directly.

fleet.label: q2-theory-lean
fleet.topic: Q2 binding-affinity prediction: what is mathematically impossible, in Lean
fleet.summary: All four requested statements (a)-(d) were stated and proved in Lean 4 (v4.35.0, Mathlib at the delphisci/lean pin) in one self-contained file, Q2Theory.lean. check.sh reports errors=0, sorryAx=0, 16/16 #print axioms lines; every theorem depends only on propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound. The setting is a finite probability space (weights summing to 1); independence is weakened to uncorrelatedness, which makes the theorems stronger. Key caveat: the attenuation bound needs the predictor to be uncorrelated with the assay noise (cov(p,e)=0); without it the bound is false (p = y_obs gives r=1). Nothing was tested on data; this track is statements and proofs only. Nothing requested failed to prove; the first compiles had errors (a rewrite in var_add, an argument name in sum_fibers, and a check.sh false positive on theorem names containing the word 'error', which I renamed) that were fixed.
fleet.lay_summary: We wrote four facts as computer-checked proofs. First, if the lab measurement of binding strength is noisy, no model that has not seen that noise can match the measurements better than a fixed ceiling set by how big the noise is compared with the real spread. Think of trying to match a ruler that wobbles: even a perfect model looks imperfect. Second, a model that only knows which protein it is looking at can explain the differences between proteins but nothing about differences among drugs for the same protein. Third, energies around a closed loop of chemical changes must add to zero, so a model's mistakes around that loop cannot all be independent. Fourth, if someone claims a score above the ceiling, the proof shows the claim cannot be right for that noise level.

glossary.plain: A proof checker: a program that accepts a mathematical proof only if every step is valid.
The large shared library of already-proved mathematics that Lean proofs build on.
A number from -1 to 1 saying how closely two lists of numbers rise and fall together.
How spread out a set of numbers is.
How much two lists of numbers move together, before scaling.
The shrinking of a measured correlation caused by noise in the measurement.
A loop of changes that returns to its starting state, so the total energy change is zero.
The marker Lean leaves when a proof has a gap; its absence means no gaps.
Having zero covariance; a weaker condition than independent.

Test (b) by computing the target-mean baseline r^2 = between/total on pooled PDBbind-type data and comparing with the model r^2; the gap above it is within-target skill.
For (c), the exchangeable result predicts error correlation -1/(n-1) around an n-edge relative free-energy cycle; check against cycle-closure residuals in published edge errors.

fleet.label: t1-reporter-alt
fleet.topic: Track 1 alternatives and neighbours
fleet.summary: Keep the chosen system (threshold-steepness separability in RBS-variant Cello repressor gates) and run ONE alternative alongside it: the RBS-tuned lac-repressor induction library of Garcia & Phillips 2011 / Razo-Mejia et al. 2018 (MIT-licensed flow_master.csv, 250 KB, now on D:). I refit it myself with a 4-parameter Hill curve. Across six RBS variants (repressor copies 11 to 870 per cell), the half-maximal IPTG (EC50) moves 4.94-fold at operator O1 and 17.47-fold at O2, while the Hill coefficient stays at 1.37-1.54 (O1) and 1.46-1.69 (O2): maximum pairwise relative difference 0.116 and 0.150, and none of 15 pairs per operator has non-overlapping 95% bootstrap CIs. At the weak operator O3 the curves are too flat for n to be determined (n 0.87-1.89, CIs wide), so that case is uninformative, not supportive. This is an independent system and a different input axis (inducer, not repressor synthesis), so it supports the idea that RBS-tuned repressor level shifts the threshold without a detectable steepness change, but it does not confirm the Cello claim itself. Seven further candidates are costed in the table (Reg-Seq, Kosuri 12,563 promoter x RBS library, Marionette, Buchler-Cross yeast sequestration, Qian resource-competition cascades, EMOPEC Shine-Dalgarno library, Ozbudak translation-vs-transcription noise) plus the two the scout already had. The strongest published competing explanation is molecular titration/sequestration (Buchler & Louis 2008; Buchler & Cross 2009), which says steepness itself depends on repressor abundance and so predicts that an RBS change should change n; resource competition (Qian 2017) is the second. Two corrections to the earlier law-mapper: law set 1.8.1 no longer contains Delphi/Turing.lean or the turing-ddi-linear-condition law (replaced by candidate turing-ddi 1.1.0 with proofs in registry/proposals/turing-ddi/law.lean), and 1.8.1 still has no Hill-type or reporter law (gene-regulatory-dynamics is still a placeholder gap).
fleet.lay_summary: The main plan tests whether turning a gene's 'volume knob' (a DNA switch that sets how much repressor protein is made) shifts when a genetic switch flips without changing how sharply it flips. I looked for other experiments that could test the same idea. The best one is a long-running set of bacteria where scientists tuned how many repressor molecules each cell makes, then slowly added a chemical and watched the glow. Re-analysing their public spreadsheet, the point where the glow turned on moved five to seventeen times, yet the sharpness of the turn-on barely changed. A rival idea says the sharpness should change when the amount of repressor changes, so the main plan is a fair fight. I recommend keeping the main plan and adding this second data set as a cross-check.

findings.evidence_quote: O3 EC50 range 0.6-23.3 uM, fold 40.07 (log2 5.32) | n range 0.87-1.89, (max-min)/mean = 0.855

findings.claim: In the lac data the plateau (fold change at saturating IPTG) falls as repressor copy number rises (O1 fitted plateau 1.034 at R=11 vs 0.437 at R=870), so an RBS change is NOT a pure translation of the curve along log-input here: dynamic range also changes. Cello's ymax/ymin should therefore be checked within families too.

Caveat on A1: the input axis differs from Cello gates. In the lac system RBS sets repressor copies and the input is an inducer that binds the repressor (allosteric MWC); in a Cello gate the input promoter drives repressor synthesis. So A1 tests 'RBS-tuned repressor level leaves n unchanged', not the Cello log-translation law itself.
findings.source: reasoning from paper abstracts (Razo-Mejia 2018, Nielsen 2016) and the CSV columns
findings.evidence_quote: first predicting the behavior of strains that span a large range of repressor copy numbers and DNA binding strengths and then constructing and measuring their response.

findings.claim: Garcia & Phillips 2011 used a collection of strains with a large variation in repressor copy number to test the simple-repression input-output function.
findings.evidence_quote: using the mathematical description of these regulatory motifs as a predictive tool to determine the number of repressors in a collection of strains with a large variation in repressor copy number

findings.claim: Razo-Mejia 2018 derive analytic expressions for EC50 and dynamic range from an MWC model, i.e. the thermodynamic framework gives a published number-making model for A1 (so A1 can be scored by prediction, not only descriptively).
findings.evidence_quote: enables us to derive analytic expressions for key properties such as the dynamic range and [EC50].

findings.claim: STRONGEST COMPETING EXPLANATION (1): molecular titration / sequestration generates steepness from abundance, so threshold AND steepness both depend on how much repressor/inhibitor is made; it predicts that an RBS change moves n, contrary to the chosen law. Shown experimentally in yeast with apparent Hill coefficients up to 12.
findings.evidence_quote: both the threshold and the degree of ultrasensitivity depend upon the abundance of the inhibitor, exactly as we observed experimentally.

findings.claim: Theory behind competing explanation (1): ultrasensitivity from titration is set mainly by the dissociation constant and the repressor concentration.
findings.evidence_quote: The ultrasensitive nature of the input-output response is mainly determined by two parameters: the dimer dissociation constant and the repressor concentration.

findings.claim: COMPETING EXPLANATION (2): resource competition makes gene-expression cassettes non-modular; RBS and DNA copy number change circuit shape through shared ribosomes/polymerases, so an RBS-driven shift can be a load effect.
findings.evidence_quote: These coefficients lead to nonregulatory interactions among genes that reshape the circuit's behavior.

findings.claim: COMPETING EXPLANATION (3), titration of repressor by extra binding sites: transcription-factor demand from other sites/copies changes the effective dose-response, a thermodynamic-model prediction tested experimentally.
findings.evidence_quote: we characterize the interplay between TF copy number and the demand for that TF.

findings.claim: Candidate A2, Reg-Seq (RPGroup-PBoC/RegSeq, MIT): massively parallel mutation scanning that returns binding-energy matrices; gives a mechanism-level (energy) separability test but is not a dose-response; GitHub reports repo size 324656 KB (about 317 MB), above the 150 MB cap, so NOT downloaded.
findings.source: https://api.github.com/repos/RPGroup-PBoC/RegSeq ; https://raw.githubusercontent.com/RPGroup-PBoC/RegSeq/master/README.md ; tree listing master (largest files 32 MB sequencing files)
findings.evidence_quote: energy matrices that characterize, in k_BT units, the binding strength of transcription factors to their target sites

findings.claim: Candidate A3, Kosuri 2013: 12,563 promoter x RBS combinations with DNA, RNA and protein read out; a ready test of whether the promoter axis and the RBS axis are separable (multiplicative) but each construct is a single state, no dose-response. The data-file location was NOT verified.
findings.evidence_quote: RNA and protein expression were within twofold of expected levels 80% and 64% of the time, respectively.

findings.claim: Kosuri 2013 also reports the failure tail of composability: the worst 5% of constructs deviated by 13-fold, which bounds how strictly any 'RBS acts independently' law can hold.
findings.evidence_quote: the worst 5% of constructs deviated from prediction by 13-fold on average

findings.claim: Candidate A4, Marionette: 12 directed-evolution-optimised sensors with >100-fold induction; useful because dose-response shape was engineered (both K and n moved by selection) - a counter-example source - but there is no RBS series. Raw data location not found.
findings.evidence_quote: a set of 12 high-performance sensors that exhibit >100-fold induction with low background and cross-reactivity.

findings.claim: Candidate A5, Buchler & Cross 2009 yeast sequestration circuit: the system in which the competing law is shown; gives a designed case where n SHOULD change with abundance (a positive control for the test's power). Values only in figures; not machine-readable here.
findings.evidence_quote: converts a graded transcriptional response into a sharply ultrasensitive response, with apparent Hill coefficients up to 12.

findings.claim: Candidate A6, Qian et al. 2017 activation-cascade library: resource demand explicitly tuned (RBS, copy number); gives the confound test (does load, not RBS, explain shifts) at the cost of building a load model; supplementary data availability not verified.
findings.evidence_quote: we create a library of genetic activation cascades in E. coli bacteria, where we explicitly tune the resource demand by each gene.

findings.claim: Candidate A7, EMOPEC (Bonde 2016): Shine-Dalgarno sequence to protein-level map; gives a validated RBS-strength predictor so 'RBS strength' becomes a number, but no dose-response. Code mirror found on GitHub (micked/EMOPEC, no licence field) but data not downloaded.
findings.source: https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.3727 via Europe PMC; GitHub search 2026-11-12
findings.evidence_quote: Measured protein levels for 91% of our designed sequences were within twofold of the desired target level.

findings.claim: Candidate A8, Ozbudak 2002 (B. subtilis): transcription and translation rates varied independently for one reporter; gives the noise-side counter-check, since single-cell noise is NOT invariant to translation rate, which matches the scout's observation that output noise varies within a Cello family. Values in figures only.
findings.evidence_quote: increased translational efficiency is the predominant source of increased phenotypic noise.

findings.claim: Burden measurement: a capacity monitor can assay the burden imposed by constructs, so a growth/burden covariate could be read alongside any gate library to test competing explanation (2).
findings.evidence_quote: We identify construct designs with reduced burden that predictably outperformed less efficient designs, despite having equivalent output.

recommendations: KEEP the chosen system. It is the only candidate where the design change (RBS in front of the repressor) acts on the same axis as the claim, with raw 250-bin histograms and untouched held-out libraries. I did not open Eco1C2G2T2 or any other holdout, so the freeze is intact.

RUN ALONGSIDE: the lac RBS library (A1) as a second, independent system. Cost: near zero (data on D:, refit takes about 2 minutes). Freeze before looking at any further operator or condition: 'n varies by at most 0.15 relative across RBS variants when curve amplitude exceeds 0.7'. Note that O2 already sits exactly at 0.150, so choose the bound and the amplitude cut-off on O1 only and score O2 and any other library as holdout; state that I have now seen both.

Add the titration model (Buchler-Louis / Buchler-Cross) as the named rival in the freeze file with its own falsifiable prediction: n increases or decreases systematically with repressor abundance within a family (trend test), versus the separability claim of no trend. The lac result is currently a mild point against a large titration effect in simple repression, not against titration in general.

Add a burden covariate (growth rate or capacity monitor, Ceroni 2015 style) to any new wet or dry leg to separate resource competition from RBS-specific effects. Cost: one extra readout per construct.
Check ymax and ymin within each Cello family, because the lac data show plateau moving with repressor level; the present freeze only tests K and n.

Low-priority extras: Kosuri 2013 for promoter-by-RBS separability (needs data-file location found first), mismatch-CRISPRi as already planned by the scout, and Reg-Seq only if a mechanistic energy-level leg is wanted (317 MB repo: fetch single files).
Lean: target the successor of gene-regulatory-dynamics at version 1.8.1; do not rely on Delphi.Turing.* names.

fleet.label: t1-reporter-crit
fleet.topic: Track 1 adversarial critique of the frozen design: threshold-steepness separability in RBS-variant repressor gates (Cello UCF libraries)
fleet.summary: I recomputed every number the designer reported from the Cello UCF files and the arithmetic is almost all right; the one error is a count (10 strict calibration pairs, not 9). The design problems are elsewhere. (1) The 'untouched' holdout Eco1C2G2T2 is not independent: 15 of its 18 gates carry the same names as Eco1C1G1T1 and 13 have identical cassette part lists, so at least 9 of its 13 RBS-only pairs are the SAME constructs as the calibration pairs, re-measured in 2019 in REU instead of RPU (no parameter is byte-identical, so it is a re-measurement, not a copy). It tests measurement reproducibility, not generalisation. (2) P5 is refuted by the data already on disk: the single 'genuine' yeast pair (LexA) has different OUTPUT promoters (pLexA1 vs pLexA2, different sequences), so it is not translation-initiation-only; the in-scope yeast count is 0, not 1. (3) P2 is redundant with P1 and weak: S>=6 is only stricter than dn<=0.25 when Kfold<2.83, 48 percent of between-repressor pairs (where n is unrelated) pass it, and the Kfold>=2 side condition was added after seeing that calibration pair B2/B3 has S=5.00. (4) P3's r>=0.80 bar is vacuous: my refit gives r=0.972, but a refit with 0.5 noise on n would still give median r=0.87, and the pair-level dn values are NOT reproduced (r=0.086 across the 10 pairs). (5) The 'pure translation along log-x' story is contradicted by the data: ymax differs up to 1.74x and ymin up to 5.5x within RBS-only pairs, while only n is tested. (6) P4 and P6 are post-hoc, ill-posed or near-certain and should be dropped or demoted. Only P1 (re-expressed per family and in standard-error units) can really fail and is worth freezing. Caveat: I have now seen the calibration refit (P3 internal holdout is spent) and the holdout's structure (gate names, cassettes, output names) but no holdout n, K, ymax or ymin value.
fleet.lay_summary: A cell can be given a dimmer or brighter volume knob for one protein by swapping a tiny piece of DNA. The plan says that this swap slides the cell's on/off switch point but does not change how sharp the switch is. I checked the plan's numbers against the public data and they mostly add up. But the 'fresh' data set kept back for testing is mostly the same DNA constructs measured again, so it is like grading a student on the same questions with a new pen. One claim about yeast is wrong because the two yeast constructs differ in another part as well. Two of the six predictions are so loose that they would pass almost no matter what, so I recommend dropping them and keeping a tighter version of the first.

findings.claim: Yeast pairs with IDENTICAL cassettes still differ widely in fitted n (CI: 2.06 vs 3.08, dn 0.40; CI434: 3.86 vs 3.92) because the gates differ in output promoter. They are rightly out of scope, but they show that two nominally same-repressor yeast gates can differ in n by 40 percent when anything else changes, so no yeast number can be read as an RBS effect.

The 'pure translation along log-x' narrative in the design's one_paragraph is contradicted by the data it is tested on: within RBS-only pairs the fitted ymax differs by up to 1.74x (PhlF P1/P3), 2.38x (933W) and ymin by up to 3.0x in E. coli (QacR) and 5.5x in yeast. In the 10 calibration pairs 5 have a ymax ratio above 1.15 and 6 a ymin ratio of 2.0 or more. The frozen predictions test only n, and the proposed Lean theorem requires shared ymax, ymin AND n.
findings.value: calibration: 5/10 pairs ymax ratio >1.15; 6/10 ymin ratio >=2.0
findings.evidence_quote: Eco1C1G1T1 P1_PhlF/P3_PhlF ymax ratio 1.74 ymin ratio 2.00 kf 7.67 dn 0.049

findings.claim: The lemma 'equal n is EXACTLY equivalent to the two curves being log-translates' (design step 6) is only true when ymax and ymin are also equal. Equal n alone does not make two Hill curves log-translates. With shared ymax, ymin, n: y1(x*K1/K2) = ymin + (ymax-ymin)/(1+(x/K2)^n) = y2(x) (own algebra), and the empirical data above show ymax, ymin are not shared.
findings.evidence_quote: given two Hill transfer functions sharing ymax, ymin and n, the second is the first composed with a scaling of the input, y2(x) = y1(x * K1/K2)

findings.claim: P1 CAN fail against the right null. Taking pairs of gates from DIFFERENT repressors in Eco1C1G1T1 (n unrelated to RBS), 177 pairs, median dn 0.366, only 32.8 percent have dn<=0.25 and 46.3 percent exceed 0.40. With the P1 refutation rule, probability of refutation under that null is 0.897 (3 pairs), 0.960 (4), 0.994 (6), 1.000 (12). But under a calibration-like truth the rule never refutes (0.000) and under calibration+seen pooled pairs it falsely refutes 1.1 percent (3 pairs) to 17.0 percent (12 pairs): the false-alarm rate grows with the number of pairs.
findings.evidence_quote: cross-family pairs: 177, median dn 0.366, frac<=0.25: 0.328, frac<=0.1587: 0.203, frac>0.40: 0.463

findings.claim: P1 is not independent across pairs: a 3-gate family gives 3 correlated pairs and a 4-gate family 6. Counting pairs instead of families inflates the apparent sample; the Eco1C2G2T2 design has 13 pairs in only 4 families (PhlF 3, SrpR 6, BM3R1 3, AmeR 1) so 'two or more pairs fail' can be triggered by one bad gate (one outlier gate in SrpR with 5 members produces up to 4 failing pairs).
findings.evidence_quote: strict RBS-only pairs (same outputs): 13 gates: 18

findings.claim: P2 (S = log2(Kfold)/dn >= 6) is algebraically equivalent to dn <= log2(Kfold)/6, i.e. dn<=0.167 at Kfold=2, 0.220 at 2.5, 0.250 at 2.83, 0.333 at 4 and 0.500 at 8. It is stricter than P1 only for 2<=Kfold<2.83 and weaker than P1 for every larger Kfold, so it is largely redundant. Between-repressor pairs with Kfold>=2 (n unrelated) pass S>=6 in 48.1 percent of 108 cases (median S 5.45), and P2 refutes under that null only 53 percent (3 pairs) to 88 percent (8 pairs), weaker than P1.
findings.value: null pass fraction 0.481; P2 null power m=3 0.531, m=4 0.717, m=6 0.692, m=8 0.881
findings.evidence_quote: cross-family S (kf>=2): n=108, median 5.45, frac S>=6: 0.481

findings.claim: S is ill-conditioned: n is shipped to two significant figures in Eco1C1G1T1, so a shipped dn of 0.0000 has a rounding interval of [0, 0.029-0.036] and 0.1587 has [0.127, 0.191]. S = log2(Kfold)/dn is therefore infinite or arbitrary for 2 of 10 pairs, and the median of S is dominated by the rounding of n.

My log-space least-squares refit of Eco1C1G1T1 from the 12x250-bin cytometry histograms (per-level histogram median, 60 random starts, scipy 1.18.1) reproduces shipped n across the 20 gates at Pearson r = 0.972 (Spearman 0.934); the refit/shipped ratio lies between 0.76 and 1.15, so 0 gates fall outside a factor of 1.5; max refit dn over the 10 pairs is 0.1115 and none exceed 0.25. P3 as frozen would therefore PASS comfortably. Note this uses up P3 as a blind internal holdout.
findings.source: s3_refit.py and s4_refit_stats.py on Eco1C1G1T1.UCF.json cytometry tables
findings.evidence_quote: Pearson r (n refit vs shipped, 20 gates): 0.972 ... gates outside [1/1.5,1.5]: 0 ... max refit dn 0.1115; pairs >0.25: 0

findings.claim: P3's r>=0.80 bar is vacuous. Between-repressor spread of n is large (sd 0.84 over 20 gates), so even shipped n plus pure noise of sd 0.5 (19 percent of mean n) gives r = 0.872 median (5th percentile 0.779), and noise sd 1.0 still gives median 0.655. The relevant pair-level statistic does not reproduce: corr(shipped dn, refit dn) over the 10 pairs = 0.086, and the within-family correlation of centred n is 0.354.
findings.value: r(noise sd 0.5) median 0.872; pair-level r 0.086; within-family r 0.354
findings.evidence_quote: corr(ship dn, refit dn) over 10 pairs = 0.086

findings.claim: The shipped pair-to-pair n differences are within estimation noise: Jacobian standard errors of refit n are 0.03-0.24 (rms SE of a pair difference 0.258, about dn 0.098), the largest refit z for any of the 10 pairs is 1.90, and 0 of 10 exceed 2. Shipped dn rms is 0.091 against fit-noise rms dn 0.079. The data are consistent with true dn = 0 for every calibration pair. (SE from a local linearisation of 12 medians, so approximate.)
findings.value: max z 1.90; rms dn shipped 0.091; rms fit-SE of dn 0.079
findings.evidence_quote: max z refit = 1.90; pairs with z>2: 0 of 10

findings.claim: Detection power per pair is limited: with SE of a pair difference 0.258 and mean n 2.63, a true dn of 0.15 gives mean z 1.53 and only 32 percent chance of z>2; dn 0.25 gives 71 percent; dn 0.40 gives 98 percent. A bound of 0.25 is therefore a coarse test that cannot distinguish dn=0 from dn=0.15 pair by pair.

The cytometry-histogram bin axis is NOT on the shipped parameter scale, so the refit cannot recover ymax, ymin or K in shipped units. Fitted ymax is 3.7 times shipped on median (ship/fit ratio 0.12-0.40, not explained by the models' alpha parameter: correlation 0.111), and K_fit/K_ship has median 0.57 (0.42-1.49) though log K correlates at r=0.903. Kfold ordering within a pair reverses in 3 of 10 pairs (all with shipped Kfold<2). n is scale-free so P3 on n is unaffected, but a refit-based S or Kfold is not comparable with shipped values. I could not determine the cause.
findings.evidence_quote: K_fit/K_ship: median 0.57 min 0.42 max 1.49

findings.claim: The design's non-monotone-gate exclusion rule (step Day 2) as literally written would remove half the calibration data: the strict monotone-median criterion fails for 10 of 20 gates and leaves only 3 of 10 strict pairs with both gates monotone. Any exclusion rule needs a numeric noise tolerance fixed in advance.
findings.value: monotone gates 10/20; pairs with both monotone 3/10
findings.evidence_quote: gates with strictly monotone median: 10/20 ... strict pairs with both gates monotone: 3/10

findings.claim: P4's headline ordering (TetR 0.1587 < phage 0.2124 < yeast 0.2604) compares maxima over 10, 5 and 1 pairs from three libraries differing in host strain, year, lab pipeline and shipped precision (2 s.f. vs full precision). On the pairs themselves, a one-sided exact permutation test TetR(10 pairs) vs phage(5 pairs) on mean dn gives p = 136/3003 = 0.045, uncorrected for shared gates. Fold, library and precision are completely confounded; yeast contributes no pair after the output-promoter check.
findings.evidence_quote: TetR (n=10, mean 0.0731) vs phage (n=5, mean 0.1363): exact permutation one-sided p = 136/3003 = 0.0453

findings.claim: P4 as a holdout test is near-vacuous: P(max TetR dn in a new library > 0.2124) is 0.000 if new pairs are drawn from the calibration pool, and rises to 0.19 (3 pairs) / 0.34 (6) / 0.47 (9) / 0.56 (12) if drawn from calibration plus phage pairs. Its outcome depends mostly on the number of pairs, and since the holdout shares 9 pairs' constructs with calibration it mainly measures re-measurement noise.
findings.evidence_quote: P4 refutation (TetR max>0.2124) m=6: if TetR~calib pool 0.000 ; if TetR~calib+phage pool 0.338

findings.claim: P6 is near-certain and its threshold post hoc: the headers show different measurement units (Eco1C1G1T1 RPU vs Eco1C2G2T2 REU), so K values are not directly comparable by construction. Its threshold 4.333 is one of the calibration Kfold values; 'cross-library K ratio of a repressor' is undefined where a repressor has several RBS variants; and Eco2C1G3T1 contents are unverified (scout claim). It tests nothing about the law.
findings.source: Eco1C2G2T2 header (range request); design-reporter.json frozen_predictions P6
findings.evidence_quote: "signal_carrier_units": "REU"; Eco1C1G1T1: 'signal_carrier_units': 'RPUG'

findings.claim: Every threshold in the freeze was chosen after seeing data: 0.25 is placed between the calibration max 0.1587 and the seen-yeast value 0.2604; 6.0 is half of 12.01; Kfold>=2.0 was chosen after seeing both calibration and the seen libraries; 4.333 in P6 and 0.2124 in P4 are observed values. The designer discloses the Kfold choice and the seen libraries, but P1's 0.25 and P2's 6.0 are tuned using the library the designer calls 'calibration only'.
findings.evidence_quote: I chose 2.0 AFTER seeing both the calibration and the two seen libraries - a disclosed, not hidden, degree of freedom.

findings.claim: Lean registry check at law set 1.8.1 (read-only): lawsets/current.json names version 1.8.1; gene-regulatory-dynamics is still 1.0.0, status 'proposed' (lawset-1.8.1.json lines 184-189) with lean_ref.module = null; the 1.8.x changelog adds no Hill, repressor or reporter law. Repo-wide search for hill/cello/repressor/ultrasens finds only altitude-coupling, flying-fish audit and laws.json hits, none about gene circuits. The earlier law-mapper's conclusion (no Hill law) therefore still holds at 1.8.1 although it was derived at 1.6.0.

recommendations: Re-label Eco1C2G2T2 honestly as a REPLICATE re-measurement of 15 shared constructs. Its best use is a pre-registered replicate test: for the 15 shared gates, compare n_new with n_old and K_new with K_old (scale-free quantities first). That gives the missing noise floor of shipped n, which should set the P1 bound instead of a bound chosen from 0.1587 and 0.2604. Freeze that analysis before any n or K value from Eco1C2G2T2 is read.

For a genuinely independent test use constructs not in calibration: the Eco1C2G2T2 gates not shared (C1_CymR, V1_VanR, F2_AmeR: 3 of 18 names are new) are too few; the phage library Eco2C1G5T1 has been seen. State the honest conclusion in advance: no independent RBS-only holdout with enough pairs exists in the shipped UCFs, so the law is supported at replicate level only until new data (for example Bth1C1G1T1, if gate-repressor identity can be recovered from its paper) is scored.

Keep P1 only, restated: unit of analysis = repressor family (4 in the holdout), statistic = z=|n_a-n_b|/sqrt(se_a^2+se_b^2) from the refit with bootstrap standard errors, refute if 2 or more families contain a pair with z>2.5 or any pair has dn>0.40 with z>2.5. Under H0 (equal n) with 13 pairs the chance of at least 2 pairs with z>2.5 is 0.011; per-pair power is 0.52 at true dn 0.25 and 0.94 at 0.40 (own normal approximation). Report that detection of dn below about 0.15 is not possible with these data.

Drop P2, P4, P5 and P6 as predictions. Keep P5's correction (in-scope yeast pairs = 0 after an output-promoter check) and P4's table as descriptive findings. Add the output-promoter equality to the side condition and compare the full structure, not only the cassette.

Rewrite P3 as a method result without a pass line, or set a bar that can fail (for example: within-family centred-n correlation >= 0.8 and refit z-scores computed from bootstrap SE, with a stated tolerance for non-monotone medians). Do not claim that agreement tests the biology: shipped n and refit n come from the same histograms. Note that my run has already unblinded P3, so any new P3 should use a different library or a different fit specification fixed before running.

Add the invariants the narrative needs or remove the narrative: either a prediction on ymax and ymin ratios (data show 5 of 10 calibration pairs with ymax ratio above 1.15 and 6 of 10 with ymin ratio at or above 2.0), or restate the law as 'n is preserved within noise; ymax, ymin and K are not'. Correct the Lean lemma statement to require shared ymax, ymin and n before 'iff log-translate'.
Fix the pair count (10 not 9) and report S only for pairs whose dn exceeds the rounding interval, or drop S entirely.
Registry: gene-regulatory-dynamics is unchanged at law set 1.8.1, so propose the successor against 1.8.1 (the earlier law-mapper worked from 1.6.0 and its conclusion stands).

glossary.plain: The short DNA stretch that sets how often the cell's protein-making machinery starts reading a gene; a stronger one means more protein.
A number saying how sharp an on/off switch is; a larger n means a steeper switch.
The input level at which the switch is halfway between off and on.
The size of the difference between two n values, as a fraction of their average.
How many times bigger the larger threshold is than the smaller one.
How many doublings of threshold shift one gets for each unit of change in steepness; made up by the designer.
Data kept unseen so that a prediction made beforehand can truly be tested.
A data file in which the Cello design software stores the measured parts and gates of a circuit library.
Relative promoter units and relative expression units: two scales used to compare gene activity with a reference.
Redoing the curve fitting from the raw measurements instead of trusting the published fitted numbers.
How many times larger a measured difference is than its estimated uncertainty.
The DNA switch that the repressor protein acts on; if it differs between two gates, they are not a clean comparison.

I did read its header, gate names, groups, cassette part lists and output-promoter names, and counted exact parameter equality (0 of 15), which now taints any claim that it was 'not opened'.

I could not explain why the cytometry histogram bin axis is on a different scale from the shipped ymax, ymin and K (ship/fit ratio 0.12-0.40, not the models' alpha), nor why shipped K is about 1.75x the refit K; the Cello fitting code and the Nielsen supplement were not read.

fleet.topic: Track 1 data and reproducibility: Cello UCF libraries for threshold-steepness separability
fleet.summary: Downloaded three Cello UCF libraries (Eco1C1G1T1 4,834,067 B; Eco2C1G5T1 46,518 B; SC1C1G1T1 1,744,232 B; git blob SHA-1 of each matches GitHub's tree listing) and ran analyse.py and refit.py. All design-reporter pair numbers reproduced exactly (BM3R1 dn 0.1587, S 12.01; 6 pairs with Kfold>=2; phage 933W dn 0.2124 S 6.74; yeast LexA dn 0.2604 S 4.68; SrpR S1 terminator differs; yeast CI/CI434 cassettes identical). One count differs: the design says 9 strict calibration pairs but its own list, and the data, give 10. A first run of the P3 cytometry refit (not previously reported) gives Pearson r = 0.972 between refit and shipped n, max refit dn 0.1115, and finds 10 of 20 gates with small non-monotone upticks at the highest input levels, which the design's day-2 exclusion rule would have dropped. Holdout libraries Eco1C2G2T2, Eco2C1G3T1 and Bth1C1G1T1 were deliberately NOT downloaded by me; only sizes and blob SHAs from the GitHub tree are recorded.
fleet.lay_summary: Synthetic biologists build tiny genetic switches that turn a gene off when another is on, like a dimmer that goes from bright to dark as you turn a knob. Two numbers describe each dimmer: where the knob must sit for the light to halve, and how sharply it flips. An earlier team claimed you can change the first number a lot without changing the second, by tweaking only one DNA 'volume dial' on the switch. I downloaded the public tables of measured switches and re-ran the sums. Every pair-by-pair number the earlier team quoted came out the same, except they counted nine matching pairs where there are really ten. I also re-estimated the sharpness myself from the raw cell measurements, and it agreed closely with the published values.

glossary.plain: A smooth S-shaped curve that describes how an output falls (or rises) as an input grows.
The input level at which the output is half way between its high and low values.
How abruptly the curve flips; bigger n is a sharper switch.
A short DNA stretch that sets how strongly a gene is turned into protein.
A JSON file that lists the parts and measured switch curves of a Cello library.
A genetic switch where one protein shuts off a gene's output.
A fingerprint of a file; any change to the file changes it.
A number from -1 to 1 saying how closely two lists of numbers rise and fall together.
Relative difference in steepness between two gates: |n1-n2| divided by their average.
How many times bigger the larger threshold is than the smaller.
The separability index log2(Kfold)/dn: octaves of threshold shift per unit of steepness drift.
Data kept unseen until the test is frozen so it cannot be tuned to.

fleet.label: t1-reporter-deep
fleet.topic: Track 1 deep literature: threshold-steepness separability in translation-initiation-variant repressor gates (Cello gate libraries)
fleet.summary:
STATE OF THE ART, built from the ground up. Each step is tagged [measured], [derived] or [assumed].

1. A gene is read in two steps. DNA is copied into messenger RNA (transcription) and the ribosome reads the RNA to make protein (translation). A ribosome binding site (RBS), the stretch of RNA just before the protein-coding part, controls how often ribosomes start. [measured] Shine and Dalgarno 1974 showed the ribosomal RNA end can pair with a conserved sequence in ribosome binding sites. Salis 2009: a model of RBS sequence predicted protein output within a factor of 2.3 over a 100,000-fold range for more than 100 designs; Espah Borujeni 2014: initiation rate follows binding free energy log-linearly and 5' structure moves it over 100-fold.

2. A repressor gate. A repressor protein sits on a promoter and blocks transcription of a reporter. More input promoter activity makes more repressor, so reporter output falls. [measured] The shipped curves (Cello UCF files) have the form y = ymin + (ymax - ymin)/(1 + (x/K)^n), x and y in relative promoter units (RPU, a ratio to promoter BBa_J23101). K is the input giving half-maximum output (the threshold); n is the steepness; ymax and ymin are the ON and OFF levels.

3. What n means. [derived/contested] The Hill form is a curve fit. Weiss 1997: the exponent is an interaction coefficient and equals the binding-site count only under strong cooperativity. TetR-family gates mostly show n about 2 (a dimer on one operator); some show n up to 6.1 [measured, Stanton 2014]. Steeper responses can also come from other mechanisms such as zero-order ultrasensitivity (Goldbeter-Koshland 1981) or repressor titration (Brewster 2014), which couple position and steepness.

4. Why an RBS change should move K but not n. [assumed] Repressor level R is proportional to (input promoter activity x) times (a translation multiplier c set by the RBS); promoter occupancy is a Hill function of R; dilution and degradation are linear; nothing else changes. [derived] Then y_c(x) = y_1(c x), K -> K/c, and n, ymax, ymin are untouched (checked numerically in translation_law.py). This is the claim 'threshold and steepness are separable design axes'. The reviews (Brophy and Voigt 2014) say RBS changes the threshold and that cooperativity or DNA looping is a different knob; they do not state exact n invariance, and I found no paper that tests it directly.

5. What the Cello data show. [measured, by me from the shipped files] Cassette = ribozyme insulator, RBS, repressor, terminator. Among pairs of gates with the same repressor that differ at exactly one position, being an RBS and moving K at least 2-fold: Eco1C1G1T1 has 6, max relative n difference dn = 0.1587; Eco1C2G2T2 has 9, max 0.2836 (shipped parameters); the phage-repressor set has 5, max 0.2124; yeast has 1, dn 0.2604. The earlier SrpR 'RBS-only family of 4' in Eco1C1G1T1 is not RBS-only: S1 differs from S2 to S4 also in terminator. Re-fitting the raw cytometry histograms reproduces shipped n in Eco1C1G1T1 (r = 0.977) but in Eco1C2G2T2 the answer depends on the fitting loss: a robust fit gives max dn 0.4254 and three of nine pairs above 0.25. Also ymin changes 1.5 to 2.2 fold (median) and ymax 1.1 to 1.2 fold (median) inside these pairs, so an RBS swap is not a pure sideways shift of the whole curve.

6. Why the data are less decisive than they look. [measured] The RBS in each library was picked by screening for dynamic range (Stanton 2014), so the variants are survivors. Shipped parameters are rounded to 2 significant figures. The Eco1C2G2T2 library was already summarised by the earlier scout, so it is not an untouched test set. Kosuri 2013: translation affects mRNA stability, and protein is within 2-fold of a multiplicative model only 64% of the time (worst 5% off by 13-fold), so promoter and RBS effects are not exactly independent.

7. Order of the key experiments: Shine-Dalgarno 1974; Goldbeter-Koshland 1981; Lutz-Bujard 1997; toggle switch and repressilator 2000; directed evolution of a circuit 2002; single-cell regulation function and noise 2005; combinatorial promoters 2007; RBS Calculator and RPU 2009; bicistronic elements, composability library and TetR-homolog gates 2013; circuit-design review 2014; Cello 2016; yeast and Bacteroides Cello 2020; Cello 2.0 protocol 2022. Best reviews: Brophy and Voigt 2014 (10.1038/nmeth.2926), Ferrell and Ha 2014 (10.1016/j.tibs.2014.08.003), Weiss 1997 (10.1096/fasebj.11.11.9285481).

8. Open problems. (a) No published direct test of n invariance under RBS-only change with matched cassettes and raw single-cell data. (b) Which fit gives the truth for Eco1C2G2T2. (c) Whether ymin/ymax drift is basal-leak physics or a measurement floor. (d) Eukaryotes: only one genuine one-position yeast pair. (e) The law library (set 1.8.1, 59 laws) still has no Hill or reporter law; gene-regulatory-dynamics is an empty placeholder.
fleet.lay_summary: A gene can be thought of as a dimmer switch: the more signal comes in, the lower the output light of a gate falls, along an S-shaped curve. Two numbers describe the S: where it bends (the threshold) and how sharply it bends (the steepness). Engineers can weaken or strengthen the 'start here' site that tells the cell's protein-making machines how often to read a repressor gene. Simple arithmetic says that should slide the S left or right without changing its sharpness, like sliding a ruler along a table. In the public data from the Cello gate libraries, that is roughly true for many gates but not exactly: the sharpness drifts by up to about a quarter in some pairs and the top and bottom of the curve also move. Whether the sharpness stays put is still an open question, because one of the datasets gives different answers depending on how the curve is fitted.

findings.claim: Cello NOT/NOR repressor gates are built so that the only handle for tuning each gate's repressor level is the RBS; the input promoter is fixed so inputs can be swapped.
findings.evidence_quote: we define the beginning of each gate to be the transcription start site and vary the repressor level by changing the strength of the RBS.

findings.claim: In Stanton et al. the RBS of each repressor was chosen by screening an RBS library and keeping the variant with the highest dynamic range (a selection step; RBS libraries built for 19 of 20 gates).
findings.evidence_quote: These libraries were screened and the RBS that produced the highest dynamic range was selected

findings.claim: Stanton et al. fit every gate response to a Hill function and define K as the input at which output is half-maximal.
findings.evidence_quote: K is the threshold level of input where the output is half-maximal.

findings.claim: Cooperativity of most TetR-family gates is about 2, consistent with dimers binding one operator; five repressors gave n > 3, the largest 6.1 (Orf2).
findings.evidence_quote: The cooperativity for the majority of gates is n ≈ 2, which is consistent with that measured for TetR, and a mechanism of dimers binding to a single operator

findings.claim: 16 of 73 mined TetR-family repressors were orthogonal and repressed their cognate promoter 5- to 207-fold.
findings.evidence_quote: 16 were identified that both strongly repress their cognate promoter (5- to 207-fold) and exhibit minimal interactions with other promoters.

findings.claim: Brophy and Voigt (review): a stronger or weaker RBS changes the threshold of a gate; multiple operators or operator position are other threshold knobs.
findings.evidence_quote: Selecting a stronger or weaker RBS, adding multiple operators, or changing operator positions within the repressible promoter can change the threshold

findings.claim: Brophy and Voigt define a gate response by three parameters: dynamic range, threshold, cooperativity.
findings.evidence_quote: the amount of input required to reach the half-maximum output (also referred to as the threshold), and 3. cooperativity of the switch

findings.claim: Brophy and Voigt: threshold mismatches between connected gates can be corrected by parts (for example mutated RBSs) that shift individual gate thresholds.
findings.evidence_quote: Connectivity mismatches can be corrected by selecting parts that shift the thresholds of individual gates.

findings.claim: Cello 1 (Nielsen 2016) designed 60 E. coli circuits; 45 worked in every output state and 92% of all output states matched prediction.
findings.evidence_quote: Of these, 45 circuits performed correctly in every output state (up to 10 regulators and 55 parts), and across all circuits 92% of the output states functioned as predicted.

findings.claim: Yeast Cello gates (Chen 2020): nine NOT/NOR gates with near-identical response functions and 400-fold dynamic range.
findings.evidence_quote: we constructed nine NOT/NOR gates with nearly identical response functions and 400-fold dynamic range.

findings.claim: The Bacteroides thetaiotaomicron Cello library is based on dCas9 sgRNA NOT/NOR gates, not protein repressors with RBS tuning, so it cannot test an RBS law.
findings.evidence_quote: we characterize a set of genome-integrated NOT/NOR gates based on single guide RNAs (CRISPR-dCas9) to inform a Bt user constraint file (UCF) for Cello.

findings.claim: Relative Promoter Unit (RPU): activity relative to reference promoter BBa_J23101; cut variation across labs and instruments by about 50%. It is the unit of x and y in Cello Hill fits.
findings.evidence_quote: We defined a Relative Promoter Unit (RPU) in order to report promoter characterization data in compatible units

findings.claim: Shine and Dalgarno (1974) showed the 3' end of E. coli 16S rRNA can pair with a conserved sequence in ribosome binding sites; this is the physical basis of an RBS.
findings.evidence_quote: The sequence A-C-C-U-C-C could recognize a conserved sequence found in the ribosome binding sites of various coliphage mRNAs

findings.claim: The RBS Calculator predicts protein output from RBS sequence on a proportional scale; over 100 predictions were accurate within a factor of 2.3 across a 100,000-fold range.
findings.evidence_quote: Experimental validation of over 100 predictions in Escherichia coli shows that the method is accurate to within a factor of 2.3 over a range of 100,000-fold.

findings.claim: The same RBS sequence in a different genetic context can give a different expression level (context dependence of an RBS change).
findings.evidence_quote: The design method also correctly predicts that reusing a ribosome binding site sequence in different genetic contexts can result in different protein expression levels.

findings.claim: Translation initiation rate relates to ribosome-mRNA binding free energy by a log-linear formula, fluorescence tracked initiation rate in steady-state growth, and 5' structure/standby sites modulate initiation over 100-fold.
findings.evidence_quote: fluorescence levels are proportional to translation initiation rates under our controlled growth conditions

findings.claim: Bicistronic-design translation elements gave arbitrary genes expression within twofold of target about 93% of the time (1000-fold range): RBS context dependence can be engineered down.
findings.evidence_quote: arbitrary genes are reliably expressed to within twofold relative target expression windows with ∼93% reliability.

findings.claim: In a 12,563-construct promoter x RBS library, protein was within twofold of a simple multiplicative model 64% of the time (RNA 80%) but the worst 5% deviated 13-fold on average. Promoter and RBS effects are close to, not exactly, separable.
findings.evidence_quote: RNA and protein expression were within twofold of expected levels 80% and 64% of the time, respectively.

findings.claim: Kosuri: translation rate affects mRNA stability, so an RBS change can alter transcript level as well as translation.
findings.evidence_quote: The large dataset allowed quantitation of global effects, such as translation rate on mRNA stability and mRNA secondary structure on translation rate.

findings.claim: The Hill coefficient is an 'interaction' coefficient, not a count of binding sites, except under marked positive cooperativity; the Hill equation is not a physical reaction scheme for multi-site binding.
findings.evidence_quote: only under the very specific condition of marked positive cooperativity does the Hill coefficient accurately estimate the number of binding sites.

findings.claim: Hill form Output = Input^n/(K^n + Input^n); hemoglobin has an apparent Hill coefficient of 2.7 (textbook sigmoid).
findings.evidence_quote: in reality the binding curve is sigmoidal with an apparent Hill coefficient of 2.7

findings.claim: Goldbeter and Koshland 1981: covalent-modification cycles operated away from first-order kinetics give amplification equivalent to allosteric proteins with high Hill coefficients (a way to get steepness without cooperative binding).
findings.evidence_quote: This amplification of the response to a stimulus can provide additional sensitivity in biological control, equivalent to that of allosteric proteins with high Hill coefficients.

findings.claim: Repressor titration by competing binding sites both shifts and sharpens the transition of a regulated gene against repressor copy number: a mechanism coupling threshold and steepness (counter to separability).
findings.evidence_quote: The stronger binding sites shift and sharpen the transition of the gene of interest with respect to LacI copy number.

findings.claim: The gene regulation function fluctuates in single cells, limiting signal transfer accuracy: a population Hill curve hides single-cell variation.
findings.evidence_quote: fluctuates dynamically in individual living cells, thereby limiting the accuracy with which transcriptional genetic circuits can transfer signals.

findings.claim: Noise in a gene has intrinsic, upstream-transmitted and global parts, so output noise is not fixed by the mean transfer curve.
findings.evidence_quote: noise in a gene was determined by its intrinsic fluctuations, transmitted noise from upstream genes, and global noise affecting all genes.

findings.claim: Early synthetic circuits: the toggle switch showed a 'nearly ideal switching threshold'.
findings.evidence_quote: exhibits a nearly ideal switching threshold.

findings.claim: Repressilator (three repressors) oscillated with periods of hours, slower than the cell cycle.
findings.evidence_quote: The resulting oscillations, with typical periods of hours, are slower than the cell-division cycle

findings.claim: Directed evolution turned a non-functional circuit with mismatched components into a functional one and produced a library of devices with a range of behaviours.
findings.evidence_quote: a nonfunctional circuit containing improperly matched components can evolve rapidly into a functional one.

findings.claim: Combinatorial promoter libraries (288 promoters, up to 3 TF inputs) spanned five decades of promoter strength.
findings.evidence_quote: we observed varied promoter strength over five decades.

findings.claim: The PLtetO-1 promoter regulated expression over up to 5000-fold with aTc, an early well-controlled inducible input.
findings.evidence_quote: The novel promoter PLtetO-1 allows the regulation of gene expression over an up to 5000-fold range with anhydrotetracycline (aTc)

findings.claim: The Cello UCF response function is the four-parameter Hill form with linear input composition x = x1 + x2.
findings.evidence_quote: ymin + (ymax - ymin) / (1.0 + (x / K)^n)

findings.claim: Each Eco1C1G1T1 gate cassette is [ribozyme insulator, RBS, repressor CDS, terminator]; for A1_AmtR: BydvJ, A1, AmtR, L3S2P55. Variant names (A1, B1..B3, P1..P3, Q1, Q2, S1..S4) are RBS parts, so RBS-only variants can be tested from the part list.
findings.evidence_quote: "name": "A1_AmtR_cassette", "components": [ "BydvJ", "A1", "AmtR", "L3S2P55" ]

findings.claim: Eco1C1G1T1 is a library of TetR homologs.
findings.evidence_quote: TetR homologs: PhlF, SrpR, BM3R1, HlyIIR, BetI, AmtR, AmeR, QacR, IcaRA, LitR, PsrA, LmrA

findings.claim: Eco1C1G1T1: 20 gates, shipped n 1.4 to 4.2, K 0.01 to 0.41 RPU (41-fold span of thresholds across gates).

Eco1C1G1T1 same-regulator pairs: 13 pairs; 10 differ in exactly one cassette position that is an RBS; 3 (all S1_SrpR vs S2/S3/S4) differ in RBS and terminator (ECK120019600 vs ECK120029600). Of the 10, 6 move K by at least 2-fold (in scope). Max relative n difference dn = |n1-n2|/mean(n) over all 13 = 0.1587 (BM3R1 B1/B2 and B2/B3, n 3.4 vs 2.9).

Eco1C2G2T2: all 13 same-regulator pairs differ at one RBS position; 9 have Kfold >= 2; max dn among those 9 is 0.2836 (BM3R1 B1/B2, Kfold 10.34); over all 13 the max is 0.2911 (PhlF P2/P3, Kfold 1.76, out of scope). One in-scope pair exceeds 0.25.
Eco2C1G5T1 (phage repressors): 5 in-scope RBS pairs, max dn 0.2124 (933W R8/R9, Kfold 2.70); Kfold up to 14.8 (P2 R13/R15, dn 0.053).

SC1C1G1T1 (yeast): only 1 pair is a one-position translation-initiation change (LexA Kozak24 vs Kozak14, Kfold 2.33, dn 0.2604). The CI and CI434 pairs have identical cassettes yet dn 0.397 and 0.015, so they differ outside the cassette and do not test translation alone.
Eco2C1G3T1 has 6 gates and no same-regulator pair, so it cannot test an RBS law.

Refit of Hill parameters from the shipped 12 x 250-bin cytometry histograms (median of each histogram, log10 least squares, 4 free parameters) reproduces the shipped values for Eco1C1G1T1: Pearson r of n = 0.977, of log K = 0.903; max refit dn over 6 in-scope pairs = 0.1153.

The same refit on Eco1C2G2T2 depends on the loss. Plain least squares gives r(n)=0.70 and max dn 1.13 because one input level (x=0.0697 in S2_SrpR) is listed out of order with an output that belongs with the highest inputs. A robust soft-L1 fit gives r(n)=0.919, r(logK)=0.987, but max refit dn 0.4254 (S1/S4 SrpR) with 3 of 9 pairs above 0.25, against 0.2836 maximum from shipped parameters. Steepness invariance in Eco1C2G2T2 is therefore fit-dependent; no ground truth was found to decide.
findings.value: shipped max dn 0.2836; robust refit max 0.4254

findings.claim: Inside in-scope RBS pairs, shipped ymax changes by a median 1.11x (max 1.74x) in Eco1C1G1T1 and 1.20x (max 2.32x) in Eco1C2G2T2; shipped ymin by a median 2.17x (max 3.00x) and 1.49x (max 3.21x). An RBS change is therefore not a pure shift of the whole curve: floor and ceiling move too.

Shipped parameters are rounded (n to 2 significant figures, K sometimes 0.01), so small dn and large K folds at low K are quantisation-limited; refit K folds are often smaller than shipped ones (BM3R1 B1/B3 shipped 6.5, refit 3.06).

If repressor level is R = c*x (c = RBS translation multiplier) and promoter output is a Hill function of R, then y_c(x) = y_1(c*x): K = K_R/c with n, ymax and ymin unchanged. Numerical check: fitted K = K0/c and n = 2.8 for c = 0.25, 2, 10.
findings.source: derived and numerically checked: translation_law.py part 1

findings.claim: In law set 1.8.1 (59 laws) the only gene-regulation law is the placeholder gene-regulatory-dynamics v1.0.0 (status proposed, class gap, no Lean module or theorem).
findings.evidence_quote: "label": "Gene regulatory dynamics (not formalised)"

findings.claim: The repo states that the Hill equation is not formalised; Altitude.lean uses only monotonicity of a Hill curve. No Lean file in lean/Delphi is named for Hill, reporter or gene regulation.
findings.evidence_quote: Arterial content nondecreasing in partial pressure (a Hill curve is, but the Hill equation, the Bohr shift and the Root effect are not formalised).

key_claims.claim: In Cello-style repressor gates the repressor level is set by choosing the RBS (the input promoter is fixed), so an RBS swap is the designed way to move the threshold.
key_claims.source: https://doi.org/10.1038/nchembio.1411 (PMC4165527 full text, fetched via NCBI efetch 2026-11-12)
key_claims.evidence_quote: we define the beginning of each gate to be the transcription start site and vary the repressor level by changing the strength of the RBS.

key_claims.claim: Under the assumptions that repressor level is proportional to input times an RBS multiplier and occupancy is a Hill function of repressor, an RBS change rescales K by 1/c and leaves n, ymax, ymin unchanged (derived, not measured).

In the shipped Eco1C1G1T1 library the largest relative n difference among same-repressor pairs is 0.1587, while Eco1C2G2T2 reaches 0.2836 in an in-scope pair, and a robust refit of its raw histograms gives up to 0.4254; invariance of n is approximate and fit-dependent.
key_claims.source: computed from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CIDARLAB/Cello-v2-1-Core/main/library/constraints/Eco1C1G1T1.UCF.json and Eco1C2G2T2.UCF.json (sha256 in data/t1-deep/SHA256.txt) by pairs.py and refit.py
key_claims.evidence_quote: ymin + (ymax - ymin) / (1.0 + (x / K)^n)

key_claims.claim: An RBS swap is not a pure translation of the whole curve: in-scope pairs show median ymin changes of 2.17x (Eco1C1G1T1) and 1.49x (Eco1C2G2T2).
key_claims.source: computed by translation_law.py part 2 from the same UCF files

could_not_find: No paper was found that tests directly whether the Hill coefficient is preserved under RBS-only changes of a repressor gate. Statements that RBS shifts the threshold come from reviews and design papers (Stanton 2014, Brophy and Voigt 2014); invariance of n is my analysis of shipped parameters.

The Nielsen 2016 Science paper and its supplement were not retrievable as full text (paywalled; not in Europe PMC open access); only the abstract was read. Same for Mutalik 2013, Weiss 1997, Rosenfeld 2005, Pedraza 2005, Elowitz 2000, Gardner 2000, Chen 2020, Jones 2022 (abstract only). Their cited numbers come from abstracts.
Stanton 2014 supplementary tables 3-5 (RBS libraries, selected RBS, fitted parameters) were not fetched; I could not read the figure of per-gate dynamic range from the supplement.

RBS Calculator predictions for the RBS sequences in the UCF libraries were not computed (the tool is not installed locally and was not run), so I cannot say whether K fold tracks predicted translation-rate fold; this is the most direct available test of c in K -> K/c.

I could not decide which fit of Eco1C2G2T2 is right: shipped parameters (max dn 0.2836) or a robust refit of the histograms (max 0.4254). At least one input level in S2_SrpR is listed out of order with a suspicious output; I did not investigate the other 17 gates by hand.
Bth1C1G1T1 was not downloaded (15 MB, sgRNA gates, repressor identities unclear); Eco2C1G3T1 has no usable pair. The yeast arm has one true pair, so it supports no conclusion about eukaryotes.
Whether the original authors fitted Hill parameters themselves or the Cello toolchain re-derived them was not determined; I did not read the Cello fitting code.
OpenAlex was not used (budget exhausted). No Lean was run. The law library is unchanged: no Hill or reporter law exists in set 1.8.1.

Eco1C2G2T2 had already been summarised by the earlier scout (family K folds and n CVs), so it is not an untouched holdout for any prediction frozen after that scout run; the orchestrator should decide whether the pre-registration is affected.
recommendations: Do not freeze 'n is invariant under RBS-only change' with a single numeric bound on shipped parameters: the bound that holds in Eco1C1G1T1 (0.1587) already fails by the shipped numbers in Eco1C2G2T2 (0.2836) and by robust refit (0.4254). Freeze the refit procedure (loss function, treatment of out-of-order input levels) before looking at holdout numbers.

State the law as the derived translation identity y_c(x) = y_1(c x) with named hypotheses (R proportional to c*x, occupancy Hill in R, linear loss) and test ymin and ymax separately; ymin moved by a median 1.5 to 2.2x.
Use only the 6 + 9 + 5 + 1 genuinely one-position RBS pairs; exclude the SrpR S1 pairs (terminator also differs) and the yeast CI and CI434 pairs (no cassette difference).

If a real test is wanted, compute RBS Calculator predicted translation-rate ratios for each pair and check Kfold against them; and look for a second source of raw single-cell data with RBS-only variants.
Add a Hill-function module and reporter steady-state law to lean/Delphi as the earlier law-mapper proposed; the 1.8.1 registry still has only the empty gene-regulatory-dynamics placeholder.

fleet.topic: Track 1 law map against law set 1.8.1, with a checked Lean law (Hill gate threshold-steepness separability)

It contains no law about gene-regulatory input-output maps: the only entry is the placeholder gene-regulatory-dynamics (module and theorem null). I wrote and checked HillSeparability.lean: for a Cello-form Hill repressor gate, rescaling K is exactly a translation of the input on the log axis (n untouched), the threshold fold is K2/K1 at every activation level, and the 10-to-90 percent input span is 81^(1/n) independent of K. check.sh: errors=0, sorryAx=0, 8/8 axiom lines. fleet.lay_summary: The project keeps a library of computer-checked biology rules. I searched it for rules about a gene switch that turns a reporter protein up or down and found none: the one entry is an empty placeholder. I then wrote and machine-checked a small new rule. A gene switch has a midpoint (how much input flips it) and a steepness (how sharply it flips). The rule proves that moving the midpoint just slides the whole curve sideways on a logarithmic ruler and leaves the steepness exactly as it was. Think of sliding a ruler along a table: the markings stay the same distance apart. Whether real engineered switches behave this way is a lab question the proof does not settle.
