bm-4d-printing-review.overall: Three of four key claims reproduce against primary text. The fourth, the slow-and-weak generalisation, is a mix of reproduced numbers and a judgment. The 'none found' proof-assistant gap is an absence claim I did not test.

claims.claim: A vat-photopolymer (SLA/DLP) humidity-actuated 4D part has been published (Small 2024, PEG-polyurethane ink, film folds in under 1 s, 50 um film over 5x faster than 150 um, lifts 50 mg); not a Formlabs resin and no Timoshenko analysis.
claims.source_says: Like a cantilever beam, the film rapidly initiated folding in less than 1s. A film having 50 μm thickness folded over 5 times faster compared to a film of around 150 μm thickness
claims.note: Full text (PMC10922657) confirms the 1 s fold, the 5x thickness effect, the 50 mg/5x load at RH~90%, SLA 400 nm and DLP 380 nm printing, and zero 'Timoshenko' hits; 'not Formlabs' and 'contradicts the earlier gap' are the agent's framing.

claims.claim: The 'stock Formlabs resins gain under 1 percent in 24 h' statement is method-dependent: Flexible 80A V2 gains +8% mass and +3% volume in 1 day in water (ASTM D471 slab); Elastic 50A V2 39.2% IPA vs Rigid 10K under 0.1% is confirmed.
claims.source_says: Flexible 80A V2 TDS, Deionized Water, 1 day: -26 hardness, +8% mass, +3% volume (1 week: -27, +9%, +7%). Solvent page: Elastic 50A Resin V2 IPA 39.2, water 0.7 (24 h weight gain); Rigid 10K <0.1.
claims.note: I read the datasheet page as an image and mapped the solvent-page columns (IPA 10th, water 18th); all numbers reproduce.

claims.claim: No hygromorph/bilayer design constrained by a proof-assistant-checked law was found; arXiv 2604.26367 is 'verified' only in a category-theoretic sense, applies the Timoshenko formula to an FFF polyamide bilayer (36.4 vs 35.3 +/- 3.1 deg), and never mentions Lean, Coq or Isabelle.
claims.source_says: Here we present a category theoretic compositional framework for verified nature-derived design. Baseline (hygroscopic / bending) n=3 Predicted 36.4° Measured 35.3 ± 3.1° 3.0%
claims.note: The preprint parts reproduce (0 hits for Lean, Coq, Isabelle, proof assistant; FFF, PA6-GF/PA612-CF, Timoshenko formula present), but 'none found anywhere' is a search-absence claim I did not independently test.

claims.claim: Humidity-driven polymer actuators are slow and weak compared with thermal SMPs/LCEs: hydrogel forces under 1 N, cellulose-filled FFF bilayers 30 min for full transformation, thin wood 24 h, thick timber about 400 h.
claims.source_says: The bilayers reach a full transformation between two RH extremes of 30% and 90% within 30 minutes. [hydrogel review] swelling and contraction forces for most hydrogel actuators are less than 1 N
claims.note: The individual numbers check out against the Cheng, Chau/Amstad, Rueggeberg and Groenquist texts, but the sweeping 'slow and weak vs thermal' comparison is a judgment, and the same agent's Small 2024 film folds in under 1 s.

bm-architecture-gaps.overall: Three of four key claims rest on passages I found verbatim in the sources. The Freiburg and embodied-carbon claims are supported. The Flexible 80A V2 swelling numbers reproduce exactly from the PDF. The mycelium claim is overgeneralised beyond what the sources say. Exclusivity and absence-of-evidence parts were not verified.

claims.claim: The best passive bio-based skin (Freiburg) has no building-performance number and a short durability record, so the open gap is geometry to solar gain and cycle life.
claims.source_says: it will be important to quantify the improvement of indoor climate regulation in future work. ... The number of cycles tested is still small compared to the entire lifetime of a building
claims.note: Both passages are in PMC11604995; 'best' is the agent's judgement and the gap framing is inference, but the factual parts check out.

claims.claim: Flexible 80A V2 shows +8 percent mass and +3 percent volume after 1 day in water (immersion), contradicting 'under 1 percent'; it is the only catalogue resin with enough swelling for a hygromorph layer; humid-air constants unpublished.
claims.source_says: Deionized Water: 1 day -26 (Shore A) +8% mass +3% volume 94% elongation 89% tensile; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%. Slabs fully immersed, wiped dry.
claims.note: The datasheet numbers reproduce from word coordinates, but 'only catalogue resin' and 'humid-air unpublished' were not shown (the cube table has no V2 row; the old Flexible 80A reads 0.7).

claims.claim: Mycelium and other living or fungal materials lack a verified reaction-to-fire class and are TRL 3-5 beyond insulation and packaging, so are the wrong first target for a small computational team.
claims.source_says: Full-scale testing in accordance with the BS EN 13501-1 standard is rarely used for MBCs ... Most MBC research currently resides between TRL 3 and TRL 5 ... (insulation/packaging TRL 7-9)
claims.note: Sources support 'rarely tested' and TRL 3-5 for mycelium composites, not a blanket 'no verified class' or any claim on other living materials; 'wrong first target' is a judgement.

claims.claim: Embodied-carbon data are missing for most emerging structural materials, so a transparent carbon sheet for the proof of concept is a real computation-only contribution.
claims.source_says: Only 18% (37 out of 204) of the emerging structural materials reviewed had EC values; less (11%) had embodied energy values.
claims.note: The 18 percent figure is verbatim in PMC13068519 (so 82 percent lack values); the 'real contribution' conclusion is the agent's opinion.

bm-bilayer-theory-verified.overall: The four key claims largely hold. Timoshenko eq.(4), the plate substitution and the sag < h/2 limit, the R&M and Aniskevich numbers, the Pezzulla (1+nu) result and the 3/2 identity all reproduce. The strip/plate boundary values (2.0 and 4.2 sqrt(h/kappa)) are the agent's own derivations. I did not re-check Alben's model, the FFC preprint, or R&M's equation images.

claims.claim: Project f(m,n) is Timoshenko's eq.(4) (also R&M, FFC with E->E/(1-nu)); narrow-strip assumptions; Timoshenko 1925 does not state the ceiling 3/2 or optimum m^2n=1; identity 3/2 - f = 3(m^2n-1)^2/(2(...)).
claims.source_says: the following general equation for the curvature of a bi-metal strip will be obtained, 1/p = 6(a2-a1)(t-t0)(1+m)^2 / h(3(1+m)^2+(1+mn)(m^2+1/(mn))). Search of pp.233-242 text found no 'optimum'/'best'.
claims.note: Eq.(4) reads as stated and the identity reproduces numerically; I searched only PDF pages 41-51 for optimum, and did not open R&M's equation images or the FFC preprint.

claims.claim: For a wide plate Timoshenko substitutes E/(1-nu), f unchanged (sphere, sag < h/2); beyond bifurcation curvature is (1+nu) times strip value (cylinder), D_c about 4.2 sqrt(h/kappa); strip safe below about 2 sqrt(h/kappa).
claims.source_says: substitute E/(1-sigma) instead of E1 and E2... equations (4) and (6) remain without any change... If the deflections are small, say less than a half of the thickness of the plate... Pezzulla: The minimization gives L + N = kappa_o(1 + nu) and K = 0
claims.note: Timoshenko and Pezzulla (1+nu) statements check out; the 4.2 and 2.0 sqrt(h/kappa) boundaries are the agent's own derived numbers, and Alben's model and sympy derivation were not re-run.

claims.claim: Diffusion-limited actuation tau ~ h^2/D (R&M) with sub-quadratic fits 1.3-1.5; D of printable polymers 0.001-0.0151 mm^2/h; 90% curvature response at 0.72 a^2/D gives 1.9-29 h (0.2 mm), 7.7-116 h (0.4), 31-463 h (0.8); no Formlabs D found.
claims.source_says: For molecular pores, D ~ 10^-9 m2/s, h_a ~ 1 mm and tau = h_a^2/D ~ 1000 s... shrinking time varies as 96 h_a^1.5 min and swelling time as 29 h_a^1.3 min. Table: Nylon 0.001, PLA T-W 0.0151 mm2/h.
claims.note: R&M and Aniskevich values match, and the agent's script rerun gives t90=0.7239 a^2/D, so the real-unit times reproduce; 'no Formlabs D' is an absence claim I could not prove.

claims.claim: Armon 2011, Alben-Balakrisnan-Smela 2011 and Freund 2000 could not be read in the original; only abstracts or a companion paper, so statements about them are second-hand.
claims.source_says: Europe PMC abstract of Armon 2011: we modeled the pod as a thin strip with a flat intrinsic metric and a saddle-like intrinsic curvature.
claims.note: The Armon abstract quote matches; the claim concerns the agent's own access limits, which I only partly confirmed (Armon abstract only, others not fetched).

bm-bioinspired-generative-design.overall: All four key claims hold in substance. Two are partly supported because they depend on absence (no law filter in other tools, no G-code route on Formlabs) and I only confirmed the Bioinspired123D, PreForm format list and CategoryTheoryDesign README parts.

claims.claim: None of the surveyed generators applies a proven law as a hard pre-print filter; Bioinspired123D explicitly does not enforce printer limits and its critic is image-based.
claims.source_says: printer-specific constraints such as minimum feature size, overhang limits, and build-volume restrictions are not explicitly enforced during generation. | vlm_critic.py: Physical stability: "stable" | "unstable"; approve=true only when both "good" and "stable".
claims.note: The Bioinspired123D half is confirmed (paper and image-based critic with a binary stable label); the blanket negative over SciAgents, Silkworm and the truss codes is a survey absence I did not check.

claims.claim: Bioinspired123D outputs Blender scripts with a dimensionless, material-free parameter space (12 base scripts); STL was exported by hand and printed on FDM; so a units/materials/layer layer must be written before bilayer or tube laws can act.
claims.source_says: selected designs generated by Bioinspired3D and Bioinspired123D were exported from Blender as STL files and fabricated via 3D printing. Most samples fabricated on a Stratasys F120 using ABS ... Bambu X1C using PLA or PETG.
claims.note: The CSV has exactly 12 base-script rows in helical, cellular and tubular families; the only 'material' hit is a Blender material_index=0 slot, not a physical material; 'by hand' is implied, and the layer-layer conclusion is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: The project already owns the elimination machinery (eliminate.mjs, three-state ledger, Lean certificates), but lean/constraints.json has no entry for the three laws, so the missing piece is constraint entries, rules_out wrappers and an extractor.
claims.source_says: eliminate.mjs line 2: Checks candidates against the formalised constraints and writes a ledger with three states per (candidate, constraint). grep for timoshenko|bilayer|hygromorph|murray|hollow in constraints.json: no matches.
claims.note: eliminate.mjs and its three-state ledger exist, and the grep of constraints.json is empty; the Lean certificate output and the 'wrappers missing' part were not checked, and the recommendation is a plan.

claims.claim: Formlabs printers take STL/OBJ/3MF/STEP via PreForm, so G-code pipelines do not reach a Form 4 or Fuse 1+ without a new export module; CategoryTheoryDesign's README says a new process needs its own S_*.py and machine_*.py and no SLA profile exists.
claims.source_says: PreForm can open 3D models in following formats: STL, OBJ, 3MF, STEP, STP, STPZ, SLDPRT ... (PreForm lists no G-code). CTD README: for a new process (e.g., DIW, SLA) copy S_print.py to S_diw.py ... require a new machine_*.py module.
claims.note: Formats confirmed (PreForm's list is longer than four and has no G-code), and the README does require a new S_* and machine_* module for SLA; the no-SLA-profile claim and the G-code-not-accepted inference rest on absence.

bm-biopolymer-films.overall: All four key claims check out against the originals. The two weaker points are the bilayer claim, which merges numbers from two different papers, and the Flexible 80A V2 water row, whose label position is ambiguous in the PDF layout. The 0.2 to 1 percent resin comparison is the agent's own estimate.

claims.claim: Cast silk fibroin films strain 5.0 to 7.3 percent in length between 10 and 90 percent RH, far above the 0.2 to 1 percent of stock resins.
claims.note: Silk figures reproduce exactly (WR strain defined over 10 to 90% RH); the 7.29% value is for porous 60% PEO films, and the 0.2 to 1% resin figure is the agent's own estimate, not from this source.

claims.claim: 8 um silk on 25 um polyimide gives a 13 to 21 cm^-1 curvature change and bends in 13 to 44 s; only polyimide has been tested as backing.
claims.source_says: depositing an 8 µm thick layer of RSF onto 3x4x0.025 mm polyimide films; This difference increased from 13 cm-1 to 21 cm-1; bilayer films took similar time to bend within 13–44 seconds and straighten within 22–40 seconds
claims.note: Each number is in the sources, but 13 to 21 comes from the 2025 paper (rising with tyrosine modification) and 13 to 44 s from the 2023 porous-silk paper, so they are not one measurement; the no-other-backing point is an absence claim.

claims.claim: Cellulose is not a large-strain material: NFC swelling about 0.06 to 0.09 percent, CNC isotropic coefficient 0.040 percent per percent moisture, only shear-aligned CNC across alignment (0.30) approaches wood-like values.
claims.source_says: swelling ratio of the 8-µm NFC film is estimated to be only about 0.06%; ... 48-µm film ... about 0.09%. Self-organized CNC films ... CHS ∼0.040 %strain/%C ... shear-oriented ... ∼0.02 and ∼0.30
claims.note: Both sources confirmed (Aalto PDF and Europe PMC abstract); the wood comparison value (beech 0.32) comes from the project record, not these sources.

claims.claim: Stock Formlabs resins' under-1-percent water gain holds for the 1 cm cube table but not for Flexible 80A Resin V2 on its data sheet (ASTM D471: +8 percent mass, +3 percent volume in 1 day).
claims.source_says: Cube table: Flexible 80A Resin water 0.7. Data sheet water row sits between rows '1 day -26 +8% +3%' and '1 week -27 +9% +7%' (label at y=401, rows at y=396 and 406).
claims.note: Reproduced with word coordinates: the Deionized Water label lies between the two rows, so the 1-day and 1-week assignment is inferred from the layout, but the figures are on the Flexible 80A V2 data sheet.

bm-buehler-materials-corpus.overall: One of four claims is supported (the Formlabs V2 water-immersion row, read from the data sheet). The arithmetic claim reproduces only in part. The two thesis-based claims could not be checked because MIT DSpace blocked every route. The 25x-tougher quote is also not in the PMC paper the agent cited, which is about spider silk.

claims.claim: Corpus has no vat-photopolymer/powder-bed/Formlabs abstracts; printed-composite results traced to Objet Connex jetting (Dimas, Gu theses).
claims.note: The MIT DSpace thesis PDFs returned a Cloudflare/HTML page via curl and HTTP 429 via WebFetch; I did not re-run corpus_stats.py, so the counts are unchecked.

claims.claim: Transferable design logic includes ML-designed printed composite about 25x tougher than the stiff material, plus humidity-gated hysteretic stimulus.
claims.note: Gu thesis was blocked (two routes); the cited PMC6397028 (Liu et al., spider silk humidity torsion) contains no 'tougher' passage, so it does not carry the 25x quote.

claims.claim: Moduli 2187 and 0.53 MPa (ratio 4126) give Timoshenko coefficient 0.0058 at equal thickness, 0.4% of the 3/2 ceiling.
claims.note: I reproduced ratio 4126.4 and coefficient 0.00580 (0.0039 of 1.5, i.e. 0.39%) with the standard Timoshenko formula; the optimum ratio 64 and 41-44 figures and the thesis moduli were not checked (thesis unfetchable).

claims.claim: Flexible 80A Resin V2 data sheet reports +8% mass, +3% volume, -26 Shore A after 1 day in deionized water.
claims.source_says: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89%
claims.note: Downloaded the Formlabs V2 TDS PDF and the row matches; the older-resin 0.7% comparison was not checked.

bm-building-physics-standards.overall: Core legal and datasheet facts reproduce from primary sources. Three of the four claims are partly supported, because each leans on an absence assertion, a count of data sheets, or an internal estimate that I did not re-verify.

claims.claim: England relevant building (storey >=18 m, dwellings/institution/residential room) must use A2-s1,d0 or A1 in external walls and specified attachments; shading slats not exempt; shading up to 4.5 m outside the rule.
claims.source_says: components associated with a solar shading device excluding components whose primary function is to provide shade or deflect sunlight such as the awning curtain or slats. ADB 12.20: Solar shading devices installed up to 4.5m above ground level are not required to meet the requirements of regulation 7(2).
claims.note: Reg 7(2), 7(3)(ha), 7(4) and ADB vol 2 para 12.20 all read as claimed; 'single hardest gate' is a judgment.

claims.claim: SBI needs 495x1500 and (1000+t)x1500 mm wings, at least 3 specimens, so a desk print cannot be classified; Formlabs publishes only UL 94 (HB at 3 mm for rated sheets, 9 of 25 sheets; Flame Retardant V-0 3 mm, V-1 2.5 mm, HB 1.5 mm); UL 94 absent from ADB.
claims.source_says: A complete test requires that at least 3 specimens are tested. Long wing: 495 mm x 1500 mm; Short wing: 1000 + (product thickness) mm x 1500 mm. Flame Retardant TDS: UL 94 V-0 (3mm) V-1 (2.5mm) HB (1.5mm).
claims.note: SBI sizes, Flame Retardant ratings, Rigid 10K HB at 3 mm and zero UL 94 matches in ADB2 all reproduced; the '9 of 25 data sheets' count was not re-checked, and 'only UL 94' is an absence claim.

claims.claim: No standard exists for humidity-responsive facade elements; practice is bespoke chamber protocol (Cheng 2024: 170 cycles 90/30 % RH at 6 h, 96 h ISO 4892 UV at 60 C, 10/20/30 C RH matrix); nearest England wording is Approved Document 7 para 1.27.
claims.source_says: AD7 1.27: Materials that are susceptible to changes in their properties may be used in building work and will meet the requirements of the regulations if the residual properties... Residual properties can be estimated at the time of their incorporation.
claims.note: Cheng parameters (170 cycles, 120 min at 90 % plus 240 min at 30 %, 96 h at 60 C, 10/20/30 C) and AD7 1.27 are confirmed; 'no standard exists' is an absence claim I could not prove.

claims.claim: Formlabs CTEs differ by 114-127 um/m/C between Rigid 10K and Tough 1000, giving 0.45-0.51 % strain over 40 K vs an estimated 0.2 % hygroscopic strain; creep/ageing data only at 22 C or graphs; Tough 1500 V2 DMA modulus inflection at 60.8 C.
claims.source_says: Tough 1500 V2 TDS: A glass transition is observed at 109.6 C, and an inflection of the storage (elastic) modulus is observed at 60.8 C.
claims.note: The 60.8 C figure and the arithmetic reproduce (161.6-48=113.6; 168.2-41=127.2; x40 K gives 0.454-0.509 %), but the 0.2 % hygroscopic estimate is the agent's own and uncheckable here, and the CTE pairing is read from garbled PDF text.

bm-category-theory-papers.overall: The paper-based claims largely hold, and the arithmetic reproduces. The Lean theorem statement matches, but the logs the agent cites are missing and two claims rest partly on the agent's own reasoning.

claims.claim: Paper formalises only the pine cone; wheat awns, flytrap, nacre, seed pods carry no equation; eq 6 gives no numerical tau, chi, m0.
claims.source_says: Here we instantiate Nat on the hygromorphic pinecone hierarchy as an example of a natural system
claims.note: Fetched page (first 100k of 126k chars) confirms pinecone-only equations and symbolic eq 6; the rest of the text was not read, so absence elsewhere is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: 'Preserve dynamics' is the simulation condition; only composition closure is proved, fidelity left to experiment; repo 'verified' flag is a tolerance test, only equilibrium angles measured.
claims.source_says: Here, verification is a claim about composition, not about any single model.
claims.note: Paper side supported (commutes with time evolution, chain-rule closure, fidelity empirical); I did not read spec.py's flag or measurement claims.

claims.claim: Lean re-run: HygromorphCeilingCheck and Hygromorphs compile with errors=0, no sorryAx; ceiling f<=3/(2h), bilayer_rules_out; list of checked/unchecked items.
claims.source_says: theorem bilayer_rules_out (h m n Δε κ_claimed : ℝ) ... (hclaim : 3 / 2 * Δε / h < κ_claimed) : bilayerCurvature h m n Δε < κ_claimed
claims.note: Theorem statement matches the ceiling claim and no sorry appears in the check file; the cited logs path does not exist, and I did not verify the rest of the list or the 'not in paper' point.

claims.claim: Prop A.25 needs tau_L=tau_T=tau_Delta and equal moisture, unstated in paper; with tau_L=1, tau_T=5 two states give dD/dt -0.0095 and -0.0895; conjugacy fixes tau so F cannot cover time-constant change.
claims.source_says: It does not state positivity, magnitudes, or any other conditions on them. The proof does not depend on their values.
claims.note: Re-running closure_check.py reproduced -0.0095 and -0.0895 and the equal-tau case; the paper's silence on tau conditions is confirmed, but the necessity argument and the F/conjugacy point are the agent's own and not checked.

bm-clients-and-market.overall: The SBIR figures and the Smart-grants closure reproduce exactly. The Fab.Pub, Hyundai and Schueco quotes are real. The 'live routes' wording, the other named clients, the Formlabs part and the 'no evidence found' conclusions were not confirmed.

claims.claim: Smart grants are closed; KTP, SBIR/STTR and Royce ICP are the live routes.
claims.source_says: Smart grants are now closed for new applications as funding is being aligned to Innovate UK’s new strategic direction.
claims.note: Smart closure confirmed, but the agent's own file says KTP round one is closed and Royce eligibility was not read, so 'live' is overstated and not checked here.

claims.claim: SBIR needs a US-owned for-profit; STTR needs a research partner; Phase I ceiling USD 335,937, Phase II USD 2,239,578 as of 16 Oct 2026; apply page shows USD 323,000.
claims.source_says: As of October 16, 2026, agencies may issue a Phase I award (including modifications) up to $335,937 and a Phase II award ... up to $2,239,578 without seeking SBA approval.
claims.note: All parts reproduced on about and apply pages, including the older $50,000-$323,000 figure.

claims.claim: Clients pay for finished installations (Hyundai via Tate, Neko Health, COS, Buro Happold); Fab.Pub has a material-intake door and GBP 250 minimum budget; no fees published.
claims.source_says: Send us the material source, approximate volume and the product or application you have in mind. / Total Budget (Minimum Budget: £250)
claims.note: Fab.Pub door, GBP 250 and Hyundai partnership confirmed; Neko, COS and Buro Happold client pages not opened by me and 'no fees published' is a negative.

claims.claim: No evidence that any facade manufacturer or Formlabs pays outsiders for material R&D; Schueco offers non-financial resources, Formlabs in-kind consumables and certification.
claims.source_says: Sometimes it’s about gaining access to non-financial resources.
claims.note: Schueco sentence confirmed (fetch returned only the second half of the quote); the Formlabs part and the negative finding were not checked.

bm-competing-approaches.overall: Three of four key claims check out. The Holstov prior-art half of claim 1 could not be opened, so it is unchecked, and the Rigid 10K range in claim 3 could not be read cleanly. The Lean statement matches the file as written. The Dingler numbers and the 4x arithmetic reproduce.

claims.claim: The 3/2 ceiling is prior art (Holstov 2015 wrote the maximum stays at 1.5); the Lean file proves the bound and equality when m^2 n = 1, not the converse.
claims.source_says: Lean: theorem timoshenkoCoefficient_le (coefficient <= 3/(2h)); timoshenkoCoefficient_eq_of_optimal with hypothesis m^2*n = 1; no converse theorem present. Holstov source not fetched.
claims.note: The Lean half matches the file as written; the Holstov quote could not be opened (Newcastle page 403/202, DOI redirect only), so the prior-art half is unchecked.

claims.claim: The formula over-predicts maximum curvature of printed soft humidity bilayers about 4 times (5.3 vs 1.2 per mm; 1.6 vs about 0.4 per mm), though it follows trends.
claims.source_says: Maximum curvature predicted from a humidity dependent E PDOT:PSS is 5.3 mm–1. A maximum curvature of 1.2 mm–1 was reached, about three times the value of the 54 µm bilayer. ...a maximum curvature of 1.6 mm–1 could be calculated
claims.note: Numbers reproduce (5.3/1.2=4.4; 0.4 is derived from 'about three times'; 1.6/0.4=4.0); 'nicely predict the trends' is also in the text.

claims.claim: Tough 1000 CTE 161.6-168.2 vs Rigid 10K 41-48 um/m/C gives 0.45-0.51 % over 40 K, against 0.2 % estimated for humidity; so a temperature-by-humidity factorial is required.
claims.source_says: Tough 1000 datasheet: 'Thermal Expansion (0-150 C) ... 161.6 m/m/°C 168.2 m/m/°C'. Rigid 10K datasheet: 'Thermal Expansion, 0-150 °C' with '48 m/m/°C' visible; other values scrambled.
claims.note: Tough 1000 values confirmed and arithmetic reproduces (113.6-127.2 x 40 K = 0.45-0.51 %), but Rigid 10K range could not be read cleanly, the 0.2 % is an unmeasured estimate, and the factorial is a recommendation.

claims.claim: SMP bilayers move in about 20 s but need heat and are one-shot; kirigami needs external strain; hydrogel bilayers need 1-280 min and are soft.
claims.source_says: Ding: 'After ~20 s, the samples had completed the transformation'; 'remains largely unchanged upon further cooling and heating'. Kirigami: 'Pulling on the sheet in the axial direction'. Review: 'bending angle ... 20 to 720° with actuation times varying from 1 to 280 min'; modulus few to 100s of kPa.
claims.note: All four parts match their sources; heat need is from Ding's 62 C water immersion.

bm-diffusion-kinetics.overall: Three of four key claims reproduce: the Crank constants, the script outputs, and both Formlabs TDS mass tables (checked by PDF word position). The diffusivity-range claim is only partly supported, because some ends of the ranges are derived or second-hand rather than measured. The Formlabs and demonstration claims depend on assumed specimen thicknesses, which the TDS sheets do not state.

claims.claim: Equilibration scales as h^2/D; one-face t50=0.197, t90=0.848, t99=1.78 h^2/D (both faces: divide by 4); optimal bilayer curvature reaches 99% at 1.65 h_a^2/D regardless of modulus ratio.
claims.note: My own Crank series gives 0.04918/0.2120/0.4453, times 4 gives 0.1967/0.848/1.781; the copied script reproduces the 1.652 curvature t99 and 1.5 ceiling, though the laminate model itself is the agent's.

claims.claim: Measured water diffusivities span four decades: polyamide/TPU/filaments 1.4e-13 to 5e-12; methacrylate resins 1.5e-12 to 1.1e-11; hydrogels and PEG-acrylates 4e-11 to 2e-10; PDMS and porous media 6e-10 to 1e-9.
claims.source_says: TPU: 'Diffusion coefficients ranged from 1.40 × 10−13 to 3.40 × 10−12 m2 s−1'. Resins: 'Bis-GMA 11.01 × 10⁻⁸ cm² s⁻¹ ... TEGDMA 1.52 × 10⁻⁸'. Hydrogel: '8.8 × 10−11 to 1.7 × 10−10 m2/s'. PDMS: 'Dwp ≃ 6–8 × 10-10 m2 s-1'.
claims.note: The first three ranges check out, but the 4e-11 hydrogel end is the agent's own inversion, the PDMS value is quoted second-hand, and the porous-media 1e-9 is a model estimate ('For molecular pores, D ~ 10-9'), not a measurement.

claims.claim: Formlabs 1 day/1 week mass data imply D about 3e-12 m2/s for Grey V5 (M_inf ~3.7%, assumed 3.2 mm) and >= 6e-12 for Flexible 80A V2 (assumed 2 mm); the '<1% in 24 h' cube numbers are far from equilibrium (10 mm cube at D=1e-12 reaches ~19% of plateau).
claims.source_says: Grey V5 TDS, DI Water row, MASS column: 101.38% (1 day), 103.23% (1 week). Flexible 80A V2: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89%; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%.
claims.note: I confirmed both TDS values by PDF word coordinates (text extraction scrambles rows) and reproduced D=3.30e-12, 9.32e-12 and the cube figure (18.6% by my own calculation), but the D values rest entirely on the agent's assumed specimen thicknesses, which the TDS does not state.

claims.claim: A demonstration finishing in hours needs D >= 1e-11 with a 0.2-0.8 mm active layer; stock rigid resins (D~1e-12) at 0.2-0.4 mm give 9-38 h; 0.8 mm or more, or dense nylon/TPU, take days to weeks.
claims.note: The arithmetic reproduces from 0.848 h^2/D; the verdict inherits the D assumptions from the other claims and is a model calculation, not a measurement.

bm-formlabs-all-resins.overall: The numbers hold up. The Flexible 80A V2 water-swelling figures, the cube-table water values and the 39.2% vs <0.1% IPA contrast all match the originals. Two claims are weaker as written. The "all Form 4 resins" chemistry claim is extrapolated from the 18 SDS fetched (14 resin SDS checked). The "no humid-air or diffusivity data exists" claim is a negative I could not confirm.

claims.claim: Flexible 80A V2 gains +8% mass/+3% volume at 1 day in deionized water and +9%/+7% at 1 week; it is the only current resin with swelling large enough to contradict a blanket under-1%-in-24h statement.
claims.source_says: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89%; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88% (hardness change, mass, volume, elongation, tensile strength).
claims.note: Numbers reproduce from the TDS ASTM D471 table; 'only resin' is the agent's inference from the cube table (all other rows at or below 0.9%), which holds for the cube test but is not a different test.

claims.claim: Every other Form 4-family resin gains 0.0-0.9% mass in water in Formlabs's 24 h cube test (Clear V5 0.9, Tough 1000 0.0, Rigid 10K <0.1); no humid-air swelling or diffusivity data exists for any of them.
claims.source_says: Clear Resin V5 water 0.9; Tough 1000 Resin water 0; Rigid 10K Resin water <0.1; other rows seen 0.1-0.8 (some marked '<1' or not tested).
claims.note: The cube-table values reproduce, but some rows use '<1' and the 'no humid-air data exists' part is a negative I could not confirm from the page.

claims.claim: Elastic/Flexible 50A takes 39.2% IPA in 24 h against under 0.1% for Rigid 10K.
claims.source_says: Elastic 50A Resin V2 IPA 39.2 (24 hr weight gain, %); Rigid 10K Resin IPA <0.1.
claims.note: Both values match the solvent-compatibility table; 'largest contrast among same-chemistry Form 4 resins' is a mild superlative, and Flex 80A V1 (11.7) and others are smaller.

claims.claim: All Form 4 SLA resins except Silicone 40A are (meth)acrylate photopolymers per their SDS; Silicone 40A is polysiloxane; no measured bond strength exists in the sources read.
claims.source_says: Flexible 80A V2 SDS: Methacrylate monomer(s) 25-40. Silicone 40A SDS: Polysiloxane crosslinker 5-10, odor 'Characteristic acrylate'. Rigid 10K: Urethane Dimethacrylate 15-25.
claims.note: The 14 SDS I checked (not all Form 4 resins) all list (meth)acrylates except Silicone 40A, which lists a polysiloxane crosslinker and also has an acrylate odor line, so 'all' is extrapolated and the no-bonding-evidence part is a negative.

bm-formlabs-printing-workflows.overall: All four claims hold against the live Formlabs pages and manual. One is partly supported: the Open Material Mode page gives the fee and the any-405-nm-resin scope, but not the 'needed' framing.

claims.claim: Form 4 uses a single resin tank and cartridge per print; changing resin type means changing both, so a two-resin strip needs two prints.
claims.source_says: Changing resin types between prints: When changing resin types, always change both the resin tank and resin cartridge.
claims.note: Quote is in the Form 4 manual; 'two prints' is a reasonable inference from it.

claims.claim: Open Material Mode is a paid per-printer licence needed for any non-Formlabs resin; stock Formlabs resins do not need it.
claims.source_says: With Open Material Mode, you can print with any type of 405 nm photopolymer resin on Formlabs SLA printers. Open Material Mode is available for a one-time lifetime fee per printer.
claims.note: The per-printer fee and non-Formlabs-resin use are stated; 'needed' and 'stock resins do not need it' are implied, not said.

claims.claim: Elastic/Flexible 50A takes up 39.2% mass in IPA in 24 h (1 cm cube) vs <0.1% for Rigid 10K; solvent is a far stronger stimulus than humidity.
claims.source_says: Elastic 50A Resin V2 ... IPA 39.2 (10th column); Rigid 10K Resin IPA <0.1; weight gain % after 24 hours, 1 cm cubes. Water for Elastic 50A V2: 0.7.
claims.note: Numbers reproduce from the table; the humidity comparison rests on the water column (0.7), which is liquid water, not humidity.

claims.claim: A strip printed flat on the build platform loses about 0.1 mm of thickness to first-layer compression, half of a 0.2 mm layer, so thickness must be measured.
claims.source_says: When printing a model directly on the build platform, expect each model to be approximately 0.1 mm shorter than designed along the Z-axis in the model's first layers. The exact compressed height varies between printers.
claims.note: 0.1 mm is stated; the half-layer comparison is simple arithmetic and the measure-it advice is a judgment.

bm-funding-materials.overall: All four key claims are factually supported against live pages except for minor unchecked parts (Sloan, Holcim). The agent's quotes largely reproduce; MAMS wording elsewhere in the file differs from the page ('deformation and failure') but is not in the key claims.

claims.claim: NSF 26-521 and 26-515 are rolling, posted 17 Aug 2026; 26-521 allows 1 proposal per person per fiscal year, 26-515 has no per-PI limit; 26-521 covers Biomaterials/Polymers etc., 26-515 covers AMDO/MAMS.
claims.source_says: "Proposals Accepted Anytime"; 26-521: no more than one proposal per fiscal year per PI/Co-PI; 26-515: "There are no restrictions or limits." Both posted August 17, 2026.
claims.note: All parts reproduce; the 'lowest-barrier' ranking is the agent's judgment but the facts hold.

claims.claim: DMREF is 1.5-2.0M over 4 years, last window 21 Jan-4 Feb 2025, biennial in odd years, no 2027 solicitation found; NSF Future Manufacturing closed with a replacement promised for FY 2026 but not found.
claims.source_says: "Awards are expected to range from $1,500,000 – $2,000,000 over ... four years"; "biennially in odd-numbered years"; window "January 21, 2025 - February 04, 2025"; FM: "plan to issue a new NSF funding opportunity ... in FY 2026".
claims.note: Page lists 25-508 as latest, consistent with no 2027 solicitation; 'not found' is the agent's own search result.

claims.claim: Nearest dated UK/EU deadlines: NMIP Sandpit 26 Nov 2026 (UK research orgs), ERC Consolidator 12 Jan 2027, Innovate UK Investor Partnerships 19 Jan 2027 (UK SMEs), EIC Pathfinder Open Stage 1 25 Feb 2027 (up to EUR 4M, 3-country consortium); UK ones exclude a US-only team.
claims.source_says: Sandpit "Closes: 26/11/2026 4:00pm", UK research organisation required; Investor Partnerships "Closes: 19/01/2027 11:00am", UK-registered SME; ERC "Deadline: 12 January 2027"; EIC Stage 1 25 February 2027.
claims.note: EIC consortium needs three entities in member/associated states, not strictly 'three countries' stated so, but close; the ERC/EIC host rules were not tested beyond that.

claims.claim: Autodesk Foundation is invite-only, Schmidt takes no unsolicited proposals, Simons MPS LOI closed 29 Oct 2026, Sloan and Holcim could not be used; only Graham (25 Feb 2027 for organisations) is open.
claims.source_says: Schmidt: "do not accept unsolicited proposals." Autodesk: "Each year we invite a small selection of organizations". Simons LOI "October 29, 2026". Graham orgs "Feb 25, 2027"; individuals page inconsistent (sidebar passed, body Sept 15, 2026).
claims.note: Autodesk, Schmidt, Simons and Graham dates check out; Sloan and Holcim were not checked, and 'only Graham is open' is a judgment (Graham Carter Manny 15 Nov 2026 is also open).

bm-hydrogels.overall: Three of the four key claims are supported by the sources or the script output. The Maennel swelling range is only partly right because 74.1% was measured in water, not PBS. The thickness-ratio claim is an internal calculation that reproduces but is not source-measured. No [held-out clade] or holdout material came up.

claims.claim: PEGDMA-600 with 1 wt% TPO printed on a Formlabs Form 2 at 405 nm, gel fraction 97.6%, giving a Formlabs hydrogel precedent.
claims.source_says: The 3D printing machine utilised was the Formlabs Form 2 SLA ... 250 mW laser at a 405 nm ... results of 99.33% and 97.58% for the UV chamber and SLA samples, respectively.
claims.note: All parts are in the paper; that TPO was the initiator for the SLA samples is an inference from its either/or wording.

claims.claim: LCD-printed GelMA bilayer strips bent to radii of 11-20 mm, linear swelling 7.83% at 30 s down to 0.70% at 70 s, E about 15-20 kPa; project Timoshenko ceiling predicts about 11 mm.
claims.source_says: radii of curvature between 11 and 20 mm depending on the geometry; Table 1: 30 s swelling 7.83%, 70 s 0.70%, modulus 14.48 to 20.23 kPa.
claims.note: Paper figures match; the 10.9-11.0 mm prediction is the agent's own calculation, and calcs.py does print R_min=10.9 mm, but the text of the paper gives 7.7% and about 1% in prose, differing slightly from the table.

claims.claim: Printed PEG-acrylate swelling is tunable from about 0.5% to 74% linear in 24 h (Maennel), and PEGDA J rises from about 4-5 at 1 kDa to about 17-36 at 5.85 kDa.
claims.source_says: TPGDA-based resins showed the lowest swelling ratio with less than 0.5% over a period of 24 h in PBS. ... RC5 exhibiting a swelling ratio of 74.1%.
claims.note: The J values match Table 2 exactly (5.5-4.2, 8.9-6.9, 35.7-16.9), but the 74.1% was reported for water, not the PBS/24 h condition the claim implies.

claims.claim: By the project's f(m,n), a kPa-to-MPa hydrogel on a GPa Formlabs resin needs a hydrogel 15-725 times thicker than the stiff layer to reach the 1.5 ceiling.
claims.source_says: calcs.py section 9 output: GelMA 19 kPa on Rigid 10K m*=725.48; on Clear V5 m*=380.44; PEGDMA-600 13 MPa on Clear V5 m*=14.54, on Rigid 10K m*=27.72.
claims.note: The script arithmetic reproduces (m*=n^-1/2, 14.5 to 725), but it rests on the project's own f(m,n) and unverified moduli, and 'mechanically dead' is a modelled result, not a measured one.

bm-ip-landscape-deep.overall: I could confirm one of the four key claims, and only in part. The EPO server gave EP4019251 B1 claim 1 and the 2026-03-25 grant mention, both as the agent described. Google Patents answered 503 on two routes and Justia and Patentscope answered 403. That left the MIT/Stratasys, Microsoft and WO2018033422 claims unchecked. The theorem-prover search counts could not be re-run, and the 'ownable subject matter' conclusion is a judgment for counsel.

claims.claim: The three building-scale wood-bilayer families are narrow and not obstacles to a printed resin or powder element (ETH/Empa WO2018033422 Ceased, lever-coupled shading; Stuttgart EP4019251 B1 and DE112019001411 pre-condition layers at one climate).
claims.source_says: Manufacturing method of a multi-layer component (1) of layered elements (0, 0'), comprising: obtaining (I) target climatic condition information of a climatic condition at a target location at a customer's site
claims.note: EP4019251 B1 claim 1 and its 2026-03-25 grant mention match, but the WO and DE pages and the Ceased status could not be fetched, and 'not obstacles' is a judgment.

claims.claim: MIT/Stratasys US 11155025 B2 is the live patent nearest a resin-printed differential-swelling part (Active, to about 2034-02-25), claim 1 narrow; the broad parent application is Abandoned.
claims.note: Google Patents returned HTTP 503 on two routes and Justia returned 403, so claim text, status and expiry were not checked.

claims.claim: Zero Google Patents documents and zero arXiv records combine a theorem prover/proof assistant with material, geometry or AM design; nearest are expired Microsoft US 8473895, live PARC IC planner, live Toyota inflatable design method; so a design-and-verification method is the most plausible ownable subject matter.
claims.note: The Google Patents queries and the Microsoft page were unreachable (503/403), and the ownability conclusion is a judgment for counsel.

claims.claim: The optimum-thickness-ratio behaviour and measured wood curvature changes are in a patent document citing Timoshenko 1925, so the bilayer principle cannot be claimed.
claims.note: WO2018033422 on Google Patents returned 503 and Patentscope returned 403, so the Timoshenko passage was not seen.

bm-lay-analogies.overall: All four key claims reproduce against the original sources (PMC2838359, Wikipedia raw formula, Holstov PDF, Formlabs page and TDS PDF); the Lean result was not re-run, only the theorem statements checked.

claims.claim: Pine-cone scale is two-layer, opens dry/closes wet, dead cones keep doing it, so no living process needed.
claims.source_says: when dead fallen dry cones are moved into a humid environment, they close and open again when dried, an experiment that may be repeated many times. (also: bilayered structure of the individual scales)
claims.note: Source states all parts; 'no living process needed' is a fair inference.

claims.claim: Ceiling kappa <= 1.5 x mismatch/h is Lean-checked (5 theorems, 0 errors, 0 sorryAx), visible in the 1863 bimetal formula with a = 1 + square >= 1, not new (Holstov 2015 plotted it).
claims.source_says: 1/R - 1/R0 = 3/(2a) * Δε/h (Villarceau, 1863); Holstov: the maximum value of the function remains constant at 1.5
claims.note: Wikipedia raw source and Holstov PDF match; Lean file has 5 theorems incl. bilayer_rules_out and no 'sorry' text; Lean run itself not repeated.

claims.claim: Formlabs 0.7% is a 24 h weight gain of a 1 cm cube for Flexible 80A and Elastic 50A V2, not equilibrium nor size change; Flexible 80A V2 gains +8% mass in a day by another method.
claims.source_says: Formlabs measures resistance to solvents by observing, measuring, and weighing printed cubes (originally 1 cm) ... for 24 hours. Flexible 80A V2 TDS: Deionized Water 1 day -26 +8% +3%
claims.note: Both rows show 0.7% water; TDS shows +8% mass at 1 day; 'not equilibrium' is inferred from the 24 h design.

claims.claim: Diffusion time scales as thickness squared ideally (4x), but pine-cone fits give exponents 1.5 (drying) and 1.3 (wetting), so half-thickness strips are 2.5 to 4 times faster.
claims.source_says: the shrinking (drying) time varies as τd = 96 h_a^1.5 min and the swelling (wetting) time varies as τd = 29 h_a^1.3 min (h_a in mm)

bm-lean-materials-laws.overall: All four key claims hold. I read the Lean sources and axiom logs and re-ran the Mathlib grep, which gave 0 files for every materials term. I did not re-run Lean. The saved mathlib_grep_out.txt omits the zero-hit lines, so the agent's quoted evidence for the last claim is incomplete even though the claim is true.

claims.claim: Reuss <= Voigt is kernel-checked for two phases (with equality case f(1-f)(E1-E2)^2 = 0) and for n phases, with only the three standard axioms.
claims.source_says: theorem reuss_le_voigt ... reussN s w E ≤ voigtN s w E; reuss_eq_voigt_iff: ↔ f * (1 - f) * (E₁ - E₂) ^ 2 = 0; axioms log: depends on axioms: [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]
claims.note: Statements match the Lean file as written; the axiom log lists only the three standard axioms for all five theorems (Lean not re-run, per instructions).

claims.claim: Euler buckling strip: load strictly increases with thickness, strictly decreases with length, scales as t^3 and 1/L^2, critical stress depends on t/(K L) only; statements about the formula, not a derivation.
claims.source_says: eulerStrip_strictMono_thickness, eulerStrip_strictAnti_length, thickness_scaling s^3, length_scaling /s^2, criticalStress = π^2 E (t/(K L))^2/12; header: 'here P_cr is a definition'.
claims.note: Each plain-words statement matches its theorem; axiom log shows only standard axioms for all eight.

claims.claim: The check gate is not vacuous: a sorry file fails with sorryAx and exit 1, while the three real files exit 0.
claims.source_says: NegativeControl.lean errors=1 sorryAx=1 ... depends on axioms: [propext, sorryAx, Classical.choice, Quot.sound] FAILED exit=1; the three real files: ALL CHECKED, exit=0.
claims.note: The control also fails on a noncomputable error, but sorryAx is listed, so the gate catches the sorry as claimed.

claims.claim: Mathlib at the pinned revision has no materials vocabulary (0 files for Voigt, Reuss, buckling, Young's modulus, Laman, rigidity matrix).
claims.source_says: I re-ran mathlib_grep.sh: Laman -> 0 files, Voigt -> 0 files, Reuss -> 0 files, buckling -> 0 files, Young's modulus -> 0 files, rigidity matrix -> 0 files.
claims.note: Reproduced by re-running the script; the saved mathlib_grep_out.txt is truncated to three lines and lacks these zeros, but the claim holds.

bm-mamou-mani-portfolio.overall: Quotes are accurate. Claims 1 is supported. Claims 2 and 3 rest on absence of data, which was only spot-checked. Claim 4's 'only structural test' is overstated because the Tate page reports load tests.

claims.claim: The practice states the durable-vs-biodegradable contradiction; PLA is a 'middle ground' that only composts industrially.
claims.source_says: there is a contradiction between the idea of sustainable or durable and biodegradable, which is the opposite. The material we use, PLA, is a nice middle ground because it's not going to compost or degrade on its own
claims.note: Frederic, Altostrata page and Dezeen (60 C, 100% humidity) all say this.

claims.claim: No quantitative moisture/UV/creep/weathering data are published; durability evidence is only qualitative (Conifera outdoors, WOW!House 3 years unchanged, Altostrata weathering wording); only moisture sentence is about composting.
claims.source_says: Outside are more Conifera modules, deliberately exposed to wind and rain to prove the longevity of PLA
claims.note: The qualitative quotes are real, but the absence claim is a negative I could only spot-check on the pages named; the Altostrata page does mention humidity only for composting.

claims.claim: Fire is handled by additives per project (Roe fireproof, RIVA fire retardant, Fab.Shield) and no fire class or test result is published.
claims.source_says: The interior piece was 3D printed robotically from a blend of fermented sugar and non-toxic fire retardant.
claims.note: The three additive statements are confirmed (Fab.Shield: 'Flame-retardant blend developed for architectural performance requirements'); no class was seen on those pages, but absence is only spot-checked.

claims.claim: The only structural test on any practice page is one in-house pull test in an invalid unit (500 kg.m2); founder concedes PLA 'not very well researched'.
claims.source_says: Our in-house tests with ARUP and Fab Pub have proven a resistance to pull forces of 500 kg.m2. ... PLA although widely used in 3D printing is not very well researched
claims.note: Quotes are accurate, but 'only' is wrong: the Tate page reports load tests with Webb Yates Engineers and the Roe page says modules are structurally tested; the 'not well researched' line is page text, not attributed to the founder.

bm-mycelium-living-materials.overall: The numbers in the four key claims reproduce against their sources (Nie, Wang, hemp-hurd and review texts, Shen abstract). Each of the three that go beyond numbers adds an overreach the sources do not carry: 'only measured', 'largest', and the Shen 2 mm layer/weakening/no-Formlabs details, which I did not confirm in the full text.

claims.claim: The only measured in-air humidity data for a mycelium layer of bilayer relevance is Nie 2026: T. versicolor film, two grown layers, E = 23.7 MPa, volumetric expansion 9.27% (A) vs 3.38% (B) between 30% and 85% RH, 0.22-0.30 mm per layer (contains PVA and glycerol).
claims.source_says: Bulk moisture expansion rate (ε_b) was higher for layer A (9.27%) than layer B (3.38%); 30% RH dry scan to ~85% RH; 10% PVA + 10% glycerol, E 23.7 MPa; thickness 0.22 and 0.30 mm.
claims.note: All numbers and the PVA/glycerol content check out, but 'the only measured' is a universal claim the source cannot support (the source itself cites Sinha et al. on living S. commune films).

claims.claim: A micrometre-thin layer of dried microbial cells is the largest humidity-strain living layer with a fitted model: volume linear in RH, 1 um cells on 200 um latex bends at 15% RH and flattens at 95% RH, fitted modulus 70 MPa.
claims.source_says: The top layer is composed of E. coli cells (1 μm thick), and the bottom layer is a latex sheet (200 μm thick). It bends at 15% RH and becomes flat at 95% RH. Fitted elastic modulus of the cell layer is 70 MPa.
claims.note: Geometry, linear volume-RH and 70 MPa are in the source, but the source does not rank this as the largest humidity strain among living layers.

claims.claim: Particulate mycelium composites are a poor swelling layer: water uptake 6-436%, drying shrinkage 2.78-17%, swelling almost all through-thickness (205-244%), in-plane under about 7%, poor wet integrity.
claims.source_says: in-plane dimensional changes were limited, with width and length changes generally remaining below approximately 7%. Review: 436% in rapeseed straw; Ganoderma on beech sawdust (6%); MBC shrinkages between 2.78% and 17%.
claims.note: Each number is in its cited text (205-244% are formulation 2 means at 2 h and 72 h, and formulations 1 and 7 lost integrity); 'poor swelling layer' is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Shen 2024 reaches 160 MPa modulus and 0.72 MPa tensile strength only on a coarse paste-printed substrate (2 mm layers) and the living phase weakens that substrate; no growth on a Formlabs resin published.
claims.source_says: our method yields the strongest mycelium composite reported to date with a modulus of 160 MPa and tensile strength of 0.72 MPa
claims.note: 160/0.72 MPa confirmed in the Europe PMC abstract; the 2 mm layer, weakening and Formlabs absence are not in the abstract or the arXiv abstract page (arXiv text not opened by me), and the absence claim is a negative.

bm-natural-benchmarks.overall: Core numbers (moduli, 22% vs 1%, 4.5 wt%, 500 um, 100 ms snap-buckling, 50% modulus reduction) check out. The m^2n/f/percent-of-ceiling values are the agent's derived arithmetic. The 29/96 min response times, the 1 mm active-layer thickness, Erodium, and flytrap water-transport timing are not in the cited sources.

claims.claim: Natural pine-cone bilayers give m^2 n = 2 to 5.7, f = 1.23-1.46 (82-97% of 3/2 ceiling); Reyssat m~1,n~5 gives 83%; paper strip 98.8%
claims.source_says: decreased upon water uptake linearly from ESF,30% = 800 MPa to ESF,75% = 200 MPa ... sclereid layer ... from ESC,50% = 35 MPa to ESC,60% = 25 MPa ... sclerenchyma fiber strands ... around 500 µm
claims.note: Source supports the moduli and ~500 um fibre thickness, but the m^2n, f and percent-of-ceiling values are the agent's own arithmetic (and Reyssat and the paper strip are not in this source); the 1000 um sclereid thickness was not found.

claims.claim: Pine-cone benchmarks: active ~1 mm, passive ~0.5 mm; 21% differential strain (22% vs 1%); ~11% over 0-100 %RH; 29 min wet / 96 min dry; 4.5 wt% at 80 %RH
claims.source_says: In the wet state, the sclereid layer was 27% thicker and 22% longer in the bending zone ... fiber strands ... 1% longer. The sclereid cells (93 mg, 23 °C, 80% rh) absorbed 4.5 wt%
claims.note: 22%, 1% and 4.5 wt% at 80% rh are confirmed and 11% contraction is for 80 to 30% rh, not 0-100; the 29/96 min times and 1 mm active thickness were not found.

claims.claim: Timoshenko-type theory fits pine cone only fairly well and over-predicts unless ~50% lower wet moduli are used
claims.source_says: A fairly good agreement is obtained ... even if overestimation is observed ... we need to take into account a 50% reduction of Young's modulus for dry tissue to fit the experimental data with the model
claims.note: Matches PMC4733047; the 800 to 200 MPa link is from the other paper and is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Flytrap closes in ~100 ms by snap-buckling; Erodium coil from single tilted cellulose layer (20 to 10 degrees); ceiling applies only to pine cone, sesame, paper strip
claims.source_says: The rapid closure of the Venus flytrap (Dionaea muscipula) leaf in about 100 ms ... the fast closure of the trap results from a snap-buckling instability
claims.note: Flytrap 100 ms and snap-buckling confirmed; the PubMed record says nothing on water transport taking minutes, Erodium, or the scope judgment.

bm-open-hardware-repro.overall: Three of four key claims hold on re-check: the Formlabs prices and the $5,108 sum, the resolution.py figures, and the $875 lifetime Open Material Mode price. The bilayer claim is only partly supported. I did not read the earlier file the Open Material Mode claim says it contradicts.

claims.claim: Every Formlabs line is priced from official store pages on 2026-11-12: Form 4 Basic $2,625, Wash V2 $699, Cure V2 $999, two extra tanks $238, 1 L resins $149-$199; Formlabs core is $5,108.
claims.source_says: Form 4 Basic $2,625; Form Wash V2 $699; Form Cure V2 $999; Form 4 Resin Tank $119; Flexible 80A 1 L $199; Flexible 50A $199; Tough 1000 $149.
claims.note: All prices reproduce, and 2625+699+999+238+547 = 5108.

claims.claim: Open Material Mode for Form 4 is officially $875, lifetime, per printer, contradicting the earlier file's reseller price of $3,748.50.
claims.source_says: Open Material Mode for Form 4 (non-biocomp) $875. Optional, one-time purchase per printer for lifetime access.
claims.note: The $875 lifetime per-printer price is confirmed; I did not read the earlier file, so the contradiction is unchecked.

claims.claim: A bilayer is built as one PreForm project of two builds (one resin per build, one tank per resin); no Formlabs statement of two resins in one job.
claims.source_says: PreForm supports projects—you can set up builds across different printers and materials. Separate tank for each individual resin color or type, switching materials is as easy as sliding in a new tank.
claims.note: Both quoted passages exist, but neither says a bilayer should be built this way; the 'no statement' part is an absence the sources cannot confirm.

claims.claim: Instruments follow from the signal: 0.1 mg balance for strips (1 mg only for the 8% resin), optical length at about 10 um/pixel with a certified scale, about 2 um pixels for thickness.
claims.source_says: resolution.py output: Flexible 80A V2 strip 174.4 mg; 0.1 mg balance error 0.3% at 8% uptake, 1 mg 2.9%; 80 um and 4.0 um targets; 2400 dpi = 10.6 um; thickness pixel <= 2.0 um.
claims.note: I re-ran the script and the numbers reproduce, though the instrument choice itself rests on the agent's tolerance assumptions.

bm-passive-facades-evidence.overall: Three of four key claims are accurate on the specifics I could check against the original papers (Cheng 2024, Aereco/AIVC paper, Van den Bossche 2007, Sowa 2020 abstract, Yang 2025, arXiv 2308.01530). Each also carries a universal 'no' or 'only' that no source supports, plus one wax-tile duration ('days') the paper does not give. The RH-versus-shade numbers match the agent's saved output, but I did not re-run the script because it writes into the agent's own folders.

claims.claim: No measured energy, comfort or daylight benefit exists for humidity-driven passive facade shading; the Freiburg study measured shade coverage only (50-90% in summer) and defers the indoor benefit to future work.
claims.source_says: While we have focused on evaluating the 4D-printed shading elements through analysis of shade coverage in this study, it will be important to quantify the improvement of indoor climate regulation in future work.
claims.note: The Freiburg part and the 50-90% shade coverage are confirmed in Cheng 2024, but the sweeping 'none exists anywhere' is an absence claim from a limited search that no source can support.

claims.claim: Relative humidity is only an indirect proxy for shade need; works in dry-summer climates, authors leave humid tropics untested; own calculation shows Singapore element mostly open in 98% of shade-wanted hours, weak in Houston, Mumbai, Sydney.
claims.source_says: temperate climate with dry and hot summers as well as humid and cold winters, creating an indirect but reliable link between the need for shading and the behavior of hygromorphic materials in response to RH
claims.note: Cheng quote and the tropical-untested statement are verbatim in the paper; the saved script output shows Singapore 0.98, Houston 0.38, Mumbai 0.43, Sydney 0.50 (I read the saved JSON, did not re-run, as the script writes into the other agent's folders).

claims.claim: Humidity-controlled ventilation is the only passive humidity-responsive element with in-service numbers: 30% airflow cut in occupied Paris dwellings vs constant-flow reference (manufacturer); independent simulation 14-27% heating saving; fails on upper floors of tall blocks without fans.
claims.source_says: The measured savings on the airflow for this project have been evaluated at 30% in average (55% if extrapolating to the statistical average occupancy in France). / System C+ allows to increase the energy savings up to 27% ... and 14% for ... average airtightness.
claims.note: The 30%, 14-27% and upper-floor ineffectiveness (Sowa abstract, simulation) all reproduce, but 'the only' element with in-service numbers is an unverifiable universal and the manufacturer authorship was not checked by me.

claims.claim: Durability evidence for any passive responsive facade element is short: 170 lab cycles and 13 months (cellulose bilayer), days (wax tile), 264 hours (hydrogel window); none approaches building lifetime.
claims.source_says: The number of cycles tested is still small compared to the entire lifetime of a building ... lost its thermochromic function after 264 hours of continuous operation due to water evaporation
claims.note: 170 cycles, 13 months and 264 h are confirmed, but the wax tile paper only says tests were done in July and September, so 'days' is not stated, and 'any element' overgeneralises.

bm-poc-designs.overall: All four key claims hold up arithmetically. I confirmed the water row in the Formlabs PDF and reproduced the ceiling script verdict, the partner table and the 0.719 and 1.65 settling numbers independently. The caveats are inputs, not arithmetic. The slab thickness, the wet and partner moduli, and the isotropic and Fickian assumptions are the agent's own, not the data sheet's.

claims.claim: The law kappa = f(m,n) d_eps/h with f <= 3/2 (equality at m^2 n = 1) is reproduced by the project's check script re-run unchanged and by an independent layered-beam solver to 1e-9, so a bilayer's curvature is predicted with no fitted parameter once free strains and thicknesses are measured.
claims.source_says: VERDICT: the ceiling holds in every check (best of 4000 hill-climbs from random starts: f = 1.500000000000). Saved solver_vs_f: solver and f_project agree to 9 decimals at 7 points.
claims.note: The script re-run and the solver agreement reproduce, but I did not re-derive the solver; 'no fitted parameter' is a framing that also assumes perfect bond, small strain and measured free strains.

claims.claim: All predictions rest on the Flexible 80A V2 row: +8% mass/+3% volume at 1 day, +9%/+7% at 1 week in deionized water, giving 1-3% linear strain; no independent measurement of hygroscopic strain or diffusivity exists in the sources read.
claims.note: I fetched the PDF and the water row matches; 1.03^(1/3)-1=0.99% and 1.07^(1/3)-1=2.28% reproduce; the 'no other measurement' part is a negative about the agent's reading, and 'every prediction' also leans on moduli and D priors.

claims.claim: Only soft-on-soft pairs (80A V2 with Flexible 50A or Silicone 40A) reach 99% of the 3/2 ceiling at printable thickness; stiff partners lose 41% (Tough 1000) to 89% (Rigid 10K).
claims.source_says: Stress at 50% Elongation 1.5 MPa 2.9 MPa (80A V2 data sheet, ASTM D412). Data sheet gives no tensile modulus; wet 3.0 MPa and partner moduli are the agent's own estimates.
claims.note: With the agent's assumed moduli my independent beam calculation gives f = 1.495, 1.493, 0.883, 0.499, 0.162, so the arithmetic holds, but the moduli inputs are secant guesses and I did not re-read the Tough 1000, Grey V5 or Rigid 10K sheets.

claims.claim: At the optimum, curvature settles in 0.719 h_a^2/D; the Formlabs 1-day/1-week data give D between 1.4e-12 and 9.3e-12 m2/s for an assumed 2 mm slab, so a 0.4 mm layer settles in hours to about a day, the louver blade in 1-10 days, a metre-scale element in months.
claims.source_says: Rectangular slabs, used for hardness, mass, and volume change, are evaluated immediately after wiping dry without a conditioning period.
claims.note: I reproduced 0.719 (t90) and 1.652 (t99) with my own Fourier moment model, and D = 9.3e-12 (mass) and 1.4e-12 (volume) for 2 mm, but the sheet states no slab thickness, so D and every time rests on an assumed 2 mm and Fickian behaviour.

bm-polyamide-sls.overall: One claim is supported and three are partly supported. The datasheet numbers, the PA11 diffusivity and the vendor 0.2% at 1.4% figure are real. The Springer paper would not open, so the 10.49% void-water and 1.6% dense-PA12 figures are unchecked. The PA12 diffusivity range, the equilibration times and the bilayer radii are the agent's own derivations. The 1.4% vendor figure is for cast PA12, not sintered.

claims.claim: PA12 (PA2200) water absorption 0.52 wt% at 23C/50%RH, 1.33 at 96%RH, 1.93 in 100C water
claims.source_says: Water absorption % 1.93 | ISO 62 / DIN 53495 % 1.33 | Water absorption % 0.52 (pdftotext rows; labels and conditions in separate columns)
claims.note: The three values are in the datasheet; the column layout is garbled, so I could not read each condition label beside its value, and I took the order from the agent's mapping.

claims.claim: 5.5-10.5 wt% immersion uptake of sintered PA12 is mostly void water (density 0.90-0.95 vs 1.01 dense); dense PA12 saturates at 1.6%
claims.source_says: UZH PA2200 datasheet: Density 0,90 – 0,95 g/cm3. Springer page would not open (paywall/redirect); Crossref gave only the title 'Effect of water absorption on the properties of selective laser-sintered PA12 specimens'.
claims.note: The sintered density is confirmed, but I could not open the Springer text for the 10.49% and porosity wording or the 1.6% dense value, and the void-versus-swelling conclusion is the agent's own inference.

claims.claim: PA11 bulk water diffusivity at 23C is 4.95e-13 m2/s; PA12 same order; 0.8 mm strip needs 76-126 h to 90% equilibrium, 4x with one face sealed
claims.note: The PA11 D value matches, but the paper has no PA12 data; the PA12 range and the 76-126 h time come from the agent's own calc, which I did not rerun.

claims.claim: No measured hygroscopic expansion coefficient exists for PA11/PA12/TPU; vendor gives 0.2% dimensional change at 1.4% uptake for PA12, giving free strain 0.1-0.2% and bilayer R of 130-1000 mm
claims.source_says: PowerCore, with a maximum absorption of 1.4%, has a corresponding dimensional change of 0.2%.
claims.note: The vendor figure is real, but it is for cast PA12GC fully submerged, not laser-sintered PA12. The 'no measured coefficient exists' claim, the 0.1-0.2% strain over 30-80% RH and the bilayer radius are unsourced extrapolation.

bm-resin-water-uptake-data.overall: The raw numbers in all four key claims reproduce from the original sources. Two claims are fully checkable and match. The Flexible 80A V2 claim overreaches in its comparison to other resins, the Denture Base OP claim rests on an absence statement no source can support, and the diffusivity claim extrapolates beyond the 1 mm plates the paper tested.

claims.claim: Flexible 80A Resin V2 gains +8% mass and +3% volume after 1 day and +9% mass and +7% volume after 1 week in deionized water (ASTM D471 slab), unlike the under-1% cube figures for other Formlabs resins.
claims.source_says: Deionized Water: 1 day -26 +8% +3% 94% 89%; 1 week -27 +9% +7% 101% 88%. 'Rectangular slabs, used for hardness, mass, and volume change, are evaluated immediately after wiping dry'
claims.note: The V2 numbers reproduce exactly from the PDF word coordinates, but 'other Formlabs resins are under 1%' is too broad because the same record lists Elastic 50A V1 at 2.3% in water.

claims.claim: Elastic 50A V1 prints both size and weight change for a 24 h cube: in solvents size/weight is 0.44 to 0.52, and in water weight is +2.3% with size only '<1%'.
claims.source_says: Water: size '<1', weight '2,3'. Acetone 19,3/37,3; isopropyl 13,3/25,6; butyl acetate 18,2/39,6; xylene 20,4/46,6; Skydrol 5 9,9/21,7.
claims.note: The ratios work out to 0.517, 0.520, 0.460, 0.438 and 0.456, so the 0.44 to 0.52 range reproduces for the major solvents.

claims.claim: No independent measurement of linear hygroscopic strain exists for a Formlabs resin; the nearest independent data are Denture Base OP sorption values that disagree 2.4-fold (17.86 ug/mm3 at 48 h vs 7.53 at 7 d) and a Form 3 Clear Resin null length result.
claims.source_says: Gad: Formlabs water sorption 'Before ... 17.86(0.83)', 48 h at 37 C. Izzettinoglu: 'Wsp-DW 7,53 ± 1,74(8,08)', 7 days. Radic: 'side lengths ... remained 4.80 cm ... within the ± 0.15 mm manufacturing tolerance'.
claims.note: All three data points and the 2.4x ratio (17.86/7.53 = 2.37) are real, but the 'no measurement exists' part cannot be shown by these sources, and the two papers used different disc thicknesses and protocols.

claims.claim: Water diffusivity in printed methacrylate photopolymer is of order 1e-12 m2/s or lower (0.85e-12 reported; about 2.6e-13 on recheck), with sorption still rising at 14 days (11.1 to 39.8 ug/mm3), so layers of 0.4 mm and up need days to equilibrate.
claims.source_says: 'D = 1.02–1.15 × 10−12 m2/s for milled and 0.85 × 10−12 m2/s for printed materials'; resin IV wsp median 11.1 (24 h) to 39.8 (14 days).
claims.note: The reported D and the 11.1 to 39.8 medians match, and my own half-time estimate gives about 2.6e-13 (half of 39.8 first reached near 53 h), but the paper's 1 mm DLP plates are non-Formlabs, and 'days for 0.4 mm' is an extrapolation rather than something the paper states.

bm-safety-lca.overall: Three of four key claims are supported by the original sources; the SDS claim matches on the six sheets I re-read but I did not check all 14.

claims.claim: All 14 Formlabs SLA resin SDS carry H317; Rigid 10K and Silicone 40A H317 alone; Durable V2 and High Temp V2 are H360; Flexible 80A V2 and High Temp V2 are H318; so the two H360 resins should be excluded from a public proof of concept.
claims.source_says: High Temp V2: "H318 Causes serious eye damage H317 May cause an allergic skin reaction H360 May impair fertility. May impair fetus." Durable V2: "H317 ... H360 May damage fertility or the unborn child."
claims.note: I re-read 6 of the sheets (Rigid 10K, Silicone 40A, High Temp V2, Durable V2, Flexible 80A V2) and they match, but I did not check all 14, and the exclusion advice is a judgment.

claims.claim: Formlabs says cleaned parts, cured resin and sintered powder cannot be recycled, and liquid resin and resin-laden solvent may be hazardous waste, so nothing printed may be called recyclable.
claims.source_says: "cannot be recycled. Discard cleaned parts and cured (hardened) resin as household waste." and "Liquid resin (whether pure liquid, dissolved in solvent, or partially cured) may be classified as hazardous waste in your region"
claims.note: Both Formlabs pages say this; the powder page also repeats "cannot be recycled"; the 'may not be called recyclable' step is the agent's inference.

claims.claim: Formlabs calls Nylon 11 'bio-based' with no percentage or supplier; the only 100% bio-based carbon (ASTM D6866, castor oil) figure is Arkema's own Rilsan PA11 INVENT NAT sheet and cannot be transferred.
claims.source_says: Formlabs: "legacy strong, highly ductile bio-based material." Arkema: "natural Polyamide 11 powder made from 100% renewable source (castor oil)"; table lists Bio-based carbon content, test ASTM D6866.
claims.note: Formlabs page gives no percentage; I did not confirm the numeric 100 in the scrambled table, but the 100% renewable castor oil statement is there.

claims.claim: EU Directive 2024/825 (applies from 27 September 2026) names 'biobased' and 'biodegradable' as generic environmental claims prohibited unless recognised excellent environmental performance can be shown.
claims.source_says: "'biodegradable', 'biobased' or similar statements that suggest or create the impression of excellent environmental performance. Such generic environmental claims should be prohibited when recognised excellent environmental performance cannot be demonstrated"
claims.note: The wording is in a recital and the text says Member States apply the measures "from 27 September 2026"; the UK-guidance remark was not checked.

bm-simulation-fem.overall: All four key claims match the agent's own output files, and the arithmetic reproduces. The checks were against local result text, with no re-runs. They test the agent's own simulations, not a published source. The large-deflection claim rests on a single Ritz trial space (degree 4) and one aspect ratio.

claims.claim: Timoshenko coefficient and 3/2 ceiling at m=n^-0.5 reproduced: 1-D to 2.9e-15, 2-D plane-stress FEM to 1.2e-7 over n=1..50, and to 5e-5 at the optimum up to n=2000.
claims.source_says: max |f_numeric - f_closed| ... 2.887e-15; max |FEM/Timoshenko f - 1| = 1.160e-07 at n=10, m=0.05; n=2000 m=0.02236 f_FEM 1.50007, rel.err +4.98e-05
claims.note: All three numbers appear in the agent's own output files s01, s02 and s06; I read the output text and did not re-run the scripts.

claims.claim: Ceiling is 3/2 only for a free strip; plane strain reaches (1+nu1)*3/2: 1.95 at nu=0.30, 2.235 at nu=0.49; modulus ratio still drops out.
claims.source_says: largest FEM coefficient = 2.23500 at n=1, m=1 (ceiling 3/2 = 1.5; ratio 1.49000); case B largest 1.95000; f_FEM at optimum identical for n=1..50
claims.note: Matches the output file; this is the agent's own FEM result, verified only in 2-D plane strain, as the agent itself says.

claims.claim: In the 3-D linear model, curvature along the strip is width-independent (equal nu under 1e-4; mismatched 0.49/0.35 at most 0.32 percent low) and cross-width curvature is synclastic.
claims.note: Table rows agree; kz/kx is not meaningful below w/h=4, which the agent states elsewhere, so the synclastic statement holds for w/h>=4 only.

claims.claim: In the large-deflection model, length curvature is 1.4 percent below Timoshenko at w=h/sqrt(f*d_eps) and 13 percent below at twice that width (n=10 optimum, L/h=40), so narrower strips behave as the 1-D law.
claims.note: 1-0.986=1.4 percent and 1-0.866=13.4 percent reproduce; h/sqrt(1.5*0.01)=8.2h so lam is about 1 there; the result comes from one polynomial Ritz model, and the 'narrower behaves as 1-D' part is an extrapolation.

bm-testing-metrology.overall: All four key claims reproduce against ISO 62, ASTM D570, the Travers and PA6.6 pages, the Formlabs Form 4 page and the project's calc output. The one caveat is the Flexible 80A V2 row, which depends on coordinate reconstruction of a scrambled PDF table. The camera resolution figure is an assumption, as the agent states.

claims.claim: ISO 62 (technically equivalent to ASTM D570) is a mass method: dry at 50 C to constant mass, weigh to 0.1 mg within 1 min, 23.0 +/- 1.0 C water, time series, re-dry for extracted material, Fick fit for D and saturation; does not measure swelling strain.
claims.source_says: Reweigh the test specimens to the nearest 0,1 mg within 1 min of removing them from the water (mass m2). ... This test method and ISO 62 are technically equivalent when the test specimen described in 6.2 is used.
claims.note: All procedural details are in ISO 62 text (6.3, m3 re-dry, Fick fit) and ASTM D570 note; swelling is only listed as an effect, with no strain method.

claims.claim: 0.2 % of 40 mm is 80 um; 3-sigma discrimination needs ~5 um; caliper (25.4 um) fails; fixed-pose photo (15 um/px) can meet it on paper; micrometer +/-1 um used in PA6.6 study.
claims.source_says: Travers: Accuracy ±.001". PA6.6 paper: digital outside micrometer (Mitutoyo Digimatic, ± 1 μm). calc_out.json strain: signal_um 80, sigma_dL_for_6.7pct_um 5.33.
claims.note: Arithmetic reproduces (80 um, 5.33 um, 3.77 um per reading) and both sources match; the camera 15 um/px is an unmeasured assumption, which the claim itself says is on paper only.

claims.claim: Form 4 prints 31-80 mm features to +/-0.2 % (floor +/-0.06 mm), same size as the swelling signal, so strain must be measured on the same coupon before and after.
claims.source_says: 31-80 mm features: +/-0.2% (lower limit: +/-0.06 mm)
claims.note: The tolerance text is on the Formlabs page; the inference to paired measurement is sound arithmetic (0.2 % of 40 mm = 80 um).

claims.claim: Flexible 80A V2 data sheet gives +8 % mass and +3 % volume in deionized water after 1 day (ASTM D471 slab), contradicting the cube-table under-1 % claim.
claims.source_says: Rectangular slabs, used for hardness, mass, and volume change, are evaluated immediately after wiping dry without a conditioning period. (Row values recovered from scrambled layout: 1 day -26 +8% +3%.)
claims.note: Slab method is verbatim and the +8 %/+3 % row is recovered by coordinates between the Deionized Water label and the 1-week row, but the PDF text is scrambled so the row assignment is inferred; 'only material with large swelling' is unchecked.

bm-wood-cellulose-hygromorphs.overall: Core numbers I could open (Holstov, Ruggeberg, Cheng, Khoshtinat, Gronquist 2019) match. Parts resting on unchecked sources (Gronquist 2018 4.5 m^-1, Dingler, Kruger, Tseo, own ETH recomputation) are unverified, and 'every modulus ratio' overstates Holstov's 'wide range'.

claims.claim: Max of Timoshenko coefficient is 1.5 for every modulus ratio, already shown numerically by Holstov 2015; novelty is the machine-checked proof.
claims.source_says: Plotting f(m,n) for a wide range of possible stiffness ratios shows that the maximum value of the function remains constant at 1.5 and in each case is achieved at single yet different thickness ratio (Figure 10).
claims.note: Holstov states 1.5 for a wide range of ratios from plots, not every ratio; the novelty statement is a judgment.

claims.claim: Benchmarks: wood 4.5-8.7 m^-1 in 24-48 h at 4.7-8 mm; printed cellulose 15.5 m^-1, 30 min, 170 cycles, 13 months on facade; cellulose acetate 51.1 m^-1 at 0.228 mm.
claims.source_says: Ruggeberg: curvatures up to 8.7*10-3 mm-1 ... after 24 hours. Cheng: average curvature of 0.0155 mm-1 at 80% RH; full transformation within 30 minutes; 170 cycles; 13 months. CA: kappa = 0.0511 mm-1, htot = 0.228 mm.
claims.note: All printed and acetate numbers and the 8.7 reproduce; the 4.5 m^-1 and 4.7-8 mm thickness (Gronquist 2018) were not checked.

claims.claim: Timoshenko error: +5 to +13% for stiff wood, +26% cellulose acetate, about 4x thin polymer films, 2.5-9x modulus ratio for printed wood-filament, correction factor 1.72 for bacterial cellulose.
claims.source_says: Ruggeberg: differences ... less than 5%; specific curvatures ... 11% and 13% higher than the calculated values. CA: analytical curvature of only 0.0645 mm-1 vs experimental 0.0511 mm-1 (26% over).
claims.note: Wood and acetate figures reproduce (the 5% is an upper bound, not +5); Dingler 4x, Kruger 2.5-9x and Tseo 1.72 were not verified.

claims.claim: Response time: 30 min (printed), 2 h 15 min (1 mm birch in humid air), 12.6-18.8 h (4.1 mm beech, 80% moisture change), 400-900+ h (15-45 mm timber); beating wood at 1 mm needs about 2 h for 80%.
claims.source_says: Holstov: 80% of the total curvature change ... achieved in approximately 2 hours 15 minutes. Gronquist 2019: approximately equilibrated after 400 hours ... 45 mm ... not visible after 900 hours.
claims.note: 30 min, 2 h 15 min and 400-900 h reproduce; 12.6-18.8 h is the agent's own calculation (not checked) and the 2 h target is an inference.

pp-broad-fish-biologists.overall: All three key claims are supported by the sources I fetched.

claims.claim: Broad Associate Members directory lists Leonard Zon with Boston Children's Hospital.
claims.source_says: Leonard Zon, Boston Children's Hospital
claims.note: Fetched directory page shows the row (via summarising fetch).

claims.claim: Broad news item describes Alex Schier as associate member at Broad and Harvard professor (2018).
claims.source_says: Alex Schier, associate member at Broad and professor at Harvard University
claims.note: Matches the news page.

claims.claim: Schier's 2025 cichlid paper gives his affiliation as Biozentrum, University of Basel; Broad status not confirmed.
claims.source_says: Schier AF ... affiliation: Biozentrum, University of Basel, Basel, Switzerland.
claims.note: Europe PMC record gives Schier's affiliation as Biozentrum Basel; the caveat is appropriately hedged.

pp-clients-and-contracts.overall: All four key claims hold against the sources. The university claim is partly supported only because it generalises from one system (UT) to all universities.

claims.claim: SBIR/STTR is reauthorized through 30 Sep 2031 and ceilings are Phase I $335,937 / Phase II $2,239,578.
claims.source_says: Crowell: "through September 30, 2031", signed April 13, 2026. sbir.gov: As of October 16, 2026, Phase I "up to $335,937", Phase II "up to $2,239,578" without SBA approval.
claims.note: Both pages give the dates and figures stated.

claims.claim: Small businesses may keep title to federally funded inventions; government gets a paid-up licence.
claims.source_says: A small business firm "may, within a reasonable time after disclosure" elect to retain title; the agency gets a "nonexclusive, nontransferrable, irrevocable, paid-up license" (202(a), (c)(4)).
claims.note: Matches 35 USC 202, with the election made within a reasonable time after disclosure.

claims.claim: University sponsored research agreements generally offer a sponsor an option to negotiate a licence, not an outright licence.
claims.source_says: "We may only offer an option to negotiate a license or a right of first refusal to negotiate a license."
claims.note: The source is one university system's checklist, so it says what UT System does, not what universities do in general.

claims.claim: Lean 4, mathlib4 and Apache-2.0 library code allow commercial redistribution with notice and licence-copy conditions and a patent-litigation termination clause.
claims.source_says: Section 2: "perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, no-charge, royalty-free, irrevocable copyright license" incl. sublicense and distribute; 4(a) "must give ... a copy of this License"; patent licences "shall terminate" on litigation.
claims.note: The mathlib4 LICENSE page was read and is Apache 2.0. The Lean 4 page fetch returned Apache 2.0 text. The Apache terms are as stated.

q1-critic.overall: All three key claims check out against the saved simulation output and the Europe PMC abstract. I did not re-run the script.

claims.claim: With zero interaction, noise alone makes 1.3% to 43.7% of enhancer pairs change order between promoters; observed reversal fractions must be compared with a noise-matched null.
